śīghramānaya bhadraṃ te pārvatīṃ śaṃkaraṃ suta ..
tayoḥ sa vacanaṃ śrutvā śīghraṃ gatvā śivālayam ..78..
4.45.d:
शीघ्रमानय भद्रं ते पार्वतीं शंकरं सुत ॥
तयोः स वचनं श्रुत्वा शीघ्रं गत्वा शिवालयम् ॥78॥
4.45.m:
"Quickly bring Pārvatī and Śaṅkara, O son; may all be well with you!"
Hearing their words, he went quickly to Śiva's abode,

4.45.s:
ājagāma samānīya pārvatīparameśvarau ..
pārvatyāgamanaṃ śrutvā bālāśca bālikāstathā ..79..
4.45.d:
आजगाम समानीय पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ॥
पार्वत्यागमनं श्रुत्वा बालाश्च बालिकास्तथा ॥79॥
4.45.m:
and returned, escorting Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord.
Hearing of Pārvatī's arrival, boys and girls,

4.45.s:
vṛddhā yuvatyo yā yāśca śailāśca dudruvurmudā ..
menā sutābhyāṃ vadhvā ca saha dudrāva sasmitā .. 4.45.80 ..
4.45.d:
वृद्धा युवत्यो या याश्च शैलाश्च दुद्रुवुर्मुदा ॥
मेना सुताभ्यां वध्वा च सह दुद्राव सस्मिता ॥ 4.45.80 ॥
4.45.m:
the elderly, young women, and whatever mountains [were present], rushed forward in joy.
Menā rushed out smiling, together with two sons and her daughter-in-law.

4.45.s:
himālayaśca mudito dudrāvānuvrajansutām ..
avaruhya rathāddevī mātaraṃ pitaraṃ gurum ..81..
4.45.d:
हिमालयश्च मुदितो दुद्रावानुव्रजन्सुताम् ॥
अवरुह्य रथाद्देवी मातरं पितरं गुरुम् ॥81॥
4.45.m:
Himālaya too, delighted, ran forward, following his daughter.
Descending from the chariot, the goddess [bowed] to her mother, father, and preceptor;

4.45.s:
praṇanāma pramuditā nimagnā''nandasāgare ..
pārvatīṃ ca samāśliṣya menakā harṣavihvalā .. 82 ..
4.45.d:
प्रणनाम प्रमुदिता निमग्ना'ऽनन्दसागरे ॥
पार्वतीं च समाश्लिष्य मेनका हर्षविह्वला ॥ 82 ॥
4.45.m:
overjoyed, immersed in an ocean of bliss, she bowed down.
Menakā, overcome with joy, embraced Pārvatī;

4.45.s:
himālayaśca mudito gatāḥ prāṇā ivāgatāḥ ..
sutāṃ nidhāya gehe sve ratnasiṃhāsanaṃ dadau ..83..
4.45.d:
हिमालयश्च मुदितो गताः प्राणा इवागताः ॥
सुतां निधाय गेहे स्वे रत्नसिंहासनं ददौ ॥83॥
4.45.m:
and Himālaya was overjoyed, as if his departed life-breath had returned.
Welcoming his daughter into his house, he gave her a jewel-throne,

4.45.s:
śūlabhṛte gaṇebhyaśca madhuparkādikaṃ mudā ..
tasthau śvaśuragehe ca sagaṇaścandraśekharaḥ ..84..
4.45.d:
शूलभृते गणेभ्यश्च मधुपर्कादिकं मुदा ॥
तस्थौ श्वशुरगेहे च सगणश्चन्द्रशेखरः ॥84॥
4.45.m:
and joyfully [offered] the honey-mixture and other honors to the trident-bearer and his attendants.
Candraśekhara stayed in his father-in-law's house together with his followers,

4.45.s:
nityaṃ ṣoḍaśopacāraiḥ pūjitaḥ saha bhāryayā ..
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ rādhe śaṃkarodvāhamaṅgalam ..
śokajaṃ harṣajanakaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 85 ..
.. iti śrībrahmavaivartte mahāpurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍe nārāyaṇanāradasaṃvāde śaṃkaravivāho nāma pañcacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 45 ..
4.45.d:
नित्यं षोडशोपचारैः पूजितः सह भार्यया ॥
इत्येवं कथितं राधे शंकरोद्वाहमङ्गलम् ॥
शोकजं हर्षजनकं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 85 ॥
॥ इति श्रीब्रह्मवैवर्त्ते महापुराणे श्रीकृष्णजन्मखण्डे नारायणनारदसंवादे शंकरविवाहो नाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 45 ॥
4.45.m:
worshiped daily with the sixteen offerings along with his wife.
"Thus has the auspicious wedding of Śaṅkara been narrated, O Rādhā,
which was born of sorrow and brings forth joy. What more do you wish to hear?"
Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Marriage of Śaṅkara,' in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa of the great Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, in the conversation between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada.

4.46.s:
rādhikovāca ..
suciraṃ ca mṛtaṃ kāmaṃ śaṃkareṇa ca jīvitam ..
ratiḥ punaḥ priyaṃ prāpya kiṃ cakāra mudā'nvitā .. 1 ..
4.46.d:
राधिकोवाच ॥
सुचिरं च मृतं कामं शंकरेण च जीवितम् ॥
रतिः पुनः प्रियं प्राप्य किं चकार मुदाऽन्विता ॥ 1 ॥

4.46.s:
strīṇāṃ svasvāmivicchedo maraṇādatiduṣkaraḥ ..
punaḥ saṃmelanaṃ bhartuḥ sukhaṃ paramadurlabham .. 2 ..
4.46.d:
स्त्रीणां स्वस्वामिविच्छेदो मरणादतिदुष्करः ॥
पुनः संमेलनं भर्तुः सुखं परमदुर्लभम् ॥ 2 ॥

4.46.s:
śivaḥ satīṃ tāṃ saṃprāpya saṅge maṅgalakarmaṇi..
ciraṃ pranaṣṭavirahaḥ kiṃ cakāra mudā'nvitaḥ .. 3 ..
4.46.d:
शिवः सतीं तां संप्राप्य सङ्गे मङ्गलकर्मणि॥
चिरं प्रनष्टविरहः किं चकार मुदाऽन्वितः ॥ 3 ॥

4.46.s:
kalatravirahaḥ puṃsāṃ sarvaśokātsuduṣkaraḥ ..
punaḥ saṃmīlanaṃ tasyāḥ prāṇadānādhikaṃ sukham .. 4 ..
4.46.d:
कलत्रविरहः पुंसां सर्वशोकात्सुदुष्करः ॥
पुनः संमीलनं तस्याः प्राणदानाधिकं सुखम् ॥ 4 ॥

4.46.s:
ratiḥ puṃso virahiṇī śivaḥ strīvirahī ciram ..
dvayordvayośca saṃprāptau kiṃ babhūva dvayoḥ sukham .. 5 ..
4.46.d:
रतिः पुंसो विरहिणी शिवः स्त्रीविरही चिरम् ॥
द्वयोर्द्वयोश्च संप्राप्तौ किं बभूव द्वयोः सुखम् ॥ 5 ॥

4.46.s:
tadevaṃ śrotumicchāmi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama ..
kṛpayā viduṣāṃ śreṣṭha savyāsaṃ kathaya prabho .. 6 ..
4.46.d:
तदेवं श्रोतुमिच्छामि परं कौतूहलं मम ॥
कृपया विदुषां श्रेष्ठ सव्यासं कथय प्रभो ॥ 6 ॥

4.46.s:
melanaṃ śaktiśivayo ratimanmathayostataḥ ..
śokāpahaṃ śrutavatāṃ sarvamaṅgalakāraṇam .. 7 ..
4.46.d:
मेलनं शक्तिशिवयो रतिमन्मथयोस्ततः ॥
शोकापहं श्रुतवतां सर्वमङ्गलकारणम् ॥ 7 ॥

4.46.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ityuktvā rādhikā devī sasmitā virarāma ha ..
kṛṣṇastadvacanaṃ śrutvā sasmitastāmuvāca ha .. 8 ..
4.46.d:
नारायण उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा राधिका देवी सस्मिता विरराम ह ॥
कृष्णस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सस्मितस्तामुवाच ह ॥ 8 ॥

4.46.s:
kṛṣṇa uvāca ..
mṛtaṃ kāmaṃ punaḥ prāpya kāmārtā kāmakāminī ..
svālayaṃ taṃ samānīya harodvāhagṛhādaho .. 9 ..
4.46.d:
कृष्ण उवाच ॥
मृतं कामं पुनः प्राप्य कामार्ता कामकामिनी ॥
स्वालयं तं समानीय हरोद्वाहगृहादहो ॥ 9 ॥

4.46.s:
bhartuḥ suveṣaṃ vividhaṃ svātmanaḥ svālibhirmudā ..
kārayāmāsa yatnena sā ratī ramaṇotsukā .. 4.46.10 ..
4.46.d:
भर्तुः सुवेषं विविधं स्वात्मनः स्वालिभिर्मुदा ॥
कारयामास यत्नेन सा रती रमणोत्सुका ॥ 4.46.10 ॥

4.46.s:
jñātvā kāmastu tadbhāvaṃ kāmaśāstravidhāyakaḥ ..
ratnayānaṃ samāruhya jagāma svālayādvanam .. 11 ..
4.46.d:
ज्ञात्वा कामस्तु तद्भावं कामशास्त्रविधायकः ॥
रत्नयानं समारुह्य जगाम स्वालयाद्वनम् ॥ 11 ॥

4.46.s:
śaileśaile'tiramye ca nadyāṃnadyāṃ nadenade ..
dvīpedvīpe sindhutaṭe puṣpodyāne manohare .. 12 ..
4.46.d:
शैलेशैलेऽतिरम्ये च नद्यांनद्यां नदेनदे ॥
द्वीपेद्वीपे सिन्धुतटे पुष्पोद्याने मनोहरे ॥ 12 ॥

4.46.s:
kāñcane bhūminikare vaṭamṛle'tinirjane ..
nadīpulinabhūmyāṃ ca puṣpite puṣpakānane .. 13 ..
4.46.d:
काञ्चने भूमिनिकरे वटमृलेऽतिनिर्जने ॥
नदीपुलिनभूम्यां च पुष्पिते पुष्पकानने ॥ 13 ॥

4.46.s:
bhramaradhvanisaṃyukte puṃskokilarutaśrute ..
sugandhivāyunā''kīrṇe dadhatī jalasīkaram .. 14 ..
4.46.d:
भ्रमरध्वनिसंयुक्ते पुंस्कोकिलरुतश्रुते ॥
सुगन्धिवायुना'ऽकीर्णे दधती जलसीकरम् ॥ 14 ॥

4.46.s:
citteṣu cetanānāṃ ca haraṇaṃ yoṣitāmaho ..
kalāmānaprakāreṇa śṛṅgāraṃ ca cakāra sā ..15..
4.46.d:
चित्तेषु चेतनानां च हरणं योषितामहो ॥
कलामानप्रकारेण शृङ्गारं च चकार सा ॥15॥

4.46.s:
pūrṇamabdaśataṃ divyaṃ sa reme vāmayā saha ..
divāniśaṃ na bubudhe saṃsaktaḥ satataṃ mudā .. 16 ..
4.46.d:
पूर्णमब्दशतं दिव्यं स रेमे वामया सह ॥
दिवानिशं न बुबुधे संसक्तः सततं मुदा ॥ 16 ॥

4.46.s:
tasthatustau ca tatraiva saṃsaktau satataṃ mudā ..
suratau ca na viratau ratiśāstraviśāradau .. 17 ..
4.46.d:
तस्थतुस्तौ च तत्रैव संसक्तौ सततं मुदा ॥
सुरतौ च न विरतौ रतिशास्त्रविशारदौ ॥ 17 ॥

4.46.s:
pativicchedasaṃtāpaṃ vijahau sā ratirmudā ..
prāpya ratnamapahṛtaṃ kaḥ kṣaṇaṃ tyaktumutsahet .. 18 ..
4.46.d:
पतिविच्छेदसंतापं विजहौ सा रतिर्मुदा ॥
प्राप्य रत्नमपहृतं कः क्षणं त्यक्तुमुत्सहेत् ॥ 18 ॥

4.46.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ ratisaṃtāpakāraṇam ..
śṛṅgāraṃ śaktiśivayoratulaṃ śṛṇu rādhike .. 19 ..
4.46.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं रतिसंतापकारणम् ॥
शृङ्गारं शक्तिशिवयोरतुलं शृणु राधिके ॥ 19 ॥

4.46.s:
śṛṇvatāṃ karṇapīyūṣaṃ paramāścaryamīpsitam ..
sarvasaṃtāpaharaṇaṃ sukhadaṃ puṇyadaṃ śubham .. 4.46.20 ..
4.46.d:
शृण्वतां कर्णपीयूषं परमाश्चर्यमीप्सितम् ॥
सर्वसंतापहरणं सुखदं पुण्यदं शुभम् ॥ 4.46.20 ॥

4.46.s:
vasañchvaśuragehe sa pārvatyā saha śaṃkaraḥ ..
tadanujñāṃ samādāya krīḍārthaṃ prayayau vanam .. 21 ..
4.46.d:
वसञ्छ्वशुरगेहे स पार्वत्या सह शंकरः ॥
तदनुज्ञां समादाय क्रीडार्थं प्रययौ वनम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.46.m: Śaṅkara took his leave and set out for the forest for sport.

4.46.s:
ratnasyandanamāruhya ratnasāraparicchadam..
ratnasāreṇa khacitaṃ racitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā .. 22 ..
4.46.d:
रत्नस्यन्दनमारुह्य रत्नसारपरिच्छदम्॥
रत्नसारेण खचितं रचितं विश्वकर्मणा ॥ 22 ॥

4.46.s:
śataśṛṅge suvasane malaye gandhamādane ..
nandane puṣpabhadre ca pāribhadre ca bhadrake..23..
4.46.d:
शतशृङ्गे सुवसने मलये गन्धमादने ॥
नन्दने पुष्पभद्रे च पारिभद्रे च भद्रके॥23॥

4.46.s:
pulinde ca kalinde ca puṃḍre piṃḍārakeṃ'dhake ..
vanevane'tiramye ca sāgarāṇāṃ taṭetaṭe .. 24 ..
4.46.d:
पुलिन्दे च कलिन्दे च पुंड्रे पिंडारकेंऽधके ॥
वनेवनेऽतिरम्ये च सागराणां तटेतटे ॥ 24 ॥

4.46.s:
nikaṭe'stagireḥ pārśvavaṭamūle manohare ..
cakāra karuṇāṃ yatra parityajya satī śivam .. 25 ..
4.46.d:
निकटेऽस्तगिरेः पार्श्ववटमूले मनोहरे ॥
चकार करुणां यत्र परित्यज्य सती शिवम् ॥ 25 ॥

4.46.s:
nānāsthāneṣu rahasi paśupakṣivivarjite ..
yathāmanorathaṃgāmī sa reme vāmayā saha .. 26 ..
4.46.d:
नानास्थानेषु रहसि पशुपक्षिविवर्जिते ॥
यथामनोरथंगामी स रेमे वामया सह ॥ 26 ॥

4.46.s:
yatrayatra śivaṃ nītvā babhrāma dharaṇītalam ..
tatsarvaṃ darśayāmāsa satīṃ śaṃbhurmudā'nvitaḥ .. 27 ..
4.46.d:
यत्रयत्र शिवं नीत्वा बभ्राम धरणीतलम् ॥
तत्सर्वं दर्शयामास सतीं शंभुर्मुदाऽन्वितः ॥ 27 ॥

4.46.s:
kṛtvā vihāraṃ suciraṃ na pūrṇaṃ mānasaṃ tayoḥ ..
mahāśṛṅgāramārebhe sahasrābdaṃ jagatpitā .. 28 ..
4.46.d:
कृत्वा विहारं सुचिरं न पूर्णं मानसं तयोः ॥
महाशृङ्गारमारेभे सहस्राब्दं जगत्पिता ॥ 28 ॥

4.46.s:
māyātīto'timāyeśo māyāsaktaḥ svamāyayā ..
kālaṃ na bubudhe yogī sukhena kālakārakaḥ .. 29 ..
4.46.d:
मायातीतोऽतिमायेशो मायासक्तः स्वमायया ॥
कालं न बुबुधे योगी सुखेन कालकारकः ॥ 29 ॥

4.46.s:
śaktiśaktimatostatra na babhūva pariśramaḥ ..
jahatoḥ sarvasaṃtāpamanyonyavirahodbhavam .. 4.46.30 ..
4.46.d:
शक्तिशक्तिमतोस्तत्र न बभूव परिश्रमः ॥
जहतोः सर्वसंतापमन्योन्यविरहोद्भवम् ॥ 4.46.30 ॥

4.46.s:
sukhasaṃsaktamanasoḥ pulakāñcitagātrayoḥ ..
kāmabāṇamūrcchitayoḥ puṣpaśayyāśayānayoḥ .. 31 ..
4.46.d:
सुखसंसक्तमनसोः पुलकाञ्चितगात्रयोः ॥
कामबाणमूर्च्छितयोः पुष्पशय्याशयानयोः ॥ 31 ॥

4.46.s:
nagnayoḥ sukhasaṃbhogādratiśāstravidhijñayoḥ ..
nakhadantaprahāraiśca kṣatavikṣatadehayoḥ .. 32 ..
4.46.d:
नग्नयोः सुखसंभोगाद्रतिशास्त्रविधिज्ञयोः ॥
नखदन्तप्रहारैश्च क्षतविक्षतदेहयोः ॥ 32 ॥

4.46.s:
candanāgurukastūrīsindūrabinduliptayoḥ..
nibaddhakeśakabarīślathayośchinnamālyayoḥ.. 33 ..
4.46.d:
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीसिन्दूरबिन्दुलिप्तयोः॥
निबद्धकेशकबरीश्लथयोश्छिन्नमाल्ययोः॥ 33 ॥

4.46.s:
vasanānāṃ nūpurāṇāṃ kaṅkaṇānāṃ ca sundari ..
valayānāṃ kuṇḍalānāṃ śabdaiḥ krīḍāṃ prakurvatoḥ .. 34 ..
4.46.d:
वसनानां नूपुराणां कङ्कणानां च सुन्दरि ॥
वलयानां कुण्डलानां शब्दैः क्रीडां प्रकुर्वतोः ॥ 34 ॥

4.46.s:
puṣpatalpaṃ dalitayorbāṣpotkarṣaṃ ca bibhratoḥ ..
tejasā samayoḥ śaśvatkrīḍayā kautukena ca .. 39 ..
4.46.d:
पुष्पतल्पं दलितयोर्बाष्पोत्कर्षं च बिभ्रतोः ॥
तेजसा समयोः शश्वत्क्रीडया कौतुकेन च ॥ 39 ॥

4.46.s:
bhāreṇa viśvaṃbharayorbhārākrāntā vasundharā ..
sā vidīrṇā cakampe ca saśailavanasāgarā..36..
4.46.d:
भारेण विश्वंभरयोर्भाराक्रान्ता वसुन्धरा ॥
सा विदीर्णा चकम्पे च सशैलवनसागरा॥36॥

4.46.s:
tayorbharabharākrāntadharāyāśca bhareṇa ca ..
bhārākrānto hi śeṣaśca tadbharārto'pi kacchapaḥ .. 37 ..
4.46.d:
तयोर्भरभराक्रान्तधरायाश्च भरेण च ॥
भाराक्रान्तो हि शेषश्च तद्भरार्तोऽपि कच्छपः ॥ 37 ॥

4.46.s:
kacchapasya bhareṇaiva sarvādhārā samīraṇāḥ ..
mahāviklavayuktāśca sarvaprāṇāśca stambhitāḥ .. 38 ..
4.46.d:
कच्छपस्य भरेणैव सर्वाधारा समीरणाः ॥
महाविक्लवयुक्ताश्च सर्वप्राणाश्च स्तम्भिताः ॥ 38 ॥

4.46.s:
stambhiteṣu samīreṣu trilokā bhayavihvalāḥ ..
brahmādayaḥ surāḥ sarve vaikuṇṭhaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ .. 39 ..
4.46.d:
स्तम्भितेषु समीरेषु त्रिलोका भयविह्वलाः ॥
ब्रह्मादयः सुराः सर्वे वैकुण्ठं शरणं ययुः ॥ 39 ॥

4.46.s:
sarvaṃ nivedanaṃ cakrurnārāyaṇapadāmbuje ..
nārāyaṇaśca bhagavānuvāca kamalodbhavam .. 4.46.40 ..
4.46.d:
सर्वं निवेदनं चक्रुर्नारायणपदाम्बुजे ॥
नारायणश्च भगवानुवाच कमलोद्भवम् ॥ 4.46.40 ॥

4.46.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
śṛṅgārabhaṅgasamayo bhavitā nādhunā vidhe ..
kālaprayuktaṃ kāryaṃ ca siddhaṃ tatsamayocitam .. 41 ..
4.46.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
शृङ्गारभङ्गसमयो भविता नाधुना विधे ॥
कालप्रयुक्तं कार्यं च सिद्धं तत्समयोचितम् ॥ 41 ॥

4.46.s:
pūrṇe varṣasahasre ca svecchayā viramiṣyati ..
śaṃbhoḥ saṃyogamiṣṭaṃ ca ko bhedaṃ kartumīśvaraḥ ..42..
4.46.d:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे च स्वेच्छया विरमिष्यति ॥
शंभोः संयोगमिष्टं च को भेदं कर्तुमीश्वरः ॥42॥

4.46.s:
strīpuṃso rativicchedamupāyena karoti yaḥ ..
tasya strīpuṃsayorbhedo bhavejjanmanijanmani .. 43 ..
4.46.d:
स्त्रीपुंसो रतिविच्छेदमुपायेन करोति यः ॥
तस्य स्त्रीपुंसयोर्भेदो भवेज्जन्मनिजन्मनि ॥ 43 ॥

4.46.s:
yātyante kālasūtre ca varṣalakṣaṃ sa pātakī ..
bhraṣṭajñāno naṣṭakīrtiralakṣmīko bhavediha..44..
4.46.d:
यात्यन्ते कालसूत्रे च वर्षलक्षं स पातकी ॥
भ्रष्टज्ञानो नष्टकीर्तिरलक्ष्मीको भवेदिह॥44॥

4.46.s:
rambhāyuktaṃ śakramimaṃ cakāra virataṃ ratau ..
mahāmunīndro durvāsāstatstrībhedo babhūva ha .. 45 ..
4.46.d:
रम्भायुक्तं शक्रमिमं चकार विरतं रतौ ॥
महामुनीन्द्रो दुर्वासास्तत्स्त्रीभेदो बभूव ह ॥ 45 ॥

4.46.s:
punaranyāṃ sa saṃprāpya niṣevya śūlapāṇinam ..
divyavarṣasahasraṃ ca vijahau virahajvaram .. 46 ..
4.46.d:
पुनरन्यां स संप्राप्य निषेव्य शूलपाणिनम् ॥
दिव्यवर्षसहस्रं च विजहौ विरहज्वरम् ॥ 46 ॥

4.46.s:
rohiṇīsahitaṃ candraṃ cakāra virataṃ ratau ..
maharṣirgautamastasya strīvicchedo babhūva ha .. 47 ..
4.46.d:
रोहिणीसहितं चन्द्रं चकार विरतं रतौ ॥
महर्षिर्गौतमस्तस्य स्त्रीविच्छेदो बभूव ह ॥ 47 ॥

4.46.s:
punaḥ śivaṃ samārādhya prāpyāhalyāṃ ca puṣkare ..
divyavarṣasahasraṃ ca vijahau virahajvaram .. 48 ..
4.46.d:
पुनः शिवं समाराध्य प्राप्याहल्यां च पुष्करे ॥
दिव्यवर्षसहस्रं च विजहौ विरहज्वरम् ॥ 48 ॥
4.46.m: Having worshipped Śiva again and regained Ahalyā at Puṣkara,

4.46.s:
muniḥ svabhāryāsaṃsakte divase nirjane vane ..
brahmāṇḍakasutaṃ nītvā cakāra virataṃ ruṣā .. 49 ..
4.46.d:
मुनिः स्वभार्यासंसक्ते दिवसे निर्जने वने ॥
ब्रह्माण्डकसुतं नीत्वा चकार विरतं रुषा ॥ 49 ॥
4.46.m:
A sage, finding [a couple] united in a solitary forest by day,
took away Brahmāṇḍaka's son and in anger made him desist from his wife. // 49

4.46.s:
babhūva putravicchedastasya kalpāntare punaḥ ..
śivaṃ niṣevya saṃprāpya putraṃ tatyāja viklavam .. 4.46.50 ..
4.46.d:
बभूव पुत्रविच्छेदस्तस्य कल्पान्तरे पुनः ॥
शिवं निषेव्य संप्राप्य पुत्रं तत्याज विक्लवम् ॥ 4.46.50 ॥
4.46.m:
In another kalpa, separation from his son befell him;
serving Śiva and regaining his son, he cast away his distress. // 50

4.46.s:
hariścandro hālikaṃ ca vṛṣalyā saha saṃyutam ..
vārayāmāsa niśceṣṭaṃ nirjane tatphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 51 ..
4.46.d:
हरिश्चन्द्रो हालिकं च वृषल्या सह संयुतम् ॥
वारयामास निश्चेष्टं निर्जने तत्फलं शृणु ॥ 51 ॥
4.46.m:
Hariścandra stopped a ploughman who was united with a low-caste woman
and motionless in a solitary place; hear the fruit of that: // 51

4.46.s:
bhraṣṭaḥ śrīrājyavittebhyastaṃ cakārāvalīlayā ..
viśvāmitro maharṣiśca tāḍayāmāsa taṃ purā .... 52 ..
4.46.d:
भ्रष्टः श्रीराज्यवित्तेभ्यस्तं चकारावलीलया ॥
विश्वामित्रो महर्षिश्च ताडयामास तं पुरा ॥॥ 52 ॥
4.46.m:
The great sage Viśvāmitra effortlessly stripped him
of prosperity, kingdom, and wealth, and tormented him in the past. // 52

4.46.s:
tataḥ śivaṃ samārādhya dātāraṃ sarvasaṃpadām ..
sadyo jagāma vaikuṇṭhaṃ sagaṇo mama mandiram .. 53 ..
4.46.d:
ततः शिवं समाराध्य दातारं सर्वसंपदाम् ॥
सद्यो जगाम वैकुण्ठं सगणो मम मन्दिरम् ॥ 53 ॥
4.46.m:
Then, having worshipped Śiva, the giver of all fortunes,
he promptly went with his retinue to Vaikuṇṭha, my abode. // 53

4.46.s:
ājāmilaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ vṛṣalyā saha saṃyutam ..
na bhiyā vārayāmāsuḥ surāstaṃ cāpi kecana .. 54 ..
4.46.d:
आजामिलं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वृषल्या सह संयुतम् ॥
न भिया वारयामासुः सुरास्तं चापि केचन ॥ 54 ॥
4.46.m:
Ajāmila, the best of the twice-born, was united with a low-caste woman,
yet none of the gods stopped him out of fear. // 54

4.46.s:
niṣpanne karmabhoge ca sa madbhakto mumoca ha ..
mannāmasmṛtimātreṇa cājagāma mamālayam .. 55 ..
4.46.d:
निष्पन्ने कर्मभोगे च स मद्भक्तो मुमोच ह ॥
मन्नामस्मृतिमात्रेण चाजगाम ममालयम् ॥ 55 ॥
4.46.m:
When the experience of his karma was completed, that devotee of mine attained release;
merely by remembering my name, he came to my abode. // 55

4.46.s:
sarvaṃ niṣekasādhyaṃ ca niṣeko balavānvidhe ..
niṣekaphaladātā'haṃ niṣekaḥ kena vāryate .. 56 ..
4.46.d:
सर्वं निषेकसाध्यं च निषेको बलवान्विधे ॥
निषेकफलदाताऽहं निषेकः केन वार्यते ॥ 56 ॥
4.46.m:
Everything is accomplished by destiny, and destiny is powerful, O Brahmā;
I am the giver of the fruit of destiny; by whom can destiny be averted? // 56

4.46.s:
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca śaṃbhoḥ saṃbhogakarmakṛt ..
niṣekaphaladātustu niṣekaphalasaṃcayam .. 57 ..
4.46.d:
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं च शंभोः संभोगकर्मकृत् ॥
निषेकफलदातुस्तु निषेकफलसंचयम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.46.m:
For a thousand celestial years, Śambhu acts in the deed of enjoyment,
[fulfilling] the accumulation of fruits of destiny ordained by the giver of destiny's fruit. // 57

4.46.s:
pūrṇe varṣasahasre ca gatvā tatra maheśvaraḥ ..
yena vīryaṃ patedbhūmau tatkariṣyati niścitam ..98 ..
4.46.d:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे च गत्वा तत्र महेश्वरः ॥
येन वीर्यं पतेद्भूमौ तत्करिष्यति निश्चितम् ॥98 ॥
4.46.m:
When the thousand years are complete, Maheśvara, going there,
will certainly do that by which the semen falls upon the earth. // 58

4.46.s:
tatra vīrye ca bhavitā skandako bhaktatārakaḥ ..
sadā bhadrasvarūpo'haṃ bhayaṃ kiṃ vo mayi sthite .. 59 ..
4.46.d:
तत्र वीर्ये च भविता स्कन्दको भक्ततारकः ॥
सदा भद्रस्वरूपोऽहं भयं किं वो मयि स्थिते ॥ 59 ॥
4.46.m:
And from that semen, Skanda, the saviour of devotees, will be born.
I am ever the embodiment of auspiciousness; what fear is there for you while I remain? // 59

4.46.s:
adhunā tvaṃ gṛhaṃ gaccha bhagavānsvagaṇaiḥ saha ..
karotu śaṃbhuḥ saṃbhogaṃ pārvatyā saha nirjane.... 4.46.60 ..
4.46.d:
अधुना त्वं गृहं गच्छ भगवान्स्वगणैः सह ॥
करोतु शंभुः संभोगं पार्वत्या सह निर्जने॥॥ 4.46.60 ॥
4.46.m:
Now, O lord, go home together with your attendants;
let Śambhu enjoy intercourse with Pārvatī in secret." // 60

4.46.s:
ityuktvā kamalākāntaḥ śīghraṃ svāntaḥpuraṃ yayau ..
svālayaṃ prayayurdevāḥ śivaḥ svastho ratau rataḥ .. 61 ..
4.46.d:
इत्युक्त्वा कमलाकान्तः शीघ्रं स्वान्तःपुरं ययौ ॥
स्वालयं प्रययुर्देवाः शिवः स्वस्थो रतौ रतः ॥ 61 ॥
4.46.m:
Having spoken thus, the beloved of Kamalā [Viṣṇu] quickly went to his inner quarters;
the gods departed to their own abodes, and Śiva, undisturbed, remained devoted to pleasure. // 61

4.46.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ityuktvā rādhikāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ sakaṭākṣāṃ ca sasmitām ..
jagāma candanavanaṃ nirjane ca tayā saha .. 62 ..
4.46.d:
नारायण उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा राधिकां कृष्णः सकटाक्षां च सस्मिताम् ॥
जगाम चन्दनवनं निर्जने च तया सह ॥ 62 ॥
4.46.m:
Having spoken thus to Rādhikā, who looked with side-glances and a smile,
Kṛṣṇa went with her into the secluded sandalwood forest, // 62

4.46.s:
atīva nirjanaṃ ramyaṃ vāyunā surabhīkṛtam ..
puṣpodyānaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ tatra krīḍāṃ cakāra ha .. 63 ..
4.46.d:
अतीव निर्जनं रम्यं वायुना सुरभीकृतम् ॥
पुष्पोद्यानैः समाकीर्णं तत्र क्रीडां चकार ह ॥ 63 ॥
4.46.m:
which was very secluded, charming, perfumed by the wind,
and filled with flower gardens; and there he engaged in sport, // 63

4.46.s:
puṣpatalpasamākīrṇe parapuṣṭarutaśrute ..
bhramaravadhvani saṃyukte kāminīnāṃ manohare .. 64 ..
4.46.d:
पुष्पतल्पसमाकीर्णे परपुष्टरुतश्रुते ॥
भ्रमरवध्वनि संयुक्ते कामिनीनां मनोहरे ॥ 64 ॥
4.46.m:
upon a bed strewn with flowers, where the song of cuckoos was heard,
filled with the humming of bees, captivating to passionate women. // 64

4.46.s:
kṛṣṇasaṃbhogamātreṇa sukhasaṃmūrcchitā ca sā ..
atīva mūrcchitaḥ kṛṣṇo rādhāṅgasparśamātrataḥ .... 65 ..
4.46.d:
कृष्णसंभोगमात्रेण सुखसंमूर्च्छिता च सा ॥
अतीव मूर्च्छितः कृष्णो राधाङ्गस्पर्शमात्रतः ॥॥ 65 ॥
4.46.m:
Merely through the enjoyment of Kṛṣṇa, she fainted from pleasure,
and Kṛṣṇa too was deeply overwhelmed merely by the touch of Rādhā's body. // 65

4.46.s:
tasthatustatra saṃyuktau rādhārāseśvarau mune ..
atīvaratiniśceṣṭau kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 66 ..
4.46.d:
तस्थतुस्तत्र संयुक्तौ राधारासेश्वरौ मुने ॥
अतीवरतिनिश्चेष्टौ किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 66 ॥
4.46.m:
There they remained united, Rādhā and the Lord of the Rāsa dance, O sage,
rendered motionless by intense pleasure. What more do you wish to hear? // 66

4.46.s:
ityevaṃ maṅgalaṃ karma yaḥ śṛṇoti samāhitaḥ ..
kadācidbandhuvicchedo na bhavettasya nārada ..67..
4.46.d:
इत्येवं मङ्गलं कर्म यः शृणोति समाहितः ॥
कदाचिद्बन्धुविच्छेदो न भवेत्तस्य नारद ॥67॥
4.46.m:
Whoever listens with concentration to this auspicious act
shall never suffer separation from kin, O Nārada. // 67

4.46.s:
mahāśokārṇave magno bhede putrakalatrayoḥ..
madbhṛtyānāṃ ca bandhūnāṃ māsaṃ śrutvā labheddhruvam .. 68 ..
4.46.d:
महाशोकार्णवे मग्नो भेदे पुत्रकलत्रयोः॥
मद्भृत्यानां च बन्धूनां मासं श्रुत्वा लभेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.46.m:
Even if sunk in a great ocean of sorrow through separation from son and wife,
or from my servants and relatives, by listening for a month one will certainly recover them. // 68

4.46.s:
sūta uvāca ..
ityuktvā dharmaputraśca virarāma mahāmuniḥ ..
punaḥ saṃpraṣṭumārebhe devarṣiḥ kautukānvitaḥ .. 69 ..
4.46.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा धर्मपुत्रश्च विरराम महामुनिः ॥
पुनः संप्रष्टुमारेभे देवर्षिः कौतुकान्वितः ॥ 69 ॥
4.46.m:
Having spoken thus, the great sage, the son of Dharma, fell silent;
and the divine sage, filled with curiosity, began to question him again. // 69

4.47.s:
nārada uvāca ..
atha krīḍāṃtare rādhā kiṃ papraccha hariṃ vibhum ..
kāṃ kathāṃ kathayāmāsa kathyatāṃ karuṇānidhe .. 1 ..
4.47.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
अथ क्रीडांतरे राधा किं पप्रच्छ हरिं विभुम् ॥
कां कथां कथयामास कथ्यतां करुणानिधे ॥ 1 ॥

4.47.s:
.. śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca .. ..
utthāya sukhasaṃbhogādrādhāṃ kṛtvā puro hariḥ ..
uvāsa malayadroṇīṃ vaṭamūle manohare .. 2 ..
4.47.d:
॥ श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥ ॥
उत्थाय सुखसंभोगाद्राधां कृत्वा पुरो हरिः ॥
उवास मलयद्रोणीं वटमूले मनोहरे ॥ 2 ॥

4.47.s:
rādhā taṃ paripapraccha sasmitaṃ sumanoharam ..
darpabhaṅgaḥ vajrabhṛto nigūḍhaṃ śrutisundaram .. 3 ..
4.47.d:
राधा तं परिपप्रच्छ सस्मितं सुमनोहरम् ॥
दर्पभङ्गः वज्रभृतो निगूढं श्रुतिसुन्दरम् ॥ 3 ॥

4.47.s:
.. śrīrādhikovāca ..
śrutaṃ yaśaḥ śūlabhṛto darpabhaṅgaśca daivataḥ ..
pārvatyā darpabhaṅgaśca vivāhaśca tayoraho ..4..
4.47.d:
॥ श्रीराधिकोवाच ॥
श्रुतं यशः शूलभृतो दर्पभङ्गश्च दैवतः ॥
पार्वत्या दर्पभङ्गश्च विवाहश्च तयोरहो ॥4॥

4.47.s:
adhunā śrotumicchāmi darpabhaṅgaṃ harerhare ..
śeṣāṇāṃ ca krameṇaiva vada vyasya jagadguro .. 5 ..
4.47.d:
अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि दर्पभङ्गं हरेर्हरे ॥
शेषाणां च क्रमेणैव वद व्यस्य जगद्गुरो ॥ 5 ॥

4.47.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
darpabhaṃgaṃ surapatestriṣu lokeṣu viśrutam ..
karṇapīyūṣamatulaṃ sundaraṃ śṛṇu sundari .. 6 ..
4.47.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
दर्पभंगं सुरपतेस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥
कर्णपीयूषमतुलं सुन्दरं शृणु सुन्दरि ॥ 6 ॥

4.47.s:
purā śatamakho darpātkṛtvā śatamakhānmudā ..
babhūva sarvadevānāmadhyakṣaḥ saṃpadā yutaḥ .. 7 ..
4.47.d:
पुरा शतमखो दर्पात्कृत्वा शतमखान्मुदा ॥
बभूव सर्वदेवानामध्यक्षः संपदा युतः ॥ 7 ॥

4.47.s:
dinedine tadaiśvaryaṃ varddhate tapasāṃ phalāt ..
dīkṣāṃ taṃ kārayāmāsa siddhamannaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ ..8..
4.47.d:
दिनेदिने तदैश्वर्यं वर्द्धते तपसां फलात् ॥
दीक्षां तं कारयामास सिद्धमन्नं बृहस्पतिः ॥8॥

4.47.s:
sa jajāpa mahāmantraṃ puṣkare śatavatsaram ..
babhūva mantrasiddhaśca paripūrṇamanorathaḥ .. 9 ..
4.47.d:
स जजाप महामन्त्रं पुष्करे शतवत्सरम् ॥
बभूव मन्त्रसिद्धश्च परिपूर्णमनोरथः ॥ 9 ॥

4.47.s:
brahmasvarūpāṃ prakṛtiṃ saṃpanmūḍho na manyate ..
sā taṃ śaśāpa svaguroḥ śāpaṃ lebhe'tikopataḥ....4.47.10..
4.47.d:
ब्रह्मस्वरूपां प्रकृतिं संपन्मूढो न मन्यते ॥
सा तं शशाप स्वगुरोः शापं लेभेऽतिकोपतः॥॥4.47.10॥

4.47.s:
ekadā prakṛteḥ śāpāddhatabuddhiḥ svasaṃsadi..
guruṃ dṛṣṭvā samutthāya na nanāma mudā'nvitaḥ .. 11 ..
4.47.d:
एकदा प्रकृतेः शापाद्धतबुद्धिः स्वसंसदि॥
गुरुं दृष्ट्वा समुत्थाय न ननाम मुदाऽन्वितः ॥ 11 ॥

4.47.s:
bṛhaspatistataḥ kopānnovāsa gṛhamāyayau ..
na tasthau tārakābhyāśe tapase kānanaṃ yayau .. 12 ..
4.47.d:
बृहस्पतिस्ततः कोपान्नोवास गृहमाययौ ॥
न तस्थौ तारकाभ्याशे तपसे काननं ययौ ॥ 12 ॥

4.47.s:
uvāca manasā dīno yātu saṃpaddhareriti ..
atha śakro matiṃ prāpya kva gato'to madīśvaraḥ ..13..
4.47.d:
उवाच मनसा दीनो यातु संपद्धरेरिति ॥
अथ शक्रो मतिं प्राप्य क्व गतोऽतो मदीश्वरः ॥13॥

4.47.s:
ityuktvā vegataḥ pīṭhājjagāma tārakāntikam..
praṇamya mātaraṃ bhaktyā nataskandhaḥ puṭāñjaliḥ .... 14 ..
4.47.d:
इत्युक्त्वा वेगतः पीठाज्जगाम तारकान्तिकम्॥
प्रणम्य मातरं भक्त्या नतस्कन्धः पुटाञ्जलिः ॥॥ 14 ॥

4.47.s:
sarvaṃ nivedanaṃ kṛtvā rurodoccairmuhurmuhuḥ ..
putrasya rodanaṃ dṛṣṭvā ruroda tārakā bhṛśam .. 15 ..
4.47.d:
सर्वं निवेदनं कृत्वा रुरोदोच्चैर्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
पुत्रस्य रोदनं दृष्ट्वा रुरोद तारका भृशम् ॥ 15 ॥

4.47.s:
vatsa gaccha gṛhaṃ naiva guruṃ drakṣyasi sāmpratam ..
durdinānte guruṃ prāpya punarlakṣmīmavāpsyasi .. 16..
4.47.d:
वत्स गच्छ गृहं नैव गुरुं द्रक्ष्यसि साम्प्रतम् ॥
दुर्दिनान्ते गुरुं प्राप्य पुनर्लक्ष्मीमवाप्स्यसि ॥ 16॥

4.47.s:
adhunā karmaṇāṃ bhogaṃ bhuṅkṣva mūḍha durāśaya..
durdine svagurau doṣaḥ sudine paritoṣaṇam ..17..
4.47.d:
अधुना कर्मणां भोगं भुङ्क्ष्व मूढ दुराशय॥
दुर्दिने स्वगुरौ दोषः सुदिने परितोषणम् ॥17॥

4.47.s:
sudinaṃ durdinaṃ śakra kāraṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ ..
ityuktvā tārakā devī virarāma pativratā .. 18 ..
4.47.d:
सुदिनं दुर्दिनं शक्र कारणं सुखदुःखयोः ॥
इत्युक्त्वा तारका देवी विरराम पतिव्रता ॥ 18 ॥

4.47.s:
jagāma śakraḥ snānārthaṃ svarṇadīṃ sumanoharām ..
dadarśa tatra rucirāṃ mārjantīṃ ca nitambinīm ..19..
4.47.d:
जगाम शक्रः स्नानार्थं स्वर्णदीं सुमनोहराम् ॥
ददर्श तत्र रुचिरां मार्जन्तीं च नितम्बिनीम् ॥19॥

4.47.s:
sasmitāṃ sakaṭākṣāṃ tāmahalyāṃ gautamapriyām ..
dṛṣṭvā ca vipulaśroṇīṃ stanayugmaṃ manoharam ..4.47.20..
4.47.d:
सस्मितां सकटाक्षां तामहल्यां गौतमप्रियाम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा च विपुलश्रोणीं स्तनयुग्मं मनोहरम् ॥4.47.20॥

4.47.s:
sa tasyāḥ śakraḥ saṃpaśyanmumoha kāmamohitaḥ ..
punaḥ sa cetanāṃ prāpya vihāya snānamīśvari .. 21 ..
4.47.d:
स तस्याः शक्रः संपश्यन्मुमोह काममोहितः ॥
पुनः स चेतनां प्राप्य विहाय स्नानमीश्वरि ॥ 21 ॥

4.47.s:
mūrtiṃ vidhāya tadbhartustatsamīpaṃ jagāma ha ..
gatvā tu snigdhavastrāṃ tāṃ samākṛṣya smarāturaḥ .. 22..
4.47.d:
मूर्तिं विधाय तद्भर्तुस्तत्समीपं जगाम ह ॥
गत्वा तु स्निग्धवस्त्रां तां समाकृष्य स्मरातुरः ॥ 22॥

4.47.s:
cakāra vividhaṃ tatra śṛṃgāraṃ sumanoharam ..
mūrcchāṃ saṃprāpa kāmena tandrāṃ ca munikāminī ..23..
4.47.d:
चकार विविधं तत्र शृंगारं सुमनोहरम् ॥
मूर्च्छां संप्राप कामेन तन्द्रां च मुनिकामिनी ॥23॥

4.47.s:
niśceṣṭā sukhasaṃbhogānniśceṣṭastridaśādhipaḥ ..
etasminnantare taptvā samāgatya munīśvaraḥ .. 24 ..
4.47.d:
निश्चेष्टा सुखसंभोगान्निश्चेष्टस्त्रिदशाधिपः ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तप्त्वा समागत्य मुनीश्वरः ॥ 24 ॥

4.47.s:
dadarśa gehe mithunaṃ maithune ca ratipriye ..
dṛṣṭvā cukopa sa munirjvalanniva hutāśanaḥ .. 25 ..
4.47.d:
ददर्श गेहे मिथुनं मैथुने च रतिप्रिये ॥
दृष्ट्वा चुकोप स मुनिर्ज्वलन्निव हुताशनः ॥ 25 ॥

4.47.s:
vijñānenātiroṣeṇa babhañja suratikṣaṇam ..
śakraḥ sa cetanāṃ prāpya dṛṣṭvā ca munipuṃgavam .. 26 ..
4.47.d:
विज्ञानेनातिरोषेण बभञ्ज सुरतिक्षणम् ॥
शक्रः स चेतनां प्राप्य दृष्ट्वा च मुनिपुंगवम् ॥ 26 ॥

4.47.s:
kālasvarūpaṃ trāsena dadhāra caraṇāmbujam ..
koparaktāsyanayano devaṃ pādānataṃ bhiyā ..
uvāca nītivacanaṃ gautamaḥ śaraṇāgatam .. 27 ..
4.47.d:
कालस्वरूपं त्रासेन दधार चरणाम्बुजम् ॥
कोपरक्तास्यनयनो देवं पादानतं भिया ॥
उवाच नीतिवचनं गौतमः शरणागतम् ॥ 27 ॥

4.47.s:
gautama uvāca ..
dhik tvāmindra suraśreṣṭha kaśyapātmaja paṇḍita .. 28 ..
4.47.d:
गौतम उवाच ॥
धिक् त्वामिन्द्र सुरश्रेष्ठ कश्यपात्मज पण्डित ॥ 28 ॥

4.47.s:
prapautra jagatāṃ sraṣṭurbuddhiste kathamīdṛśī ..
mātāmahaḥ svayaṃ dakṣo'ditirmātā pativratā .. 29 ..
4.47.d:
प्रपौत्र जगतां स्रष्टुर्बुद्धिस्ते कथमीदृशी ॥
मातामहः स्वयं दक्षोऽदितिर्माता पतिव्रता ॥ 29 ॥

4.47.s:
karmasādhyaḥ svabhāvaśca kuladharmaṃ prabādhate ..
vedaṃ vijñāya jñānī tvaṃ yonilubdho'si karmaṇā .. 4.47.30 ..
4.47.d:
कर्मसाध्यः स्वभावश्च कुलधर्मं प्रबाधते ॥
वेदं विज्ञाय ज्ञानी त्वं योनिलुब्धोऽसि कर्मणा ॥ 4.47.30 ॥

4.47.s:
yonīnāṃ ca sahasraṃ ca tava gātre bhavatviha ..
pūrṇavarṣaṃ ca satataṃ yonigandhaṃ tvamāpnuhi .. 31 ..
4.47.d:
योनीनां च सहस्रं च तव गात्रे भवत्विह ॥
पूर्णवर्षं च सततं योनिगन्धं त्वमाप्नुहि ॥ 31 ॥

4.47.s:
tataḥ sūryaṃ samārādhya yoniścakṣurbhaviṣyati ..
mama prāṇeśvarī duṣṭā yena mūḍha tvayā kṛtā .. 32 ..
4.47.d:
ततः सूर्यं समाराध्य योनिश्चक्षुर्भविष्यति ॥
मम प्राणेश्वरी दुष्टा येन मूढ त्वया कृता ॥ 32 ॥

4.47.s:
macchāpena guroḥ kopādbhraṣṭaśrīrbhava sāmpratam ..
gurorapekṣayā mūḍha prāṇā nāpahṛtāstava .. 33 ..
4.47.d:
मच्छापेन गुरोः कोपाद्भ्रष्टश्रीर्भव साम्प्रतम् ॥
गुरोरपेक्षया मूढ प्राणा नापहृतास्तव ॥ 33 ॥

4.47.s:
tejasvino'tibandhorme baṃdhubhedabhiyā sura ..
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha devendra gaccha vatsa svamandiram .. 34..
4.47.d:
तेजस्विनोऽतिबन्धोर्मे बंधुभेदभिया सुर ॥
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ देवेन्द्र गच्छ वत्स स्वमन्दिरम् ॥ 34॥

4.47.s:
śubhāśubhaṃ ca yatkiṃcitsarvaṃ karmodbhavaṃ bhavet ..
mahāmunīndravacanādgataḥ śakraśca puṣkaram ...35..
4.47.d:
शुभाशुभं च यत्किंचित्सर्वं कर्मोद्भवं भवेत् ॥
महामुनीन्द्रवचनाद्गतः शक्रश्च पुष्करम् ॥.35॥

4.47.s:
cakārārādhanaṃ bhaktyā naiṣkṛtyaṃ ca cakāra ha ..
pādānatāmahalyāṃ tāmuvāca munipuṃgavaḥ .. 36 ..
4.47.d:
चकाराराधनं भक्त्या नैष्कृत्यं च चकार ह ॥
पादानतामहल्यां तामुवाच मुनिपुंगवः ॥ 36 ॥
4.47.m: Then to Ahalyā, who was bowed at his feet, the eminent sage said:

4.47.s:
vanaṃ gatvā ciraṃ tiṣṭha vidhāya mūrtimaśmanaḥ .. ..
akāmāṃ cakame śakraḥ sarvaṃ jānāmyahaṃ priye .. 37 ..
4.47.d:
वनं गत्वा चिरं तिष्ठ विधाय मूर्तिमश्मनः ॥ ॥
अकामां चकमे शक्रः सर्वं जानाम्यहं प्रिये ॥ 37 ॥
4.47.m:
"Go to the forest and remain there for a long time, assuming a form of stone.
Indra lusted after you when you were unwilling; I know everything, dear one.

4.47.s:
tathā ca parabhogyā me na bhogyā vrajādhame ..
paravīryaṃ yadudare kāmato'kāmato'pi vā ..38..
4.47.d:
तथा च परभोग्या मे न भोग्या व्रजाधमे ॥
परवीर्यं यदुदरे कामतोऽकामतोऽपि वा ॥38॥
4.47.m:
Even so, having been enjoyed by another, you are not to be enjoyed by me; depart, wretched woman!
When the semen of another enters the womb, whether willingly or unwillingly,

4.47.s:
ahalye yāti daivena tadupāyaṃ niśāmaya ..
akāmato na ca duṣṭā sā prāyaścittena śuddhyati ..39..
4.47.d:
अहल्ये याति दैवेन तदुपायं निशामय ॥
अकामतो न च दुष्टा सा प्रायश्चित्तेन शुद्ध्यति ॥39॥
4.47.m:
O Ahalyā, by fate's decree, hear the remedy for that:
she who is without desire is not corrupted; she is purified by expiation.

4.47.s:
kāmabhogena tyājyā sā karmabhogena śuddhyati ..
pitṛpāke daivapāke pūjāyāṃ nādhikāriṇī ..4.47.40 ..
4.47.d:
कामभोगेन त्याज्या सा कर्मभोगेन शुद्ध्यति ॥
पितृपाके दैवपाके पूजायां नाधिकारिणी ॥4.47.40 ॥
4.47.m:
Through willing enjoyment she must be abandoned, but through the experience of karmic retribution she becomes pure.
She has no entitlement in cooking for the ancestors, cooking for the gods, or in worship;

4.47.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi kālasūtraṃ prayāti sā..
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi kṣayaṃ kṛtvā svakarmaṇaḥ .. 41 ..
4.47.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि कालसूत्रं प्रयाति सा॥
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि क्षयं कृत्वा स्वकर्मणः ॥ 41 ॥
4.47.m:
she goes to the Kālasūtra [hell] for sixty thousand years.
Having exhausted her actions for sixty thousand years [she is purified]."

4.47.s:
svāmino vacanātsā tu praṇamya svāminaṃ bhiyā ..
nātha nātheti kurvantī rudantī vanamāpa sā .. 42 ..
4.47.d:
स्वामिनो वचनात्सा तु प्रणम्य स्वामिनं भिया ॥
नाथ नाथेति कुर्वन्ती रुदन्ती वनमाप सा ॥ 42 ॥
4.47.m:
At the command of her husband, bowing to her husband in fear,
crying 'Lord, Lord!' and weeping, she went into the forest.

4.47.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi bhuktvā bhogaṃ munipriyā ..
śrīrāmacaraṇasparśātsadyaḥ śuddhā babhūva ha ..43..
4.47.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि भुक्त्वा भोगं मुनिप्रिया ॥
श्रीरामचरणस्पर्शात्सद्यः शुद्धा बभूव ह ॥43॥
4.47.m:
Having endured her retribution for sixty thousand years, that beloved of the sage
became purified instantly by the touch of glorious Rāma's feet.

4.47.s:
trailokyamohanaṃ rūpaṃ vidhāya munikāminī ..
jagāma gautamābhyāśaṃ muniḥ saṃprāpya sundarīm .. 44 ..
4.47.d:
त्रैलोक्यमोहनं रूपं विधाय मुनिकामिनी ॥
जगाम गौतमाभ्याशं मुनिः संप्राप्य सुन्दरीम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.47.m:
Assuming a form that enchanted the three worlds, the sage's wife
went near to Gautama; having recovered his beautiful wife, the sage [was pleased].

4.47.s:
atha śakrasya vṛttāṃtaṃ paramaṃ śṛṇu sundari ..
pāpaghnaṃ puṇyabījaṃ tatsaṃvyasya kathayāmi te .. 45 ..
4.47.d:
अथ शक्रस्य वृत्तांतं परमं शृणु सुन्दरि ॥
पापघ्नं पुण्यबीजं तत्संव्यस्य कथयामि ते ॥ 45 ॥
4.47.m:
"Now hear the supreme account of Indra, O beautiful woman,
which destroys sin and is the seed of merit; I shall narrate it to you in full detail.

4.47.s:
ekadā ca guroḥ kopātprakṛteravahelanāt ..
brahmahatyā vajrabhṛto babhūva hatacetasaḥ .. 46 ..
4.47.d:
एकदा च गुरोः कोपात्प्रकृतेरवहेलनात् ॥
ब्रह्महत्या वज्रभृतो बभूव हतचेतसः ॥ 46 ॥
4.47.m:
Once, due to the anger of his guru and his disregard for Prakṛti,
the sin of killing a brahmin came upon the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose senses were confounded.

4.47.s:
śakrastyaktagururdaivagrasto daityanipīḍitaḥ ..
jagāma śaraṇaṃ bhīto brahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ gurum .... 47 ..
4.47.d:
शक्रस्त्यक्तगुरुर्दैवग्रस्तो दैत्यनिपीडितः ॥
जगाम शरणं भीतो ब्रह्माणं जगतां गुरुम् ॥॥ 47 ॥
4.47.m:
Indra, having abandoned his guru, seized by fate and tormented by the Daityas,
terrified, went for refuge to Brahmā, the guru of the universe.

4.47.s:
tadājñayā viśvarūpaṃ cakāra ca purohitam ..
babhūva tatra viśvasto daivādbuddhihato hariḥ .. 48 ..
4.47.d:
तदाज्ञया विश्वरूपं चकार च पुरोहितम् ॥
बभूव तत्र विश्वस्तो दैवाद्बुद्धिहतो हरिः ॥ 48 ॥
4.47.m:
By his command, he made Viśvarūpa his family priest.
Hari [Indra] placed his trust in him there, his intellect clouded by fate.

4.47.s:
daityadauhitrasya bhāvaṃ vijñāya ca vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
praciccheda śirastasya tīkṣṇabāṇena līlayā .. 49 ..
4.47.d:
दैत्यदौहित्रस्य भावं विज्ञाय च विचक्षणः ॥
प्रचिच्छेद शिरस्तस्य तीक्ष्णबाणेन लीलया ॥ 49 ॥
4.47.m:
Then, discerning the intention of that grandson of a Daitya, the wise [Indra]
severed his head effortlessly with a sharp arrow.

4.47.s:
viśvarūpapitā tvaṣṭā śrutvā sadyaścukopa ha ..
iṃdraśatro vivarddhasvetyuktvā yajñaṃ cakāra ha .. 4.47.50 ..
4.47.d:
विश्वरूपपिता त्वष्टा श्रुत्वा सद्यश्चुकोप ह ॥
इंद्रशत्रो विवर्द्धस्वेत्युक्त्वा यज्ञं चकार ह ॥ 4.47.50 ॥
4.47.m:
Tvaṣṭṛ, the father of Viśvarūpa, hearing of it, instantly became enraged.
Saying, 'O enemy of Indra, grow forth!', he performed a sacrifice.

4.47.s:
yajñakuṃḍātsamuttasthau vṛtro nāma mahāsuraḥ ..
cakāra nigrahaṃ kopāddevānāmavalīlayā.. 51 ..
4.47.d:
यज्ञकुंडात्समुत्तस्थौ वृत्रो नाम महासुरः ॥
चकार निग्रहं कोपाद्देवानामवलीलया॥ 51 ॥
4.47.m:
From the sacrificial fire-pit arose a great Asura named Vṛtra.
In anger, he easily subjugated the gods.

4.47.s:
śakro mahāmunerasthnāṃ vajraṃ kṛtvā sudāruṇam ..
jaghāna vṛtraṃ devānāṃ kaṃṭakaṃ daityamardanaḥ .. 52 ..
4.47.d:
शक्रो महामुनेरस्थ्नां वज्रं कृत्वा सुदारुणम् ॥
जघान वृत्रं देवानां कंटकं दैत्यमर्दनः ॥ 52 ॥
4.47.m:
Indra, having made a dreadful thunderbolt from the bones of a great sage,
slew Vṛtra, the thorn in the side of the gods, being the crusher of Daityas.

4.47.s:
brahmahatyā śunāsīraṃ dudrāva hatacetanam ..
raktavastraparīdhānā vṛtrastrīveṣadhāriṇī .. 53 ..
4.47.d:
ब्रह्महत्या शुनासीरं दुद्राव हतचेतनम् ॥
रक्तवस्त्रपरीधाना वृत्रस्त्रीवेषधारिणी ॥ 53 ॥
4.47.m:
Then the sin of killing a brahmin rushed toward Śunāsīra [Indra], whose mind was bewildered,
clad in red garments, wearing the guise of Vṛtra's wife.

4.47.s:
saptatālapramāṇā sā śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukā ..
īṣāpramāṇadaśanā mahābhītaṃ cakāra tam .. 94 ..
4.47.d:
सप्ततालप्रमाणा सा शुष्ककण्ठोष्ठतालुका ॥
ईषाप्रमाणदशना महाभीतं चकार तम् ॥ 94 ॥
4.47.m:
She was seven palmyra trees in height, with parched throat, lips, and palate;
with teeth the size of cart-poles, she struck great terror into him.

4.47.s:
dhāvaṃtaṃ paridhāvaṃtī baliṣṭhā hatacetanam ..
khaḍgahastā dayāhīnā vegena paridhāvati .. 55 ..
4.47.d:
धावंतं परिधावंती बलिष्ठा हतचेतनम् ॥
खड्गहस्ता दयाहीना वेगेन परिधावति ॥ 55 ॥
4.47.m:
As he fled, she, mighty, ran pursuing him whose mind was bewildered;
holding a sword in her hand, pitiless, she ran with great speed.

4.47.s:
iṃdro dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ ghorāṃ smāraṃsmāraṃ guroḥ padam ..
viveśa mānasasaro mṛṇālasūkṣmasūtrataḥ .. 56..
4.47.d:
इंद्रो दृष्ट्वा च तां घोरां स्मारंस्मारं गुरोः पदम् ॥
विवेश मानससरो मृणालसूक्ष्मसूत्रतः ॥ 56॥
4.47.m:
Seeing that terrible female and constantly remembering the feet of his guru,
Indra entered lake Mānasa through a minute lotus-fibre.

4.47.s:
tatra gaṃtuṃ na śaktā sā brahmaṇaḥ śāpakāraṇāt ..
sā tasthau vaṭaśākhāyāṃ sarasastaṭasannidhau .. 57 ..
4.47.d:
तत्र गंतुं न शक्ता सा ब्रह्मणः शापकारणात् ॥
सा तस्थौ वटशाखायां सरसस्तटसन्निधौ ॥ 57 ॥
4.47.m:
Unable to go there because of the curse of Brahmā,
she stayed on the branch of a banyan tree near the bank of the lake.

4.47.s:
athātra nahuṣo bhūpastrilokeśo babhūva ha ..
sa yayāce śacīṃ devānbaliṣṭho durbalānapi .. 58 ..
4.47.d:
अथात्र नहुषो भूपस्त्रिलोकेशो बभूव ह ॥
स ययाचे शचीं देवान्बलिष्ठो दुर्बलानपि ॥ 58 ॥
4.47.m:
Then here king Nahuṣa became the ruler of the three worlds.
He, being strong, demanded Śacī from the gods, who were weak.

4.47.s:
śacī śrutvā mahābhītā tārakāṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau ..
tārā nirbhartsya svapatiṃ bhṛtyapatnīṃ rarakṣa ca .. 59 ..
4.47.d:
शची श्रुत्वा महाभीता तारकां शरणं ययौ ॥
तारा निर्भर्त्स्य स्वपतिं भृत्यपत्नीं ररक्ष च ॥ 59 ॥
4.47.m:
Śacī, hearing this, was deeply terrified and went to Tārakā for refuge.
Rebuking her own husband, Tārā protected the servant's wife.

4.47.s:
śacīmāśvāsya svagururjagāma tatsaro mudā ..
ājuhāva śunāsīraṃ kātaraṃ hatacetanam .. 4.47.60 ..
4.47.d:
शचीमाश्वास्य स्वगुरुर्जगाम तत्सरो मुदा ॥
आजुहाव शुनासीरं कातरं हतचेतनम् ॥ 4.47.60 ॥
4.47.m:
Having consoled Śacī, their guru joyfully went to that lake.
He called out to Śunāsīra, who was distressed and senseless.

4.47.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca ..
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha he vatsa bhayaṃ kiṃ te mayi sthite ..
tvadīśvaraṃ svareṇaiva niśāmaya bhayaṃ tyaja ..
svaraṃ bṛhaspaterjñātvā sarvasiddhīśvaro hariḥ .. 61 ..
4.47.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ हे वत्स भयं किं ते मयि स्थिते ॥
त्वदीश्वरं स्वरेणैव निशामय भयं त्यज ॥
स्वरं बृहस्पतेर्ज्ञात्वा सर्वसिद्धीश्वरो हरिः ॥ 61 ॥
4.47.m:
"Arise, arise, O child! What fear can you have while I am here?
Recognise your master by his voice alone; cast away your fear!"
Recognising the voice of Bṛhaspati, Hari, the master of all perfections,

4.47.s:
sūkṣmarūpaṃ parityajya svarūpaṃ ca dadhāra saḥ ..
utthāya sadyaḥ saṃbhrāto guruṃ taṃ sūryavarcasam ..62..
4.47.d:
सूक्ष्मरूपं परित्यज्य स्वरूपं च दधार सः ॥
उत्थाय सद्यः संभ्रातो गुरुं तं सूर्यवर्चसम् ॥62॥
4.47.m:
abandoned his subtle form and assumed his own form.
Rising at once, bewildered, seeing that guru who had the radiance of the sun,

4.47.s:
dṛṣṭvā nanāma saṃprītyā saṃprītaṃ tyaktakopakam ..
padāṃbuje nipatitaṃ rudaṃtaṃ bhayavihvalam .. 63 ..
4.47.d:
दृष्ट्वा ननाम संप्रीत्या संप्रीतं त्यक्तकोपकम् ॥
पदांबुजे निपतितं रुदंतं भयविह्वलम् ॥ 63 ॥
4.47.m:
he bowed with great affection to him, who was pleased and had cast aside his anger.
[The guru,] placing on his chest with love him who had fallen at his lotus feet,

4.47.s:
nidhāya vakṣasi premṇā ruroda premavihvalaḥ ..
rudaṃtaṃ vākpatiṃ tuṣṭaṃ tuṣṭāva tridaśeśvaraḥ ..
puṭāṃjaliḥ pulakito bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharaḥ .. 64 ..
4.47.d:
निधाय वक्षसि प्रेम्णा रुरोद प्रेमविह्वलः ॥
रुदंतं वाक्पतिं तुष्टं तुष्टाव त्रिदशेश्वरः ॥
पुटांजलिः पुलकितो भक्तिनम्रात्मकंधरः ॥ 64 ॥
4.47.m:
weeping and overwhelmed with fear, himself wept, overwhelmed with love.
To the Lord of Speech who was weeping, now content, the lord of the gods offered praise,
with folded hands, his hair standing on end, his neck bowed in devotion.

4.47.s:
iṃdra uvāca ..
kṣamasva bhagavandoṣaṃ kṛpāṃ kuru kṛpānidhe .. 65 ..
4.47.d:
इंद्र उवाच ॥
क्षमस्व भगवन्दोषं कृपां कुरु कृपानिधे ॥ 65 ॥
4.47.m: "Forgive my fault, O Lord; grant mercy, O treasure of compassion!

4.47.s:
bhṛtyāparādhaṃ satataṃ na gṛhṇāti sadīśvaraḥ ..
svabhāryāsu svaśiṣyeṣu svabhṛtyeṣu suteṣu ca .. 66 ..
4.47.d:
भृत्यापराधं सततं न गृह्णाति सदीश्वरः ॥
स्वभार्यासु स्वशिष्येषु स्वभृत्येषु सुतेषु च ॥ 66 ॥
4.47.m:
A true master never takes note of the offense of a servant.
Towards one's own wives, disciples, servants, and sons,

4.47.s:
durbalaḥ sabalo vā'pi ko daṃḍaṃ kartumakṣamaḥ ..
triṣu koṭiṣu deveṣu devako'hamapaṃḍitaḥ ..67..
4.47.d:
दुर्बलः सबलो वाऽपि को दंडं कर्तुमक्षमः ॥
त्रिषु कोटिषु देवेषु देवकोऽहमपंडितः ॥67॥
4.47.m:
who, whether weak or strong, is incapable of inflicting punishment?
Among the thirty million gods, I am an ignorant minor god.

4.47.s:
tvatprasādātsuraśreṣṭha kṛpayā varddhitastvayā ..
saṃhartumīśastvaṃ sarvamahaṃ ko vāpi kīṭavat .. 68 ..
4.47.d:
त्वत्प्रसादात्सुरश्रेष्ठ कृपया वर्द्धितस्त्वया ॥
संहर्तुमीशस्त्वं सर्वमहं को वापि कीटवत् ॥ 68 ॥
4.47.m:
By your favour, O best of gods, I was raised up by your grace.
You are capable of destroying everything; but what am I, [insignificant] like a worm?

4.47.s:
svayaṃ vidhātuḥ pautraśca punaḥ sraṣṭuṃ svayaṃ kṣamaḥ ..
iti tasya stavaṃ śrutvā parituṣṭo guruḥ svayam ..
uvāca vacanaṃ prītyā prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ .. 69 ..
4.47.d:
स्वयं विधातुः पौत्रश्च पुनः स्रष्टुं स्वयं क्षमः ॥
इति तस्य स्तवं श्रुत्वा परितुष्टो गुरुः स्वयम् ॥
उवाच वचनं प्रीत्या प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ॥ 69 ॥
4.47.m:
You are yourself the grandson of the Creator, capable yourself of creating anew."
Hearing his hymn of praise, the guru himself, thoroughly pleased,
spoke these words with affection, his face and eyes gracious.

4.47.s:
gururuvāca ..
sthiro bhava mahābhāga niścalāṃ kamalāṃ labha .. 4.47.70 ..
4.47.d:
गुरुरुवाच ॥
स्थिरो भव महाभाग निश्चलां कमलां लभ ॥ 4.47.70 ॥
4.47.m: "Be steadfast, O highly fortunate one! Attain unwavering Kamalā!

4.47.s:
saṃprāpya paramaiśvaryaṃ pūrvasmācca caturguṇam ..
gacchāmarāvatīṃ vatsa rājyaṃ kuru puraṃdara .. 71 ..
4.47.d:
संप्राप्य परमैश्वर्यं पूर्वस्माच्च चतुर्गुणम् ॥
गच्छामरावतीं वत्स राज्यं कुरु पुरंदर ॥ 71 ॥
4.47.m:
Having obtained supreme sovereignty, fourfold greater than before,
go to Amarāvatī, my child; rule the kingdom, O Puraṃdara!

4.47.s:
hataśatrurmatprasādādgatvā paśya śacīṃ satīm ..
ityevamuktvā sa guruḥ saśiṣyo gaṃtumudyataḥ .. 72 ..
4.47.d:
हतशत्रुर्मत्प्रसादाद्गत्वा पश्य शचीं सतीम् ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स गुरुः सशिष्यो गंतुमुद्यतः ॥ 72 ॥
4.47.m:
With your enemies slain by my favour, go and see the virtuous Śacī."
Having spoken thus, that guru prepared to go together with his disciple.

4.47.s:
dadarśa purato ghorāṃ brahmahatyāṃ suduḥsahām ..
dṛṣṭvā śakro mahābhītastaṃ guruṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau .. 73 ..
4.47.d:
ददर्श पुरतो घोरां ब्रह्महत्यां सुदुःसहाम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा शक्रो महाभीतस्तं गुरुं शरणं ययौ ॥ 73 ॥
4.47.m:
Before him he saw the terrible, unbearable sin of slaying a brahmin.
Seeing it, Śakra was terrified and sought refuge with that guru.

4.47.s:
bṛhaspatirmahābhītaḥ sasmāra madhusūdanam ..
etasminnaṃtare tatra vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī .. 74 ..
4.47.d:
बृहस्पतिर्महाभीतः सस्मार मधुसूदनम् ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र वाग्बभूवाशरीरिणी ॥ 74 ॥
4.47.m:
Bṛhaspati, greatly frightened, remembered Madhusūdana.
In the meantime, a bodiless voice arose there,

4.47.s:
svalpākṣarā ca bahvarthā tāṃ śuśrāva bṛhaspatiḥ ..
saṃsāravijayaṃ nāma sarvāśubhavināśanam .. 75 ..
4.47.d:
स्वल्पाक्षरा च बह्वर्था तां शुश्राव बृहस्पतिः ॥
संसारविजयं नाम सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.47.m:
consisting of few syllables and having vast meaning; Bṛhaspati heard it:
"The one named Saṃsāravijaya, which destroys all inauspiciousness—"

4.47.s:
rādhike vacanaṃ śrutvā śiṣyaṃ rakṣādhuneti ca..
tadā tvatkavacaṃ dattvā śiṣyāya śiṣyavatsalaḥ ..76..
4.47.d:
राधिके वचनं श्रुत्वा शिष्यं रक्षाधुनेति च॥
तदा त्वत्कवचं दत्त्वा शिष्याय शिष्यवत्सलः ॥76॥
4.47.m:
O Rādhikā!—hearing the words, "Now protect your disciple!"
he who was affectionate to his disciple then gave your armour to the disciple,

4.47.s:
cakāra bhasmasāttāṃ ca huṃkāreṇaiva līlayā ..
tadā śiṣyaṃ gṛhītvā ca gatvā tāmamarāvatīm ..77..
4.47.d:
चकार भस्मसात्तां च हुंकारेणैव लीलया ॥
तदा शिष्यं गृहीत्वा च गत्वा ताममरावतीम् ॥77॥
4.47.m:
and with a mere "huṃ" effortlessly reduced her to ashes.
Then, taking his disciple and going to that Amarāvatī,

4.47.s:
dadarśa cchinnabhagnāṃ ca śatruṇā vacanādguroḥ ..
bharturāgamanaṃ śrutvā śacī saṃhṛṣṭamānasā ..78..
4.47.d:
ददर्श च्छिन्नभग्नां च शत्रुणा वचनाद्गुरोः ॥
भर्तुरागमनं श्रुत्वा शची संहृष्टमानसा ॥78॥
4.47.m:
he saw it torn and broken by the enemy, according to the words of the guru.
Hearing of her husband's arrival, Śacī, delighted in mind,

4.47.s:
praṇamya ca guruṃ bhaktyā svakāṃtaṃ praṇanāma sā ..
śrutvā''gamanamiṃdrasya samājagmuḥ surāḥ priye ..
ṛṣayo munayaścaiva harṣagadgadamānasāḥ ..79 ..
4.47.d:
प्रणम्य च गुरुं भक्त्या स्वकांतं प्रणनाम सा ॥
श्रुत्वा'ऽगमनमिंद्रस्य समाजग्मुः सुराः प्रिये ॥
ऋषयो मुनयश्चैव हर्षगद्गदमानसाः ॥79 ॥
4.47.m:
bowed down to the guru with devotion, and bowed to her husband.
Hearing of Indra's arrival, the gods came together, O beloved,
as well as the rishis and sages, their minds faltering with joy.

4.47.s:
yojayāmāsa satkāraṃ nirmātumamarāvatīm ..
pūrṇamabdaśataṃ śilpī nirmame tvamarāvatīm.. 4.47.80 ..
4.47.d:
योजयामास सत्कारं निर्मातुममरावतीम् ॥
पूर्णमब्दशतं शिल्पी निर्ममे त्वमरावतीम्॥ 4.47.80 ॥
4.47.m:
He made preparations to rebuild Amarāvatī.
For a full hundred years the artisan built Amarāvatī,

4.47.s:
nānāratnavicitrāḍhyāṃ maṇiratneṃdranirmitām ..
manoharāṃ nirupamāṃ na hi tuṣṭo yayā hariḥ ..81..
4.47.d:
नानारत्नविचित्राढ्यां मणिरत्नेंद्रनिर्मिताम् ॥
मनोहरां निरुपमां न हि तुष्टो यया हरिः ॥81॥
4.47.m:
richly adorned with diverse gems, built with sapphire and ruby;
yet, charming and peerless as it was, Hari was not satisfied by it.

4.47.s:
viśvakarmā gṛhaṃ gaṃtuṃ na śaśāka vinā''jñayā..
paramodvignacittaśca brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau .. 82 ..
4.47.d:
विश्वकर्मा गृहं गंतुं न शशाक विना'ऽज्ञया॥
परमोद्विग्नचित्तश्च ब्रह्माणं शरणं ययौ ॥ 82 ॥
4.47.m:
Viśvakarman was unable to go home without permission;
with a deeply agitated mind, he sought refuge with Brahmā.

4.47.s:
vijñāya tadabhiprāyaṃ tamuvāca vidhiḥ svayam ..
tava karmakṣayādeva tāvacchvo bhaviteti ca ..83..
4.47.d:
विज्ञाय तदभिप्रायं तमुवाच विधिः स्वयम् ॥
तव कर्मक्षयादेव तावच्छ्वो भवितेति च ॥83॥
4.47.m:
Knowing his intention, the Creator himself said to him:
"Only through the exhaustion of your work shall that happen tomorrow."

4.47.s:
śrutvā tadvacanaṃ kāruḥ śīghraṃ prāpāmarāvatīm ..
brahmā jagāma vaikuṇṭhe praṇamyovāca mātaram ..84..
4.47.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं कारुः शीघ्रं प्रापामरावतीम् ॥
ब्रह्मा जगाम वैकुण्ठे प्रणम्योवाच मातरम् ॥84॥
4.47.m:
Hearing his word, the craftsman quickly reached Amarāvatī.
Brahmā went to Vaikuṇṭha, bowed, and spoke to his mother.

4.47.s:
harirbrahmāṇamāśvāsya prasthāpya svagṛhaṃ ca tam ..
viprarūpaṃ samāsthāya cājagāmāmarāvatīm .. 85 ..
4.47.d:
हरिर्ब्रह्माणमाश्वास्य प्रस्थाप्य स्वगृहं च तम् ॥
विप्ररूपं समास्थाय चाजगामामरावतीम् ॥ 85 ॥
4.47.m:
Hari, reassuring Brahmā and sending him to his own abode,
assumed the form of a brahmin and came to Amarāvatī.

4.47.s:
daṇḍī chattrī śuklavāsā bibhrattilakamujjvalam ..
atikharvaḥ śukladaṃtaḥ sasmitaḥ sumanoharaḥ .. 86 ..
4.47.d:
दण्डी छत्त्री शुक्लवासा बिभ्रत्तिलकमुज्ज्वलम् ॥
अतिखर्वः शुक्लदंतः सस्मितः सुमनोहरः ॥ 86 ॥
4.47.m:
Carrying a staff and parasol, clad in white garments, bearing a radiant tilaka,
very dwarfish, with white teeth, smiling, and exceedingly handsome.

4.47.s:
vayasā'tiśiśurbuddhyā jñānavṛddhyā vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
svayaṃ vidhāturdhātā ca dātā ca sarvasaṃpadām .. 87 ..
4.47.d:
वयसाऽतिशिशुर्बुद्ध्या ज्ञानवृद्ध्या विचक्षणः ॥
स्वयं विधातुर्धाता च दाता च सर्वसंपदाम् ॥ 87 ॥
4.47.m:
In age a very young child, but in intellect, through the growth of knowledge, discerning;
himself the creator of the creator, and the giver of all fortunes.

4.47.s:
iṃdradvāre samuttiṣṭhandvārapālamuvāca ha ..
brūhīdaṃ brahmaṇo dvāre śīghraṃ tvāṃ draṣṭumāgataḥ .. 88 ..
4.47.d:
इंद्रद्वारे समुत्तिष्ठन्द्वारपालमुवाच ह ॥
ब्रूहीदं ब्रह्मणो द्वारे शीघ्रं त्वां द्रष्टुमागतः ॥ 88 ॥
4.47.m:
Standing at Indra's door, he spoke to the door-keeper:
“Say this at the door: ‘A brāhmaṇa has quickly come to see you.’”

4.47.s:
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā dvāri jñānaṃ cakāra tam ..
sa ca śīghraṃ samāgamya dadarśa brāhmaṇārbhakam .. 89 ..
4.47.d:
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा द्वारि ज्ञानं चकार तम् ॥
स च शीघ्रं समागम्य ददर्श ब्राह्मणार्भकम् ॥ 89 ॥
4.47.m:
Hearing this speech, the doorkeeper informed him.
And coming quickly, he saw the brāhmaṇa boy

4.47.s:
bālakānāṃ bālikānāṃ samūhaiḥ pariveṣṭitam ..
hasadbhiśca mahotsāhātsasmitaṃ tejasā'nvitam .. 4.47.90 ..
4.47.d:
बालकानां बालिकानां समूहैः परिवेष्टितम् ॥
हसद्भिश्च महोत्साहात्सस्मितं तेजसाऽन्वितम् ॥ 4.47.90 ॥
4.47.m:
surrounded by crowds of boys and girls,
who were laughing with great excitement, smiling and endowed with splendor.

4.47.s:
praṇanāma harirbhaktyā taṃ hariṃ śiśurūpiṇam ..
āśiṣaṃ yuyuje prītyā taṃ harirbhaktavatsalaḥ .. 91 ..
4.47.d:
प्रणनाम हरिर्भक्त्या तं हरिं शिशुरूपिणम् ॥
आशिषं युयुजे प्रीत्या तं हरिर्भक्तवत्सलः ॥ 91 ॥
4.47.m:
Hari [Indra] bowed down with devotion to that Hari in the form of a child;
Hari, affectionate to his devotees, gladly bestowed a blessing upon him.

4.47.s:
madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā śakraḥ pūjāṃ cakāra tam ..
papracchāgamanaṃ kasmādvadeti viprabālakam .. 92 ..
4.47.d:
मधुपर्कादिकं दत्त्वा शक्रः पूजां चकार तम् ॥
पप्रच्छागमनं कस्माद्वदेति विप्रबालकम् ॥ 92 ॥
4.47.m:
Having offered the honey-mixture and other honors, Śakra worshipped him;
and he asked the brāhmaṇa boy: “Speak, why have you come?”

4.47.s:
iṃdrasya vacanaṃ śrutvā tamuvāca dvijārbhakaḥ ..
megha gambhīrayā vācā bṛhaspatigurorguruḥ .. 93 ..
4.47.d:
इंद्रस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तमुवाच द्विजार्भकः ॥
मेघ गम्भीरया वाचा बृहस्पतिगुरोर्गुरुः ॥ 93 ॥
4.47.m: with a voice deep as a thundercloud—he, the teacher of Bṛhaspati's teacher.

4.47.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca ..
samāgato'haṃ tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ praṣṭuṃ vacanamīpsitam ..
citraṃ nagaranirmāṇaṃ samākarṇyādbhutaṃ hare .. 94 ..
4.47.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच ॥
समागतोऽहं त्वां द्रष्टुं प्रष्टुं वचनमीप्सितम् ॥
चित्रं नगरनिर्माणं समाकर्ण्याद्भुतं हरे ॥ 94 ॥
4.47.m:
“I have come to see you and to ask a desired question,
having heard of the marvelous, wonderful construction of your city, O Hari [Indra].

4.47.s:
kativarṣaṃ ca nirmāṇe bhavānsaṃkalpito yathā ..
katicittāṃ viśvakarmā nirmāṇaṃ vā kariṣyati .... 95 ..
4.47.d:
कतिवर्षं च निर्माणे भवान्संकल्पितो यथा ॥

4.47.m:
“I know your father, child, the Prajāpati Kaśyapa,
and his father, the sage named Marīci, a treasure of austerity;
and, having praised him, the Lord Brahmā arisen from Viṣṇu's navel-lotus,
and that Viṣṇu, the protector, endowed with the supreme quality of sattva;
and the dissolution into a single ocean, devoid of living beings and terrible.
How manifold is creation, O Śakra, and how manifold is the kalpa, indeed!
And how manifold is the cosmic egg, and the Brahmās, Viṣṇus, and Maheśvaras!
Who is capable of traversing how many kinds of Indras there are across the cosmic eggs?
Even if there were a counting of the particles of dust upon the earth, O lord of the gods,
still there is no counting of Śakras—so the wise know.
Śakra's lifespan and tenure of authority is seventy-one yugas;
with the fall of twenty-eight Śakras, a day and night of Brahmā passes.
The lifespan of Brahmā by measure is indeed one hundred and eight [years];
and what count is there of lord Indras? There is no counting of Brahmās either!

Everywhere there is a count of cosmic eggs, there are Brahmās, Viṣṇus, and Maheśvaras.
In the utterly pure waters born from the hair-pores of Mahāviṣṇu,
a cosmic egg exists just as an artificial boat floats on the ocean of existence.
Thus, according to the measure of his hairs, the cosmic eggs are countless.
And in a cosmic egg, how manifold are the gods who are just like you!

his throat, lips, and palate parched with thirst, [Indra] again questioned the brāhmaṇa:
“Why do you laugh, O best of brāhmaṇas? Tell me the reason quickly!
Or who are you, concealed by māyā, appearing as a child, an ocean of virtues?”
spiritual wisdom, the essence of conduct, the supreme, excellent seed of knowledge.
“A swarm of ants has been seen; the reason for this is deeply hidden.
"Do not ask me, [for it is] the seed of grief, the cause of knowledge distinct from yours,
the felling of the root of the tree of worldly existence for worldly beings,
an unsurpassed lamp of knowledge, concealed by the darkness of ignorance,
hidden in all the Vedas, hard to attain even for the Siddhas,

Having spoken thus, the eminent twice-born remained standing there, smiling.
Śakra questioned him again, his throat, lips, and palate parched.
"Tell me quickly, O young Brahmin boy, this ancient lamp of knowledge.
I do not know who you are, a child [yet] a heap of wisdom embodied in person."
Hearing Indra's words, Janārdana in the form of a Brahmin
began to impart knowledge exceedingly hard to attain for lords of yogins.

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शीघ्रमाजगाम मुनीश्वरः ॥ 33 ॥
अतिवृद्धो महायोगी ज्ञानेन वयसा महान् ॥
कृष्णाजिनी जटाधारी बिभ्रत्तिलकमुज्ज्वलम् ॥॥ 34 ॥
वक्षःस्थले रोमचक्रं बिभर्ति मस्तके कटम् ॥
स्थितं सर्वं मध्यदेशे किंचिदुत्पाटितं स्फुटम् ॥ 35 ॥
समागत्य द्वयोर्मध्ये तस्थौ स्थाणुवदेव सः ॥
महेन्द्रो ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा प्रणनाम मुदाऽन्वितः ॥ 36 ॥
4.47.m:
bestowing happiness, bestowing merit, essential, ferrying across the ocean of hell.
The whole world, moving and unmoving, O lord of the gods, is like a dream.
And death sits on the head of all through the conjunction of time.
All fortune and misfortune of living beings is like a bubble in water.
O Śakra, it ever revolves; the wise man is not attached to it."
Having spoken thus, the Brahmin remained standing there, smiling.
Astonished, the sovereign of the gods did not hold himself in high esteem.
In that interval, there quickly arrived a great sage,
exceedingly aged, a great yogin, great in wisdom and in years,
wearing a black antelope skin, bearing matted locks, displaying a radiant tilaka mark.
He bore a circle of hair on his chest and a straw mat on his head,
which was all present in the middle, [though] partly plucked out clearly.
Having arrived, he stood between the two like a pillar.
Seeing the Brahmin, Mahendra, filled with joy, bowed down.

4.47.s:
madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ ..

मधुपर्कादिकं दत्त्वा पूजयामास भक्तितः ॥

तुष्टावातिथिभावेन मुदा सादरपूर्वकम् ॥

स्ववाञ्छितं परं प्राह सर्वं विनयपूर्वकम् ॥ 38 ॥
बालक उवाच ॥
कुतस्त्वमागतो विप्र किन्नाम तव वा वद ॥
को वाऽत्रागमने हेतुर्निवासः केन हेतुना ॥ 39 ॥
4.47.m:
He asked after the Brahmin's welfare and showed him deference once more.
He praised him as a guest, joyfully and respectfully.
That Brahmin child engaged in conversation with him,
and uttered all of his highest wish with utter humility.
"Where have you come from, O Brahmin? Tell me, what is your name?
Or what is the purpose of coming here, and for what reason is your dwelling?

4.47.s:
kaṭaṃ kathaṃ mastake te lomacakraṃ ca vakṣasi ..

4.47.d:
कटं कथं मस्तके ते लोमचक्रं च वक्षसि ॥
अत्युन्नतं मध्यदेशे किंचिदुत्पाटितं मुने ॥॥ 4.47.140 ॥
मां चेत्कृपाऽस्ति ते विप्र सर्वं संव्यस्य कथ्यताम् ॥
अत्यद्भुतमिदं सर्वं श्रोतुं कौतूहलं मम ॥ 41 ॥
स शिशोर्वचनं श्रुत्वा तमुवाच महामुनिः ॥
सर्वं स्वकीयवृत्तान्तं शक्रस्य पुरतो मुदा ॥42॥
मुनिरुवाच ॥ अल्पायुषा मया विप्र कुत्रापि न कृता गृहाः ॥
न विवाहश्चोपजीव्यं भिक्षोपजीविनाऽधुना ॥ 43 ॥
लोमशेति च मन्नाम हेतुर्विप्रस्य दर्शनम् ॥
वर्षणातपशान्त्यर्थं मस्तकस्थं कटं मम ॥ 44 ॥
वक्षस्थलस्थितं रोमचक्रं तत्कारणं शृणु ॥
सांसारिकाणां भयदं विवेकजननं परम् ॥ 45 ॥
आयुःसंख्याप्रमाणं मे लोमचक्रं च वक्षसि ॥
शक्रैकपतनं विप्र लोमैकोत्पाटनं मम ॥ 46॥
4.47.m:
Why is there a straw mat on your head, and a circle of hair on your chest,
raised high in the middle and partly plucked out, O sage?
If you have compassion for me, O Brahmin, let all be told in detail.
All this is very wondrous; my curiosity is keen to hear it."
Hearing the child's words, that great sage spoke to him,
joyfully narrating his entire story in the presence of Śakra.
The sage said: / 'O brahmin, having a short life, I have nowhere built a house;
nor [have I undertaken] marriage or a livelihood, living now on alms.
My name is Lomaśa, and the reason is seen by a brahmin:
to ward off rain and heat, a straw mat rests on my head.
Hear the cause of the circle of hair on my chest:
it causes fear to worldly men and brings forth supreme discernment.
The circle of hair upon my chest is the measure of the span of my life:
with the fall of one Indra, O brahmin, one hair of mine is plucked out.

4.47.s:
utpāditāni lomāni tena madhye sthitāni ca ..

kalatreṇa ca putreṇa gṛheṇa kiṃ prayojanam .. 48 ..

4.47.d:
उत्पादितानि लोमानि तेन मध्ये स्थितानि च ॥
ब्रह्मणो द्विपरार्धे च मम मृत्युर्निरूपितः ॥ 47 ॥
असंख्यविधयो ब्रह्मन्मरिष्यन्ति मृता अपि ॥
कलत्रेण च पुत्रेण गृहेण किं प्रयोजनम् ॥ 48 ॥
ब्रह्मणः पतने चक्षुर्निमेषश्च हरेर्भवेत् ॥
तत्पादपद्ममतुलं चिन्तयामि निरंतरम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.47.m:
The hairs in the middle were plucked out by that;
and at the end of two parārdhas of Brahmā, my death is ordained.
Countless Brahmās, O brahmin, will die, and [countless] have died.
What is the use of a wife, a son, or a house?
At the fall of a Brahmā, a twinkling of an eye of Hari occurs.
I constantly meditate on his peerless lotus feet.

4.47.s:
durlabhaṃ śrīharerdāsyaṃ bhaktirmuktirgarīyasī ..

śacī jagāma śokārtā saṃtrastā śaraṇaṃ guroḥ .. 55 ..
4.47.d:
दुर्लभं श्रीहरेर्दास्यं भक्तिर्मुक्तिर्गरीयसी ॥
स्वप्नवत्सर्वमैश्वर्यं तद्भक्तिव्यवधायकम् ॥ 4.47.150 ॥
इदं मद्गुरुणा दत्तं शंभुना ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥
विना भक्तिं न गृह्णामि सालोक्यादिचतुष्टयम् ॥ 51 ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स मुनिर्जगाम शिवसन्निधिम् ॥
शिशुरूपी हरिस्तत्रैवान्तर्धानं चकार ह ॥ 52 ॥
इन्द्रस्तु स्वप्नवद्दृष्ट्वा बभूव तत्र विस्मितः ॥
तृष्णामात्रं च संपत्तौ नास्त्येव परमेश्वरे ॥ 53 ॥
विश्वकर्माणमानीय प्रियमुक्त्वा शतक्रतुः ॥
दत्त्वा रत्नानि संपूज्य तं प्रस्थापितवान्गृहम् ॥ 54 ॥
सर्वं विन्यस्य पुत्रे च शरणं गन्तुमुद्यतः ॥
शचीं राज्यश्रियं त्यक्त्वा विवेकी क्षयकामुकः ॥ 55 ॥
दृष्ट्वा विवेकिनं कान्तं हृदयेन विदूयता ॥
शची जगाम शोकार्ता संत्रस्ता शरणं गुरोः ॥ 55 ॥
4.47.m:
Servitude to Śrī Hari is hard to attain; devotion is higher than liberation.
All lordly power is like a dream, an obstacle to devotion to him.
This supreme knowledge was given by my guru, Śambhu.
Without devotion, I do not accept the fourfold [liberation] such as sālokya.'
Having spoken thus, that sage went into the presence of Śiva;
and Hari in the form of a child vanished right there.
Indra, however, having seen [it] like a dream, was astonished there;
in the supreme lord there is no craving whatever for wealth.
Having summoned Viśvakarman and spoken pleasing words, Indra,
giving gems and honouring him, sent him home.
Entrusting everything to his son, he prepared to take refuge [in ascetic life],
abandoning Śacī and royal fortune, full of discernment, desiring renunciation.
Seeing her beloved full of discernment, with an aching heart,
Śacī, distressed by grief and alarmed, went to the guru for refuge.

4.47.m:
Having made all known, she brought Bṛhaspati,
and the lovely woman instructed Indra with the essence of moral conduct.
Having composed the guru's special treatise endowed with the sentiment of a married couple,
she herself with affection made him study it gladly.
The sage, the lord of speech, also instructed him in that special treatise;
then he ruled the kingdom, O delighter of Vṛndāvana!

4.47.m:

prītyā samarpayāmāsa śaṅkare dīnavatsale .. 15 ..
4.48.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा ब्रह्मा तं सूर्यमानीय भक्तितः ॥
प्रीत्या समर्पयामास शङ्करे दीनवत्सले ॥ 15 ॥
4.48.m: Brahmā lovingly surrendered him to Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to the humble. // 15

4.48.s:
śaṃbhustamāśiṣaṃ kṛtvā vidhiṃ natvā jagadvidhiḥ ..
prasannavadanaḥ śrīmānālayaṃ prayayau mudā .. 16 ..
4.48.d:
शंभुस्तमाशिषं कृत्वा विधिं नत्वा जगद्विधिः ॥
प्रसन्नवदनः श्रीमानालयं प्रययौ मुदा ॥ 16 ॥

4.48.s:
iti dhātṛkṛtaṃ stotraṃ saṃkaṭe yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ ..
bhayātpramucyate bhīto baddho mucyeta bandhanāt .. 17 ..
4.48.d:
इति धातृकृतं स्तोत्रं संकटे यः पठेन्नरः ॥
भयात्प्रमुच्यते भीतो बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥ 17 ॥

4.48.s:
rājadvāre śmaśāne ca magnapote mahārṇave ..
stotrasmaraṇamātreṇa mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 18 ..
4.48.d:
राजद्वारे श्मशाने च मग्नपोते महार्णवे ॥
स्तोत्रस्मरणमात्रेण मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 18 ॥

4.49.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
sūryaḥ praṇamya brahmāṇaṃ mudāyuktastadājñayā ..
cakāra vinayaṃ prītyā tejasvī triguṇātmakaḥ .. 1 ..
4.49.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
सूर्यः प्रणम्य ब्रह्माणं मुदायुक्तस्तदाज्ञया ॥
चकार विनयं प्रीत्या तेजस्वी त्रिगुणात्मकः ॥ 1 ॥

4.49.s:
atha vahnerupākhyānaṃ sāvadhānaṃ niśāmaya ..
gopanīyaṃ purāṇeṣu karṇapīyūṣamuttamam ..2..
4.49.d:
अथ वह्नेरुपाख्यानं सावधानं निशामय ॥
गोपनीयं पुराणेषु कर्णपीयूषमुत्तमम् ॥2॥

4.49.s:
trailokyaṃ bhasmasātkartumekadā'gniḥ samudyataḥ..
śatatālapramāṇāntāṃ śikhāṃ kṛtvā bhayānakīm..3..
4.49.d:
त्रैलोक्यं भस्मसात्कर्तुमेकदाऽग्निः समुद्यतः॥
शततालप्रमाणान्तां शिखां कृत्वा भयानकीम्॥3॥

4.49.s:
kṣubhitaḥ kupitaścaiva bhṛgoḥ śāpasya kāraṇāt ..
svaṃ ca tejasvinaṃ matvā tucchaṃ matvā'nyamātmanaḥ ..4..
4.49.d:
क्षुभितः कुपितश्चैव भृगोः शापस्य कारणात् ॥
स्वं च तेजस्विनं मत्वा तुच्छं मत्वाऽन्यमात्मनः ॥4॥

4.49.s:
etasminnantare viṣṇurājagāmāvalīlayā..
vahnestāṃ dāhikīṃ śaktiṃ tāṃ jahāra puraḥ sthitaḥ .. 5 ..
4.49.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विष्णुराजगामावलीलया॥
वह्नेस्तां दाहिकीं शक्तिं तां जहार पुरः स्थितः ॥ 5 ॥

4.49.s:
māyayā śiśurūpī ca tamuvāca janārdanaḥ ..
sasmito vinayaṃ kṛtvā bhaktinamrātmakandharaḥ .. 6 ..
4.49.d:
मायया शिशुरूपी च तमुवाच जनार्दनः ॥
सस्मितो विनयं कृत्वा भक्तिनम्रात्मकन्धरः ॥ 6 ॥

4.49.s:
śiśuruvāca ..
kathaṃ ruṣṭo'si bhagavanbhavānmāṃ kāraṇaṃ vada ..
trailokyaṃ bhasmasātkartumudyato'si nirarthakam ..7..
4.49.d:
शिशुरुवाच ॥
कथं रुष्टोऽसि भगवन्भवान्मां कारणं वद ॥
त्रैलोक्यं भस्मसात्कर्तुमुद्यतोऽसि निरर्थकम् ॥7॥

4.49.s:
tvameva bhṛguṇā śapto bhṛgośca damanaṃ kuru ..
ekāparādhāttrailokyaṃ bhasmīkartuṃ na cārhasi .. 8 ..
4.49.d:
त्वमेव भृगुणा शप्तो भृगोश्च दमनं कुरु ॥
एकापराधात्त्रैलोक्यं भस्मीकर्तुं न चार्हसि ॥ 8 ॥

4.49.s:
viśvaṃ ca brahmaṇā sṛṣṭaṃ tasya pātā svayaṃ hariḥ ..
saṃhartā bhagavānrudra evameva kramo bhavet .. 9 ..
4.49.d:
विश्वं च ब्रह्मणा सृष्टं तस्य पाता स्वयं हरिः ॥
संहर्ता भगवान्रुद्र एवमेव क्रमो भवेत् ॥ 9 ॥

4.49.s:
tatkathaṃ bhasmasātkartumīśvare śaṃkare sthite ..
rakṣitāraṃ hariṃ jitvā saṃhāraṃ kuru satvaram .. 4.49.10 ..
4.49.d:
तत्कथं भस्मसात्कर्तुमीश्वरे शंकरे स्थिते ॥
रक्षितारं हरिं जित्वा संहारं कुरु सत्वरम् ॥ 4.49.10 ॥

4.49.s:
ityuktvā brāhmaṇabaṭuḥ śarapatraṃ puraḥ sthitam ..
atiśuṣkaṃ kare dhṛtvā dagdhaṃ kartuṃ dadau mudā ..11..
4.49.d:
इत्युक्त्वा ब्राह्मणबटुः शरपत्रं पुरः स्थितम् ॥
अतिशुष्कं करे धृत्वा दग्धं कर्तुं ददौ मुदा ॥11॥

4.49.s:
dṛṣṭvā śuṣkendhano vahnirlelihāno bhayānakaḥ ..
sa vavre śikhayā vipraṃ meghena śaśinaṃ yathā .. 12 ..
4.49.d:
दृष्ट्वा शुष्केन्धनो वह्निर्लेलिहानो भयानकः ॥
स वव्रे शिखया विप्रं मेघेन शशिनं यथा ॥ 12 ॥

4.49.s:
na ca dagdhaṃ śuṣkapatraṃ lomaikaṃ ca śiśostathā ..
dṛṣṭvā vrīḍāyuto vahnirnistabdho hi śiśoḥ puraḥ ..13..
4.49.d:
न च दग्धं शुष्कपत्रं लोमैकं च शिशोस्तथा ॥
दृष्ट्वा व्रीडायुतो वह्निर्निस्तब्धो हि शिशोः पुरः ॥13॥

4.49.s:
kṛtvā vahnerdarpabhaṅgamantardhānaṃ cakāra saḥ ..
vahniḥ svamūrtiṃ saṃhṛtya svasthānaṃ bhītavadyayau .. 14 ..
4.49.d:
कृत्वा वह्नेर्दर्पभङ्गमन्तर्धानं चकार सः ॥
वह्निः स्वमूर्तिं संहृत्य स्वस्थानं भीतवद्ययौ ॥ 14 ॥

4.49.s:
ukto vahnerdarpabhaṅgaḥ paraṃ vai śrotumicchasi ..
nityanūtanamākhyānaṃ devānāṃ darpamocanam .. 15 ..
4.49.d:
उक्तो वह्नेर्दर्पभङ्गः परं वै श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
नित्यनूतनमाख्यानं देवानां दर्पमोचनम् ॥ 15 ॥

4.49.s:
śrīrādhikovāca ..
śeṣāṇāṃ darpabhaṃgaṃ ca krameṇa kathaya prabho ..
kathāpīyūṣadhārāṃte śrutvā tṛpyeta ko bhuvi .. 16 ..
4.49.d:
श्रीराधिकोवाच ॥
शेषाणां दर्पभंगं च क्रमेण कथय प्रभो ॥
कथापीयूषधारांते श्रुत्वा तृप्येत को भुवि ॥ 16 ॥

4.49.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
rādhikāvacanaṃ śrutvā sasmito bhagavānprabhuḥ ..
kathāṃ kathitumārebhe śrutvā ramyāṃ purātanīm .. 17 ..
4.49.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
राधिकावचनं श्रुत्वा सस्मितो भगवान्प्रभुः ॥
कथां कथितुमारेभे श्रुत्वा रम्यां पुरातनीम् ॥ 17 ॥

4.49.s: iti śrībrahmavaivarte mahāpurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍe nārāyaṇanāradasaṃvāde agnidarpamocanaṃ nāmaikonapañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 49 .. ..
4.49.d: इति श्रीब्रह्मवैवर्ते महापुराणे श्रीकृष्णजन्मखण्डे नारायणनारदसंवादे अग्निदर्पमोचनं नामैकोनपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ॥ 49 ॥ ॥

4.50.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
durvāsaso darpabhaṅgaṃ kathayāmi śṛṇu priye ..
mahāmuneryogataśca rudrāṃśasyātitejasaḥ ..1..
4.50.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
दुर्वाससो दर्पभङ्गं कथयामि शृणु प्रिये ॥
महामुनेर्योगतश्च रुद्रांशस्यातितेजसः ॥1॥
4.50.m:
I shall tell the breaking of Durvāsas's pride; listen, O beloved,
of the great sage proficient in yoga, an aṃśa of Rudra, endowed with supreme splendour. // 1

4.50.s:
ekadā cāmbarīṣaśca kṛtvā ca dvādaśīvratam ..
pāraṇaṃ kartumārebhe bhojayitvā dvijānbahūn .. 2 ..
4.50.d:
एकदा चाम्बरीषश्च कृत्वा च द्वादशीव्रतम् ॥
पारणं कर्तुमारेभे भोजयित्वा द्विजान्बहून् ॥ 2 ॥
4.50.m:
Once, Ambarīṣa, having observed the vow of Dvādaśī,
he began to break his fast, having fed many twice-borns.

4.50.s:
etasminnantare tatra cājagāma muniḥ svayam ..
kṣudhārtaśca tṛṣārttaśca viṣṇuvrataparāyaṇaḥ .. 3 ..
4.50.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र चाजगाम मुनिः स्वयम् ॥
क्षुधार्तश्च तृषार्त्तश्च विष्णुव्रतपरायणः ॥ 3 ॥
4.50.m:
At that moment, the sage himself arrived there,
afflicted by hunger and afflicted by thirst, devoted to the vow of Viṣṇu.

4.50.s:
māṃ bhojaya mahābhāgetyevaṃ sa nṛpamuktavān ..
rājā bhaktyā dadau tasmai paramānnaṃ sudhopamam .. 4 ..
4.50.d:
मां भोजय महाभागेत्येवं स नृपमुक्तवान् ॥
राजा भक्त्या ददौ तस्मै परमान्नं सुधोपमम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.50.m:
“Feed me, fortunate one!” thus he said to the king.
With devotion, the king gave him divine rice-pudding resembling nectar.

4.50.s:
sakeśaṃ pāyasaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ śaptumudyataḥ ..
jaṭāṃ nikṛtya śirasaḥ sthāpayāmāsa bhūtale .. 5 ..
4.50.d:
सकेशं पायसं दृष्ट्वा राजानं शप्तुमुद्यतः ॥
जटां निकृत्य शिरसः स्थापयामास भूतले ॥ 5 ॥
4.50.m:
Seeing hair in the milk-rice, he was ready to curse the king;
plucking a matted lock from his head, he placed it on the surface of the earth.

4.50.s:
jaṭāmadhyātsamudbhūto jvaladagniśikhopamaḥ ..
saptatālapramāṇaśca puruṣaḥ pralayāṃtakaḥ.. 6 ..
4.50.d:
जटामध्यात्समुद्भूतो ज्वलदग्निशिखोपमः ॥
सप्ततालप्रमाणश्च पुरुषः प्रलयांतकः॥ 6 ॥
4.50.m:
From the midst of the matted lock there arose one resembling a blazing tongue of fire,
a man seven palm trees tall, like the end of dissolution.

4.50.s:
nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ sa rājānaṃ kopena hantumudyataḥ ..
bhayena kampitāḥ sarve śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukāḥ ..7..
4.50.d:
नृपश्रेष्ठं स राजानं कोपेन हन्तुमुद्यतः ॥
भयेन कम्पिताः सर्वे शुष्ककण्ठोष्ठतालुकाः ॥7॥
4.50.m:
In anger, he stepped forward to kill the king, best of monarchs.
All trembled with fear, their throats, lips, and palates dried up.

4.50.s:
sasmāra ca mahābhīto rājā mama padāmbujam ..
sarvavighrasyopaśamaḥ smṛtimātrādbabhūva ha .. 8 ..
4.50.d:
सस्मार च महाभीतो राजा मम पदाम्बुजम् ॥
सर्वविघ्रस्योपशमः स्मृतिमात्राद्बभूव ह ॥ 8 ॥
4.50.m:
Greatly terrified, the king remembered my lotus feet.
By mere remembrance, the pacification of every obstacle indeed came to pass.

4.50.s:
etasminnantare cakraṃ durnivāryaṃ sudarśanam ..
tejasā mama tulyaṃ ca koṭisūryaprabhopamam .. 9 ..
4.50.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चक्रं दुर्निवार्यं सुदर्शनम् ॥
तेजसा मम तुल्यं च कोटिसूर्यप्रभोपमम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.50.m:
At that moment, the irresistible Sudarśana discus,
equal in splendor to me and resembling the radiance of ten million suns,

4.50.s:
āvirbabhūva sahasā sabhāmadhye ca ghūrṇitam ..
nikṛtya kṛtyāpuruṣaṃ dudrāva munipuṅgavam .. 4.50.10 ..
4.50.d:
आविर्बभूव सहसा सभामध्ये च घूर्णितम् ॥
निकृत्य कृत्यापुरुषं दुद्राव मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥ 4.50.10 ॥
4.50.m:
suddenly appeared, spinning in the midst of the assembly.
Having cut down the phantom man, it rushed after the eminent sage.

4.50.s:
saśaila sāgarāṃ pṛthvīṃ kāñcanīṃ bhūmimuttamām ..
bhrāmayitvā mahīṃ sarvāṃ punardudrāva taṃ munim .. 11 ..
4.50.d:
सशैल सागरां पृथ्वीं काञ्चनीं भूमिमुत्तमाम् ॥
भ्रामयित्वा महीं सर्वां पुनर्दुद्राव तं मुनिम् ॥ 11 ॥
4.50.m:
Around the earth with its mountains and oceans, the supreme golden realm,
having chased him around the entire earth, it rushed again after that sage.

4.50.s:
dhāvantaṃ muktakeśaṃ taṃ bhītaṃ kātaramāturam..
tejasā''cchādya sūryaṃ taṃ dīptiṃ kurvantamuttamām ..12..
4.50.d:
धावन्तं मुक्तकेशं तं भीतं कातरमातुरम्॥
तेजसा'ऽच्छाद्य सूर्यं तं दीप्तिं कुर्वन्तमुत्तमाम् ॥12॥
4.50.m:
He ran with disheveled hair, afraid, distressed, and afflicted,
[the discus] obscuring the sun with its brilliance, producing an extraordinary light.

4.50.s:
kailāsaṃ saptavargaṃ ca brahmalokamanāmayam ..
viprendro bhramaṇaṃ kṛtvā vaikuṇṭhaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau .. 13..
4.50.d:
कैलासं सप्तवर्गं च ब्रह्मलोकमनामयम् ॥
विप्रेन्द्रो भ्रमणं कृत्वा वैकुण्ठं शरणं ययौ ॥ 13॥
4.50.m:
Having wandered to Kailāsa, to the seven worlds, and to the disease-free Brahmaloka,
the foremost of the twice-born went to Vaikuṇṭha for refuge.

4.50.s:
pādapadme patantaṃ ca dadarśa viprapuṅgavam ..
kṛpayā ca kṛpāsindhurdadau viprāya nirbhayam .. 14 ..
4.50.d:
पादपद्मे पतन्तं च ददर्श विप्रपुङ्गवम् ॥
कृपया च कृपासिन्धुर्ददौ विप्राय निर्भयम् ॥ 14 ॥
4.50.m:
He saw the foremost of the twice-born falling at his lotus feet;
and out of compassion, the ocean of mercy granted freedom from fear to the twice-born.

4.50.s:
nārāyaṇavareṇaiva babhūva vijvaro dvijaḥ..
punaryayau hariṃ stutvā nṛpagehaṃ tadājñayā..15..
4.50.d:
नारायणवरेणैव बभूव विज्वरो द्विजः॥
पुनर्ययौ हरिं स्तुत्वा नृपगेहं तदाज्ञया॥15॥
4.50.m:
By the very boon of Nārāyaṇa, the twice-born was relieved of fever;
having praised Hari, he went back to the king's house by his command.

4.50.s:
rājā munīndraṃ saṃprāpya bhojayāmāsa pāyasam ..
svayaṃ ca pāraṇaṃ cakre sastrīkaḥ sahabāndhavaḥ..16..
4.50.d:
राजा मुनीन्द्रं संप्राप्य भोजयामास पायसम् ॥
स्वयं च पारणं चक्रे सस्त्रीकः सहबान्धवः॥16॥
4.50.m:
Having welcomed the lord of sages, the king fed him milk-rice,
and broke the fast himself together with his wife and kinsmen.

4.50.s:
rājānamāśiṣaṃ kṛtvā bhuktvā vipro gṛhaṃ yayau ..
mayā niyojitaṃ cakraṃ bhaktānāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca .. 17..
4.50.d:
राजानमाशिषं कृत्वा भुक्त्वा विप्रो गृहं ययौ ॥
मया नियोजितं चक्रं भक्तानां रक्षणाय च ॥ 17॥
4.50.m:
Having blessed the king and eaten, the twice-born went home.
The discus was dispatched by me for the protection of my devotees.

4.50.s:
naśyanti sarve pralaye na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati..
sarve devā mama prāṇā bhaktāḥ prāṇādhikā mama..18..
4.50.d:
नश्यन्ति सर्वे प्रलये न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति॥
सर्वे देवा मम प्राणा भक्ताः प्राणाधिका मम॥18॥
4.50.m:
All perish at the dissolution; my devotee does not perish.
All the gods are my life-breath; my devotees are dearer to me than life.

4.50.s:
tvaṃ ca lakṣmīrmahāmāyā sāvitrī vā sarasvatī..
brahmā śaṃbhuranantaśca dharmaśca brāhmaṇāstathā..19..
4.50.d:
त्वं च लक्ष्मीर्महामाया सावित्री वा सरस्वती॥
ब्रह्मा शंभुरनन्तश्च धर्मश्च ब्राह्मणास्तथा॥19॥
4.50.m:
Both you and Lakṣmī, Mahāmāyā, Sāvitrī, or Sarasvatī,
Brahmā, Śaṃbhu, and Ananta, and Dharma, and the brāhmaṇas likewise,

4.50.s:
gopāṅganāśca gopāśca sarve priyatamā mama..
tebhyaḥ priyāḥ parā bhaktāḥ priyo bhaktānna kaścana ..4.50.20..
4.50.d:
गोपाङ्गनाश्च गोपाश्च सर्वे प्रियतमा मम॥
तेभ्यः प्रियाः परा भक्ताः प्रियो भक्तान्न कश्चन ॥4.50.20॥
4.50.m:
and the cowherd maidens and the cowherds, are all most dear to me;
higher than them are the devotees who are dear; none is dearer than a devotee.

4.50.s:
dattvā sudarśanaṃ cakraṃ bhaktānāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca..
tathāpi na pratītirme svayaṃ draṣṭuṃ prayāmi tān..21..
4.50.d:
दत्त्वा सुदर्शनं चक्रं भक्तानां रक्षणाय च॥
तथापि न प्रतीतिर्मे स्वयं द्रष्टुं प्रयामि तान्॥21॥
4.50.m:
Even having given the Sudarśana discus for the protection of the devotees,
still I have no peace of mind; I go myself to see them.

4.50.s:
durvāsaso darpabhaṅgaḥ śruto mattaḥ sureśvari ..
ājñāpaya mahābhāge kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 22 ..
4.50.d:
दुर्वाससो दर्पभङ्गः श्रुतो मत्तः सुरेश्वरि ॥
आज्ञापय महाभागे किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 22 ॥
4.50.m:
The crushing of the pride of Durvāsas has been heard from me, O ruler of the gods.
Command me, O highly fortunate one, what more do you wish to hear?

4.50.s:
śrīrādhikovāca ..
dhanvantarerdarpabhaṅgaṃ kathayasva jagadguro ..
purāṇe gopanīyaṃ ca śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama .. 23 ..
4.50.d:
श्रीराधिकोवाच ॥
धन्वन्तरेर्दर्पभङ्गं कथयस्व जगद्गुरो ॥
पुराणे गोपनीयं च श्रोतुं कौतूहलं मम ॥ 23 ॥
4.50.m:
Tell of the crushing of Dhanvantari's pride, O teacher of the universe;
it is to be kept secret in the Purāṇa, and I am eager to hear it.

4.50.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
rādhikāvacanaṃ śrutvā jahāsa madhusūdanaḥ ..
kathāṃ kathitumārebhe śrutiramyāṃ purātanīm .. 24 ..
4.50.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
राधिकावचनं श्रुत्वा जहास मधुसूदनः ॥
कथां कथितुमारेभे श्रुतिरम्यां पुरातनीम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.50.m:
Hearing the words of Rādhikā, Madhusūdana laughed,
and began to tell an ancient tale delightful to the ear.

4.51.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
nārāyaṇāṃśo bhagavānsvayaṃ dhanvantarirmahān ..
purā samudramathane samuttasthau mahodadheḥ .. 1..
4.51.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
नारायणांशो भगवान्स्वयं धन्वन्तरिर्महान् ॥
पुरा समुद्रमथने समुत्तस्थौ महोदधेः ॥ 1॥
4.51.m:
The lord himself, the great Dhanvantari, a portion of Nārāyaṇa,
formerly arose from the great ocean at the churning of the ocean.

4.51.s:
sarvavedeṣu niṣṇāto maṃtratantraviśāradaḥ ..
śiṣyo hi vainateyasya śaṅkarasyopaśiṣyakaḥ .. .. 2 ..
4.51.d:
सर्ववेदेषु निष्णातो मंत्रतन्त्रविशारदः ॥
शिष्यो हि वैनतेयस्य शङ्करस्योपशिष्यकः ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
4.51.m:
Skilled in all the Vedas, expert in mantras and tantras,
he was the pupil of Garuḍa and a secondary pupil of Śaṅkara.

4.51.s:
śiṣyāṇāṃ ca sahasreṇa gataḥ kailāsamīśvari ..
dadarśa takṣakaṃ mārge lelihānaṃ bhayānakam .. 3 ..
4.51.d:
शिष्याणां च सहस्रेण गतः कैलासमीश्वरि ॥
ददर्श तक्षकं मार्गे लेलिहानं भयानकम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.51.m:
Accompanied by a thousand disciples, O goddess, he went to Kailāsa;
on the way he saw Takṣaka licking [his fangs], terrifying,

4.51.s:
lakṣanāgaiḥ parivṛtaṃ śūlatulyaṃ viṣolbaṇam ..
bhoktuṃ kopātsamāyāṃtamevaṃ dṛṣṭvā jahāsa ca .. 4 ..
4.51.d:
लक्षनागैः परिवृतं शूलतुल्यं विषोल्बणम् ॥
भोक्तुं कोपात्समायांतमेवं दृष्ट्वा जहास च ॥ 4 ॥
4.51.m:
surrounded by a hundred thousand serpents, sharp as a spear, fierce with venom.
Seeing him approaching in anger to devour them, he laughed.

4.51.s:
dambhī dhanvantareḥ śiṣyo dhṛtvā takṣakamulbaṇam ..
maṃtreṇa jṛṃbhitaṃ kṛtvā nirviṣaṃ taṃ cakāra ha .. 5 ..
4.51.d:
दम्भी धन्वन्तरेः शिष्यो धृत्वा तक्षकमुल्बणम् ॥
मंत्रेण जृंभितं कृत्वा निर्विषं तं चकार ह ॥ 5 ॥
4.51.m:
Seizing the violent Takṣaka, an arrogant disciple of Dhanvantari,
having rendered him gaping with a mantra, indeed made him devoid of poison.

4.51.s:
amūlyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ ca jahāra mastake sthitam ..
kareṇa bhrāmayitvā ca prerayāmāsa dūrataḥ.. .. 6 ..
4.51.d:
अमूल्यं मणिरत्नं च जहार मस्तके स्थितम् ॥
करेण भ्रामयित्वा च प्रेरयामास दूरतः॥ ॥ 6 ॥
4.51.m:
And he took away the priceless jewel located upon his head.
And whirling [him] around with his hand, he hurled [him] far away. // 6

4.51.s:
niśceṣṭastakṣakastasthau tatra mārge yathā mṛtaḥ ..
gaṇā nivedanaṃ cakurgatvā vāsukisannidhim ..7..
4.51.d:
निश्चेष्टस्तक्षकस्तस्थौ तत्र मार्गे यथा मृतः ॥
गणा निवेदनं चकुर्गत्वा वासुकिसन्निधिम् ॥7॥
4.51.m:
Motionless, Takṣaka lay there on the path as if dead.
The attendants went to the presence of Vāsuki and made a report. // 7

4.51.s:
vāsukistatsamākarṇya prajvalannatikopataḥ ..
sarpānprasthāpayāmāsāsaṃkhyāṃścaiva viṣolbaṇān .. 8 ..
4.51.d:
वासुकिस्तत्समाकर्ण्य प्रज्वलन्नतिकोपतः ॥
सर्पान्प्रस्थापयामासासंख्यांश्चैव विषोल्बणान् ॥ 8 ॥
4.51.m:
Hearing that, Vāsuki blazed with violent rage,
and dispatched innumerable serpents potent with poison, // 8

4.51.s:
sarpasenāgraṇīnāṃ ca mukhyānpañca viśāradān ..
droṇakālīyakarkoṭapuṇḍarīkadhanaṃjayān .. 9 ..
4.51.d:
सर्पसेनाग्रणीनां च मुख्यान्पञ्च विशारदान् ॥
द्रोणकालीयकर्कोटपुण्डरीकधनंजयान् ॥ 9 ॥
4.51.m:
as well as the five foremost and skilled commanders of the serpent army:
Droṇa, Kālīya, Karkoṭa, Puṇḍarīka, and Dhanañjaya. // 9

4.51.s:
sarve nāgāḥ samājagmuryatra dhanvantariḥ svayam ..
bhayamāpuḥ śiṣyagaṇā dṛṣṭvā nāgānasaṃkhyakān .. 4.51.10 ..
4.51.d:
सर्वे नागाः समाजग्मुर्यत्र धन्वन्तरिः स्वयम् ॥
भयमापुः शिष्यगणा दृष्ट्वा नागानसंख्यकान् ॥ 4.51.10 ॥
4.51.m:
All the serpents arrived where Dhanvantari himself was.
The groups of disciples became terrified upon seeing the innumerable serpents. // 10

4.51.s:
nāganiśvāsavātena sarve śiṣyā mṛtā iva..
niśceṣṭā jñānarahitāḥ śerate dharaṇītale .. 11 ..
4.51.d:
नागनिश्वासवातेन सर्वे शिष्या मृता इव॥
निश्चेष्टा ज्ञानरहिताः शेरते धरणीतले ॥ 11 ॥
4.51.m:
From the breath-wind of the serpents, all the disciples became as if dead;
motionless and devoid of consciousness, they lay upon the surface of the earth. // 11

4.51.s:
dhanvantariśca bhagavānpīyūṣavarṣaṇena ca ..
jīvayāmāsa śiṣyāṃśca maṃtreṇa ca guruṃ smaran.. 12 ..
4.51.d:
धन्वन्तरिश्च भगवान्पीयूषवर्षणेन च ॥
जीवयामास शिष्यांश्च मंत्रेण च गुरुं स्मरन्॥ 12 ॥
4.51.m:
Then the blessed Dhanvantari, by showering nectar
and through a mantra, remembering his guru, revived the disciples. // 12

4.51.s:
cetanāṃ kārayitvā ca śiṣyāṇāṃ ca jagadguruḥ ..
cakāra jṛṃbhitaṃ mantraiḥ sarpasaṃghaṃ viṣolbaṇam .. 13 ..
4.51.d:
चेतनां कारयित्वा च शिष्याणां च जगद्गुरुः ॥
चकार जृंभितं मन्त्रैः सर्पसंघं विषोल्बणम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.51.m:
Having restored consciousness to his disciples, the teacher of the universe
rendered the host of serpents, potent with poison, stunned with mantras. // 13

4.51.s:
sarve babhūvurniśceṣṭā jṛṃbhitāste mṛtā iva ..
ko'pi nālaṃ tato devi vārtāṃ dātuṃ gaṇeṣu ca .. 14 ..
4.51.d:
सर्वे बभूवुर्निश्चेष्टा जृंभितास्ते मृता इव ॥
कोऽपि नालं ततो देवि वार्तां दातुं गणेषु च ॥ 14 ॥
4.51.m:
All of them became motionless, paralyzed as if dead.
None among them, O goddess, was able to convey the news to the hosts. // 14

4.51.s:
vāsukirbubudhe sarvaṃ sarvajñaḥ sarvasaṃkaṭam ..
ājuhāva jagadgaurīṃ bhaginīṃ jñānarūpiṇīm .. 15 ..
4.51.d:
वासुकिर्बुबुधे सर्वं सर्वज्ञः सर्वसंकटम् ॥
आजुहाव जगद्गौरीं भगिनीं ज्ञानरूपिणीम् ॥ 15 ॥
4.51.m:
The all-knowing Vāsuki comprehended all, the entire calamity.
He summoned his sister, Jagadgaurī, the embodiment of wisdom. // 15

4.51.s:
vāsukiruvāca ..
manase tvaṃ samāgaccha nāgānrakṣātisaṅkaṭāt ..
jagattraye mahābhāge pūjā tava bhaviṣyati.. 16 ..
4.51.d:
वासुकिरुवाच ॥
मनसे त्वं समागच्छ नागान्रक्षातिसङ्कटात् ॥
जगत्त्रये महाभागे पूजा तव भविष्यति॥ 16 ॥
4.51.m:
O Manasā, come and protect the serpents from this grave danger!
In the three worlds, O highly fortunate one, worship shall be yours. // 16

4.51.s:
vāsukervacanaṃ śrutvā prahasyovāca kanyakā ..
vākyapīyūṣatulyaṃ ca vinayāvanatasthitā .. 17 ..
4.51.d:
वासुकेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्योवाच कन्यका ॥
वाक्यपीयूषतुल्यं च विनयावनतस्थिता ॥ 17 ॥
4.51.m:
Hearing Vāsuki's words, the maiden smiled and spoke
words equal to nectar, remaining bowed down with humility. // 17

4.51.s:
manasovāca ..
nāgendra śṛṇu madvākyaṃ yāsyāmi samaraṃ prati ..
bhadrābhadraṃ daivasādhyaṃ kariṣyāmi yathocitam .. 18 ..
4.51.d:
मनसोवाच ॥
नागेन्द्र शृणु मद्वाक्यं यास्यामि समरं प्रति ॥
भद्राभद्रं दैवसाध्यं करिष्यामि यथोचितम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.51.m:
O lord of serpents, listen to my words. I shall go to battle.
Good and bad fortune depend on destiny; I shall do what is fitting. // 18

4.51.s:
taṃ śatruṃ saṃhariṣyāmi līlayā samarasthale ..
ahaṃ yaṃ nihaniṣyāmi taṃ ko rakṣitumīśvaraḥ .. 19 ..
4.51.d:
तं शत्रुं संहरिष्यामि लीलया समरस्थले ॥
अहं यं निहनिष्यामि तं को रक्षितुमीश्वरः ॥ 19 ॥
4.51.m:
I shall destroy that enemy effortlessly on the battlefield.
Whom I will slay, who is capable of protecting him? // 19

4.51.s:
yadi brahmādayo devāḥ samāyānti raṇasthale ..
tathāpi tava śatruṃ ca prajeṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ..4.51.20..
4.51.d:
यदि ब्रह्मादयो देवाः समायान्ति रणस्थले ॥
तथापि तव शत्रुं च प्रजेष्यामि न संशयः॥4.51.20॥
4.51.m:
Even if the gods headed by Brahmā come to the battlefield,
still I will utterly vanquish your enemy, without a doubt. // 20

4.51.s:
gururme bhagavāñcheṣaḥ siddhamantraṃ ca dattavān ..
nārāyaṇasya jagatāmīśasya paramādbhutam .. 21 ..
4.51.d:
गुरुर्मे भगवाञ्छेषः सिद्धमन्त्रं च दत्तवान् ॥
नारायणस्य जगतामीशस्य परमाद्भुतम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.51.m:
My guru, the blessed Śeṣa, gave [me] an effective mantra,
supremely wonderful, of Nārāyaṇa, the lord of the worlds. // 21

4.51.s:
bibharmi kavacaṃ kaṇṭhe paraṃ trailokyamaṅgalam ..
saṃsāraṃ bhasmasātkṛtvā punaḥ sraṣṭumahaṃ kṣamā .. 22..
4.51.d:
बिभर्मि कवचं कण्ठे परं त्रैलोक्यमङ्गलम् ॥
संसारं भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनः स्रष्टुमहं क्षमा ॥ 22॥
4.51.m:
I wear on my neck the supreme armour that brings welfare to the three worlds.
Having reduced the universe to ashes, I am capable of creating it anew. // 22

4.51.s:
śiṣyā'haṃ maṃtraśāstreṣu śaṃbhorbhagavataḥ purā ..
mahājñānaṃ dattavānsa mahyaṃ ca kṛpayā vibhuḥ .. 23 ..
4.51.d:
शिष्याऽहं मंत्रशास्त्रेषु शंभोर्भगवतः पुरा ॥
महाज्ञानं दत्तवान्स मह्यं च कृपया विभुः ॥ 23 ॥
4.51.m:
I was formerly a disciple in the scriptures of mantras under the blessed Śambhu;
with grace that all-pervading lord bestowed supreme knowledge upon me. // 23

4.51.s:
śaṃbhośca śiṣyo garuḍo gaṇayāmi na taṃ dhruvam ..
dhanvaṃtaristacchiṣyāṇāmekaḥ kiṃ gaṇayāmi tam .. 24 ..
4.51.d:
शंभोश्च शिष्यो गरुडो गणयामि न तं ध्रुवम् ॥
धन्वंतरिस्तच्छिष्याणामेकः किं गणयामि तम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.51.m:
