Garuḍa is Śambhu's disciple; I surely count him as nothing.
Dhanvantari is one of his disciples; how should I count him? // 24

4.51.s:
ityuktvā sā jagāmaikā tyaktvā nāgagaṇānruṣā ..
praṇamya śrīhariṃ śaṃbhuṃ śeṣaṃ ca hṛṣṭamānasā .. 25 ..
4.51.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सा जगामैका त्यक्त्वा नागगणान्रुषा ॥
प्रणम्य श्रीहरिं शंभुं शेषं च हृष्टमानसा ॥ 25 ॥
4.51.m:
Having spoken thus, leaving the hosts of serpents in fury, she went alone,
having bowed down to glorious Hari, Śambhu, and Śeṣa with a delighted heart. // 25

4.51.s:
yatra dhanvantarirdevaḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ ..
tatrājagāma sā devī koparaktekṣaṇā ruṣā .. 26..
4.51.d:
यत्र धन्वन्तरिर्देवः प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ॥
तत्राजगाम सा देवी कोपरक्तेक्षणा रुषा ॥ 26॥
4.51.m:
Where the god Dhanvantari stood, with a gracious face and eyes,
there that goddess arrived, with eyes red with fury out of wrath. // 26

4.51.s:
dṛṣṭimātreṇa sarvāśca jīvayāmāsa sundarī ..
viṣadṛṣṭyā śatruśiṣyānniśceṣṭāṃśca cakāra ha .. 27 ..
4.51.d:
दृष्टिमात्रेण सर्वाश्च जीवयामास सुन्दरी ॥
विषदृष्ट्या शत्रुशिष्यान्निश्चेष्टांश्च चकार ह ॥ 27 ॥
4.51.m:
With a mere glance, the beautiful woman revived all [the serpents],
and with a poisonous glance she rendered the enemy's disciples motionless. // 27

4.51.s:
dhanvantaristu bhagavānmantraśāstraviśāradaḥ ..
mantreṇa yatnaṃ kṛtavānnotthāpayitumīśvaraḥ ..28..
4.51.d:
धन्वन्तरिस्तु भगवान्मन्त्रशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
मन्त्रेण यत्नं कृतवान्नोत्थापयितुमीश्वरः ॥28॥
4.51.m:
The blessed Dhanvantari, learned in the scriptures of mantras,
made an effort with mantras, but was not able to revive them. // 28

4.51.s:
dṛṣṭvā dhanvaṃtariṃ devī prahasyovāca satvaram ..
bahūktimarthayuktāṃ ca sāhaṃkārā sureśvari .. 29 ..
4.51.d:
दृष्ट्वा धन्वंतरिं देवी प्रहस्योवाच सत्वरम् ॥
बहूक्तिमर्थयुक्तां च साहंकारा सुरेश्वरि ॥ 29 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing Dhanvantari, the goddess, the queen of the gods, quickly spoke with a laugh
many meaningful words, full of pride: // 29

4.51.s:
manasovāca ..
mantrārthaṃ mantraśilpaṃ ca mantrabhedaṃ mahauṣadham ..
vada jānāsi kiṃ siddha śiṣyo'si garuḍasya ca .. 4.51.30 ..
4.51.d:
मनसोवाच ॥
मन्त्रार्थं मन्त्रशिल्पं च मन्त्रभेदं महौषधम् ॥
वद जानासि किं सिद्ध शिष्योऽसि गरुडस्य च ॥ 4.51.30 ॥
4.51.m:
The meaning of mantras, the craft of mantras, the varieties of mantras, and the great herb—
tell me, do you know them, O accomplished one, as you are a disciple of Garuḍa? // 30

4.51.s:
ahaṃ ca vainateyaśca śiṣyau śaṃbhośca viśrutau ..
sukalpakālaṃ suciramahaṃ dhanvantare śṛṇu .. 31 ..
4.51.d:
अहं च वैनतेयश्च शिष्यौ शंभोश्च विश्रुतौ ॥
सुकल्पकालं सुचिरमहं धन्वन्तरे शृणु ॥ 31 ॥
4.51.m:
Both I and the son of Vinatā are renowned disciples of Śambhu
since an auspicious kalpa long ago; listen, O Dhanvantari! // 31

4.51.s:
ityuktvā sarasaḥ padmaṃ samānīya jagatprasūḥ ..
mantrasaṃvalitaṃ kṛtvā prerayāmāsa kopataḥ .. 32 ..
4.51.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सरसः पद्मं समानीय जगत्प्रसूः ॥
मन्त्रसंवलितं कृत्वा प्रेरयामास कोपतः ॥ 32 ॥
4.51.m:
Having spoken thus, the mother of the universe brought a lotus from the lake,
empowered it with mantras, and hurled it in anger. // 32

4.51.s:
dṛṣṭvā''gataṃ padmapuṣpaṃ jvaladagniśikhopamam ..
(dhanvatariśca niḥśvāsairbhasmasāttaccakāra ha) ..33 ..
4.51.d:
दृष्ट्वा'ऽगतं पद्मपुष्पं ज्वलदग्निशिखोपमम् ॥
(धन्वतरिश्च निःश्वासैर्भस्मसात्तच्चकार ह) ॥33 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing the lotus flower approaching like a blazing flame of fire,
Dhanvantari reduced it to ashes with his breaths. // 33

4.51.s:
tacca dhanvatarirdṛṣṭvā samaṃtrareṇumuṣṭinā ..
cakāra niṣkalaṃ bhasma tāṃ prahasyāvalīlayā .. 34 ..
4.51.d:
तच्च धन्वतरिर्दृष्ट्वा समंत्ररेणुमुष्टिना ॥
चकार निष्कलं भस्म तां प्रहस्यावलीलया ॥ 34 ॥
4.51.m:
And seeing that, Dhanvantari, with a handful of dust empowered by mantras,
smilingly and effortlessly reduced it entirely to ashes. // 34

4.51.s:
devī jagrāha śaktiṃ ca grīṣmasūryasamaprabhām ..
maṃtrasaṃvalitāṃ kṛtvā prerayāmāsa taṃ ripum .. 35 ..
4.51.d:
देवी जग्राह शक्तिं च ग्रीष्मसूर्यसमप्रभाम् ॥
मंत्रसंवलितां कृत्वा प्रेरयामास तं रिपुम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.51.m:
The goddess seized a spear with a brilliance equal to the summer sun,
and having charged it with mantras, she hurled it at that enemy. // 35

4.51.s:
dṛṣṭvā jājvalyamānāṃ tāṃ śaktiṃ dhanvatariḥ svayam ..
viṣṇudattena śūlena sa tu ciccheda līlayā .. 36 ..
4.51.d:
दृष्ट्वा जाज्वल्यमानां तां शक्तिं धन्वतरिः स्वयम् ॥
विष्णुदत्तेन शूलेन स तु चिच्छेद लीलया ॥ 36 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing that blazing spear, Dhanvantari himself
effortlessly cut it down with the trident given by Viṣṇu. // 36

4.51.s:
tāṃ ca śaktiṃ vṛthā dṛṣṭvā prajajvāleśvarī ruṣā ..
jagrāha nāgapāśaṃ ca ghoramavyarthamulbaṇam .. 37 ..
4.51.d:
तां च शक्तिं वृथा दृष्ट्वा प्रजज्वालेश्वरी रुषा ॥
जग्राह नागपाशं च घोरमव्यर्थमुल्बणम् ॥ 37 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing that spear rendered useless, the goddess blazed with rage;
she took up the serpent-noose—dreadful, infallible, and ferocious, // 37

4.51.s:
nāgalakṣasamāyuktaṃ siddhamantreṇa mantritam ..
prerayāmāsa kopena kālāntakasamaprabham ..38..
4.51.d:
नागलक्षसमायुक्तं सिद्धमन्त्रेण मन्त्रितम् ॥
प्रेरयामास कोपेन कालान्तकसमप्रभम् ॥38॥
4.51.m:
joined with a hundred thousand serpents and consecrated with a perfected mantra;
in anger she hurled [it], with a radiance like the Destroyer at the end of time. // 38

4.51.s:
dhanvatarirnāgapāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sasmito mudā ..
sasmāra garuḍaṃ tūrṇamājagāma khageśvaraḥ .. 39 ..
4.51.d:
धन्वतरिर्नागपाशं दृष्ट्वा च सस्मितो मुदा ॥
सस्मार गरुडं तूर्णमाजगाम खगेश्वरः ॥ 39 ॥
4.51.m:
Dhanvantari, having seen the serpent-noose, smiled with joy
and remembered Garuḍa; swiftly the lord of birds arrived. // 39

4.51.s:
sarpāstramāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā garuḍo harivāhanaḥ ..
vidhāya cañcunā śīghraṃ bubhuje kṣudhitaściram .. 4.51.40 ..
4.51.d:
सर्पास्त्रमागतं दृष्ट्वा गरुडो हरिवाहनः ॥
विधाय चञ्चुना शीघ्रं बुभुजे क्षुधितश्चिरम् ॥ 4.51.40 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing the serpent-weapon arrive, Garuḍa, the mount of Hari,
quickly seized it in his beak and devoured it, being long hungry. // 40

4.51.s:
nāgāstraṃ niṣphalaṃ dṛṣṭvā koparaktekṣaṇā bhṛśam ..
jagrāha bhasmamuṣṭiṃ ca śivadattāṃ purā priye .. 41 ..
4.51.d:
नागास्त्रं निष्फलं दृष्ट्वा कोपरक्तेक्षणा भृशम् ॥
जग्राह भस्ममुष्टिं च शिवदत्तां पुरा प्रिये ॥ 41 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing the serpent-weapon rendered fruitless, her eyes reddened with rage,
she seized a handful of ashes given formerly by Śiva, O beloved. // 41

4.51.s:
bhasmamuṣṭiṃ mantrapūtāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca preritāṃ yathā ..
pakṣavātena cikṣepa śiṣyaṃ paścānnidhāya ca .. 42 ..
4.51.d:
भस्ममुष्टिं मन्त्रपूतां दृष्ट्वा च प्रेरितां यथा ॥
पक्षवातेन चिक्षेप शिष्यं पश्चान्निधाय च ॥ 42 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing the handful of ashes purified by mantras hurled as it was,
[Garuḍa] blew it away with the wind of his wings, placing his disciple behind. // 42

4.51.s:
nirastāṃ bhasmamuṣṭiṃ ca dṛṣṭvā devī cukopa ha ..
jagrāha śūlamavyarthaṃ hantuṃ dhanvantariṃ svayam .. 43 ..
4.51.d:
निरस्तां भस्ममुष्टिं च दृष्ट्वा देवी चुकोप ह ॥
जग्राह शूलमव्यर्थं हन्तुं धन्वन्तरिं स्वयम् ॥ 43 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing the handful of ashes dispelled, the goddess was enraged;
she seized the infallible trident to slay Dhanvantari herself— // 43

4.51.s:
śivadattaṃ ca śūlaṃ ca śatasūryasamaprabham ..
avyarthaśūlaṃ lokeṣu pralayāgnisamaprabham .. 44 ..
4.51.d:
शिवदत्तं च शूलं च शतसूर्यसमप्रभम् ॥
अव्यर्थशूलं लोकेषु प्रलयाग्निसमप्रभम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.51.m:
the trident given by Śiva, equal in radiance to a hundred suns,
an infallible trident in all the worlds, radiant like the fire of cosmic dissolution. // 44

4.51.s:
atha brahmā tathā śaṃbhurājagāma raṇājiram ..
dhanvaṃtareśca rakṣārthaṃ śamanārthaṃ khagasya ca ..45..
4.51.d:
अथ ब्रह्मा तथा शंभुराजगाम रणाजिरम् ॥
धन्वंतरेश्च रक्षार्थं शमनार्थं खगस्य च ॥45॥
4.51.m:
Then Brahmā and Śambhu came to the battlefield
in order to protect Dhanvantari and to pacify the bird. // 45

4.51.s:
dṛṣṭvā śaṃbhuṃ jagadgaurī vidhiṃ ca jagatāṃ patim ..
bhaktyā nanāma tāveva niḥśaṅkā śūladhāriṇī .. 46 ..
4.51.d:
दृष्ट्वा शंभुं जगद्गौरी विधिं च जगतां पतिम् ॥
भक्त्या ननाम तावेव निःशङ्का शूलधारिणी ॥ 46 ॥
4.51.m:
Seeing Śambhu and Vidhi, the fair lady of the world and lord of the worlds,
the trident-bearer bowed to them with devotion, fearless. // 46

4.51.s:
dhanvantariśca garuḍaḥ praṇanāma sureśvarau ..
tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā tau ca cakraturāśiṣam .. 47 ..
4.51.d:
धन्वन्तरिश्च गरुडः प्रणनाम सुरेश्वरौ ॥
तुष्टाव परया भक्त्या तौ च चक्रतुराशिषम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.51.m:
Dhanvantari and Garuḍa bowed to the two lords of the gods
and praised them with supreme devotion, and the two gave their blessing. // 47

4.51.s:
uvāca brahmā madhuraṃ hitaṃ dhanvatariṃ mudā ..
pūjārthaṃ manasāyāśca lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. .. 48 ..
4.51.d:
उवाच ब्रह्मा मधुरं हितं धन्वतरिं मुदा ॥
पूजार्थं मनसायाश्च लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥ ॥ 48 ॥
4.51.m:
With joy Brahmā spoke sweet and beneficial words to Dhanvantari,
wishing for the welfare of the worlds, for the sake of the worship of Manasā. // 48

4.51.s:
brahmovāca ..
dhanvaṃtare mahābhāga sarvaśāstraviśārada ..
raṇaṃ te manasā sārddhaṃ na hi sāmyaṃ ca me matam .. 49 ..
4.51.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ॥
धन्वंतरे महाभाग सर्वशास्त्रविशारद ॥
रणं ते मनसा सार्द्धं न हि साम्यं च मे मतम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.51.m:
O Dhanvantari of great fortune, learned in all the treatises!
A battle with Manasā is not appropriate, in my judgment. // 49

4.51.s:
śivadattena śūlena durnivāryeṇa sarvataḥ ..
trailokyaṃ bhasmasātkartuṃ kṣameyaṃ tridaśeśvarī .. 4.51.50 ..
4.51.d:
शिवदत्तेन शूलेन दुर्निवार्येण सर्वतः ॥
त्रैलोक्यं भस्मसात्कर्तुं क्षमेयं त्रिदशेश्वरी ॥ 4.51.50 ॥
4.51.m:
With the trident given by Śiva, entirely irresistible,
this sovereign of the gods is capable of reducing the three worlds to ashes. // 50

4.51.s:
dhyāne kauthumaśākhoktaṃ kṛtvā bhaktyā samāhitaḥ ..
dattvā ṣoḍaśopacāraṃ devyāśca kuru pūjanam .. 51 ..
4.51.d:
ध्याने कौथुमशाखोक्तं कृत्वा भक्त्या समाहितः ॥
दत्त्वा षोडशोपचारं देव्याश्च कुरु पूजनम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.51.m:
Composed in mind, having performed the meditation stated in the Kauthuma branch with devotion,
and offering the sixteen services, perform the worship of the goddess. // 51

4.51.s:
āstikoktena stotreṇa stavanaṃ kartumarhasi ..
parituṣṭā ca manasā varaṃ tubhyaṃ pradāsyati .. 52 ..
4.51.d:
आस्तिकोक्तेन स्तोत्रेण स्तवनं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
परितुष्टा च मनसा वरं तुभ्यं प्रदास्यति ॥ 52 ॥
4.51.m:
You should offer praise with the hymn uttered by Āstīka;
thoroughly pleased, Manasā will grant you a boon. // 52

4.51.s:
brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā cakārānumatiṃ śivaḥ ..
vainateyaśca saṃprītyā bodhayāmāsa yatnataḥ .. 53 ..
4.51.d:
ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा चकारानुमतिं शिवः ॥
वैनतेयश्च संप्रीत्या बोधयामास यत्नतः ॥ 53 ॥
4.51.m:
Hearing the word of Brahmā, Śiva gave his assent,
and the son of Vinatā eagerly instructed him with affection. // 53

4.51.s:
eṣāṃ ca vacanaṃ śrutvā snātvā śuciralaṃkṛtaḥ ..
vidhiṃ purohitaṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ kartuṃ samudyataḥ .. 54 ..
4.51.d:
एषां च वचनं श्रुत्वा स्नात्वा शुचिरलंकृतः ॥
विधिं पुरोहितं कृत्वा पूजां कर्तुं समुद्यतः ॥ 54 ॥
4.51.m:
Hearing their words, bathed, pure, and adorned,
making Vidhi his family priest, he prepared to perform the worship. // 54

4.51.s:
dhanvantariruvāca ..
ihāgaccha jagadgauri gṛhāṇa mama pūjanam..
pūjyā tvaṃ triṣu lokeṣu purā kaśyapakanyake .. 55 ..
4.51.d:
धन्वन्तरिरुवाच ॥
इहागच्छ जगद्गौरि गृहाण मम पूजनम्॥
पूज्या त्वं त्रिषु लोकेषु पुरा कश्यपकन्यके ॥ 55 ॥
4.51.m:
Come here, O fair lady of the world! Accept my worship;
in former times you were worthy of worship in the three worlds, O daughter of Kaśyapa! // 55

4.51.s:
tvayā jitaṃ jagatsarvaṃ devi viṣṇusvarūpayā ..
tena te'straprayogaśca na kṛto raṇabhūmiṣu .. 56 ..
4.51.d:
त्वया जितं जगत्सर्वं देवि विष्णुस्वरूपया ॥
तेन तेऽस्त्रप्रयोगश्च न कृतो रणभूमिषु ॥ 56 ॥
4.51.m:
The entire world has been conquered by you, O goddess, whose true nature is Viṣṇu;
therefore, no employment of weapons was made by you on the battlegrounds. // 56

4.51.s:
ityuktyā saṃyato bhūtvā bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharaḥ ..
gṛhītvā śuklakusumaṃ dhyānaṃ kartuṃ samudyataḥ .. 57 ..
4.51.d:
इत्युक्त्या संयतो भूत्वा भक्तिनम्रात्मकंधरः ॥
गृहीत्वा शुक्लकुसुमं ध्यानं कर्तुं समुद्यतः ॥ 57 ॥
4.51.m:
Having spoken thus, restrained, with his neck bowed in devotion,
taking a white flower, he prepared to perform meditation: // 57

4.51.s:
cārucampakavarṇābhāṃ sarvāṅgasumanoharām ..
īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyāṃ śobhitāṃ sūkṣmavāsasā ..58..
4.51.d:
चारुचम्पकवर्णाभां सर्वाङ्गसुमनोहराम् ॥
ईषद्धास्यप्रसन्नास्यां शोभितां सूक्ष्मवाससा ॥58॥
4.51.m:
‘Her complexion glowing like a lovely campaka flower, captivating in all her limbs,
her face cheerful with a gentle smile, adorned with fine garments, // 58

4.51.s:
sucārukabarīśobhāṃ ratnābharaṇabhūṣitām ..
sarvābhayapradāṃ devīṃ bhaktānugrahakātarām..59..
4.51.d:
सुचारुकबरीशोभां रत्नाभरणभूषिताम् ॥
सर्वाभयप्रदां देवीं भक्तानुग्रहकातराम्॥59॥
4.51.m:
radiant with beautiful braided hair, adorned with jewelled ornaments,
the goddess who grants all fearlessness, eager to bestow grace on her devotees, // 59

4.51.s:
sarvavidyāpradāṃ śāntāṃ sarvavidyāviśāradām ..
nāgendravāhinīṃ devīṃ bhaje nāgeśvarīṃ parām .. 4.51.60 ..
4.51.d:
सर्वविद्याप्रदां शान्तां सर्वविद्याविशारदाम् ॥
नागेन्द्रवाहिनीं देवीं भजे नागेश्वरीं पराम् ॥ 4.51.60 ॥
4.51.m:
the giver of all sciences, peaceful, proficient in all sciences,
riding on the king of serpents—I worship that supreme goddess, sovereign of the serpents.’ // 60

4.51.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ kusumaṃ dattvā nānādravyasamanvitam ..
dattvā ṣoḍaśopacāraṃ pūjayāmāsa tāṃ priye .. 61 ..
4.51.d:
ध्यात्वैवं कुसुमं दत्त्वा नानाद्रव्यसमन्वितम् ॥
दत्त्वा षोडशोपचारं पूजयामास तां प्रिये ॥ 61 ॥
4.51.m:
Having meditated thus and offered a flower, along with various items,
and offering the sixteen services, he worshipped her, O beloved. // 61

4.51.s:
stotraṃ cakāra yatnācca pulakāñcitavigrahaḥ ..
puṭāñjaliyuto bhūtvā bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharaḥ .. 62 ..
4.51.d:
स्तोत्रं चकार यत्नाच्च पुलकाञ्चितविग्रहः ॥
पुटाञ्जलियुतो भूत्वा भक्तिनम्रात्मकंधरः ॥ 62 ॥
4.51.m:
With hair bristling with joy on his body, he composed a hymn of praise with devotion,
folding his hands and bowing his neck in devotion. // 62

4.51.s:
dhanvatariruvāca ..
namaḥ siddhisvarūpāyai siddhidāyai namo namaḥ ..
namaḥ kaśyapakanyāyai varadāyai namo namaḥ .. 63 ..
4.51.d:
धन्वतरिरुवाच ॥
नमः सिद्धिस्वरूपायै सिद्धिदायै नमो नमः ॥
नमः कश्यपकन्यायै वरदायै नमो नमः ॥ 63 ॥
4.51.m:
Homage to her whose essence is perfection, who grants perfection, homage, homage!
Obeisance to the daughter of Kaśyapa, obeisance, obeisance to the giver of boons! // 63

4.51.s:
namaḥ śaṃkarakanyāyai śaṃkarāyai namo namaḥ ..
namaste nāgavāhinyai nāgeśvaryai namo namaḥ .. 64 ..
4.51.d:
नमः शंकरकन्यायै शंकरायै नमो नमः ॥
नमस्ते नागवाहिन्यै नागेश्वर्यै नमो नमः ॥ 64 ॥
4.51.m:
Obeisance to the daughter of Śaṅkara, obeisance, obeisance to Śaṅkarā!
Obeisance to you who ride upon serpents, obeisance, obeisance to the mistress of serpents! // 64

4.51.s:
nama āstīkajanani jananyai jagatāṃ mama ..
namo jagatkāraṇāyai jaratkārustriyai namaḥ .. 69 ..
4.51.d:
नम आस्तीकजननि जनन्यै जगतां मम ॥
नमो जगत्कारणायै जरत्कारुस्त्रियै नमः ॥ 69 ॥
4.51.m:
Obeisance, O mother of Āstīka, O mother of the worlds, [and] my [mother]!
Obeisance to the cause of the world, obeisance to the wife of Jaratkāru! // 69

4.51.s:
namo nāgabhaginyai ca yoginyai ca namo namaḥ ..
namaściraṃ tapasvinyai sukhadāyai namo namaḥ .. 66 ..
4.51.d:
नमो नागभगिन्यै च योगिन्यै च नमो नमः ॥
नमश्चिरं तपस्विन्यै सुखदायै नमो नमः ॥ 66 ॥
4.51.m:
Obeisance to the sister of the serpents, and obeisance, obeisance to the yoginī!
Obeisance to the eternal ascetic, obeisance, obeisance to the giver of happiness! // 66

4.51.s:
namastapasyārūpāyai phaladāyai namo namaḥ ..
suśīlāyai ca sādhvyai ca śāntāyai ca namo namaḥ .. 67 ..
4.51.d:
नमस्तपस्यारूपायै फलदायै नमो नमः ॥
सुशीलायै च साध्व्यै च शान्तायै च नमो नमः ॥ 67 ॥
4.51.m:
Obeisance to the embodiment of austerity, obeisance, obeisance to the giver of fruits!
Obeisance, obeisance to the virtuous, the chaste, and the tranquil! // 67

4.51.s:
ityevamuktvā bhaktyā ca praṇanāma prayatnataḥ ..
tuṣṭā devī varaṃ dattvā satvaraṃ svālayaṃ yayau .. 68 ..
4.51.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भक्त्या च प्रणनाम प्रयत्नतः ॥
तुष्टा देवी वरं दत्त्वा सत्वरं स्वालयं ययौ ॥ 68 ॥
4.51.m:
Having spoken thus with devotion, he diligently bowed down.
Satisfied, the goddess granted a boon and quickly departed for her own abode. // 68

4.51.s:
brahmarudravainateyāḥ samājagmurnijālayam ..
dhanvaṃtariśca bhagavāñjagāma nijamandiram .. 69 ..
4.51.d:
ब्रह्मरुद्रवैनतेयाः समाजग्मुर्निजालयम् ॥
धन्वंतरिश्च भगवाञ्जगाम निजमन्दिरम् ॥ 69 ॥
4.51.m:
Brahmā, Rudra, and the son of Vinatā went back to their own abodes,
and the lord Dhanvantari went to his own palace. // 69

4.51.s:
jagmurnāgāḥ prahṛṣṭāśca phaṇārājivirājitāḥ ..
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ stavarājaṃ mayā tava .. 4.51.70 ..
4.51.d:
जग्मुर्नागाः प्रहृष्टाश्च फणाराजिविराजिताः ॥
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं स्तवराजं मया तव ॥ 4.51.70 ॥
4.51.m:
The serpents, adorned with rows of hoods, departed overjoyed.
Thus has this entire king of hymns been related by me to you. // 4.51.70

4.51.s:
vidhinā mātaraṃ bhaktimāstīkaśca cakāra ha ..
tadā tuṣṭā jagadgaurī putraṃ taṃ munipuṃgavam .. 71 ..
4.51.d:
विधिना मातरं भक्तिमास्तीकश्च चकार ह ॥
तदा तुष्टा जगद्गौरी पुत्रं तं मुनिपुंगवम् ॥ 71 ॥
4.51.m:
Āstīka worshipped [his] mother according to the proper rites;
then Jagadgaurī was pleased with that son, the foremost among sages. // 71

4.51.s:
idaṃ stotraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ bhaktiyuktaśca yaḥ paṭhet ..
vaṃśajānāṃ nāgabhayaṃ nāsti tasya na saṃśayaḥ .. 72 ..
4.51.d:
इदं स्तोत्रं महापुण्यं भक्तियुक्तश्च यः पठेत् ॥
वंशजानां नागभयं नास्ति तस्य न संशयः ॥ 72 ॥
4.51.m: his descendants have no fear of serpents, of this there is no doubt. // 72

4.52.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
sarveṣāṃ darpabhaṅgaśca kathitaśca śrutastvayā ..
kṣudrāṇāṃ mahatāṃ caiva kṛta eva na saṃśayaḥ ..1 ..
4.52.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
सर्वेषां दर्पभङ्गश्च कथितश्च श्रुतस्त्वया ॥
क्षुद्राणां महतां चैव कृत एव न संशयः ॥1 ॥
4.52.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
The breaking of the pride of all has been told and heard by you; / it was indeed done to both the small and the great, there is no doubt. // 1
And now arise, go to the forest of Vṛndāvana; / O beautiful one, let me quickly see the cowherd women afflicted by separation. // 2
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having heard this speech, the proud mistress of delight / said to Kṛṣṇa: 'Carry me, Lord, I am not able to go.' // 3
Hearing Rādhikā's word, Madhusūdana laughed, / and saying 'Climb upon me', he disappeared. // 4
That Rādhā, who moves like thought, wept for a moment, / and having searched for him here and there, she went to the forest of Vṛndā. // 5
Weeping and afflicted with grief, she entered the sandalwood forest; / there she saw the cowherd women stricken with grief and bewildered by fear. // 6
With reddish faces and tearful eyes, wandering through the whole forest, / crying 'O Lord! O Lord!', without food and filled with anger. // 7
Seeing them, Rādhikā, distressed by the separation of love, / told the story of her wandering on Mount Malaya and the rest. // 8
Together with them, Rādhā wept, distressed by separation, / calling out loudly 'O Lord, Lord!', lamenting again and again. // 9
Reproaching Kṛṣṇa with anger, she rebuked him for a moment; / for a moment they were all prepared out of anger to cast off their bodies. // 10
In the meantime, Kṛṣṇa showed himself / to Rādhikā and the company of cowherd women there in the sandalwood forest. // 11
Rādhā and the cowherd maidens, seeing the lord of their lives with joy, / smiled and ran forward, their bodies thrilled with horripilation. // 12
Quickly embracing Kṛṣṇa, in anger she snatched his flute; / and breaking his garland and yellow garment, that proud woman, // 13
Delighting in Vṛndāvana, became pleased and made him wear / the garment, a charming garland, and the delightful flute once more. // 14
She smeared him with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron; / gazing at his face again and again, she kissed him with supreme respect. // 15
For a moment she scolded him, for a moment she offered a hymn of praise; / for a moment she joyfully gave him betel with camphor. // 16
Then all the cowherd maidens wept, overwhelmed by love; / they made full declaration of their sorrow born of separation, // 17
Of abandoning their bodies, their bathing, and the giving up of food, / and of their constant wandering from forest to forest day and night. // 18
For a moment they scolded him, for a moment they gladly offered a hymn of praise; / for a moment they gave him ornaments, and for a moment sandalwood. // 19
Some said: 'Watch and constantly guard this thief of our lives! / This should never be done by him again.' // 20
Some said: 'Quickly place him in the middle, / bound by the rope of love in our hearts!' // 21
Some said: 'There is never any trust in him; / with effort, look, look at this thief of consciousness!' // 22
Some said in anger: 'He is cruel, a killer of men! / He does not speak to me again, O Nārada!' // 23
Whatever forests were solitary and delightful, / the cowherd women wandered through them with Kṛṣṇa playfully. // 24
Thus, putting that eternal Lord in their midst, all the cowherd women / went to another forest where the delightful rāsa-circle was. // 25
Having reached the rāsa, the lord of delight sat on a golden throne, / as the moon shines in the sky at night with the host of stars. // 26
Assuming various forms there with them, Janārdana / once more engaged in delightful sport with those passionate women. // 27
Himself taking Rādhā by the hand, overcome with love, he mounted / the previously described house of love-making built by Viśvakarman. // 28
Fragrant, smeared with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron, / upon a bed of campaka flowers there he slept with her. // 29
Skilled in the science of love, the passionate lover playfully / engaged in various kinds of amorous enjoyment with the passionate woman. // 30
Their love-making there lasted for a very long time, O sage; / devoted to pleasure, their love was charming; there was no cessation at that moment. // 31
Thus they two remained there, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, eager for delight; / and those forms of Kṛṣṇa remained in love-making with the cowherd women. // 32
Nārada said:
The wise pronounce 'Rādhā' first and 'Kṛṣṇa' afterwards. / Tell me the reason for this, to me your devotee, O lover of devotees! // 33
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, I shall explain the three kinds of reasons for this: / Prakṛti is the mother of the universe, and Puruṣa is the father of the universe. // 34
The mother is greater than the father by a hundred times in the three worlds. / 'Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa' and 'Gaurī-Īśa'—thus is the phrase heard in the Veda. // 35
'Kṛṣṇa-Rādhā' or 'Īśa-Gaurī' is never heard in the world. / 'Be gracious, O Rohiṇī-Candra, accept this offering of mine!' // 36

4.52.s:
adhunā ca samuttiṣṭha gaccha vṛndāvanaṃ vanam ..
gopikā virahārtāśca śīghraṃ paśyāmi sundari ..2 ..
4.52.d:
अधुना च समुत्तिष्ठ गच्छ वृन्दावनं वनम् ॥
गोपिका विरहार्ताश्च शीघ्रं पश्यामि सुन्दरि ॥2 ॥

4.52.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā māninī rasikeśvarī ..
uvāca kṛṣṇaṃ naya māṃ na śaktā gaṃtumīśvara .. 3 ..
4.52.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा मानिनी रसिकेश्वरी ॥
उवाच कृष्णं नय मां न शक्ता गंतुमीश्वर ॥ 3 ॥

4.52.s:
rādhikā vacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya madhusūdanaḥ ..
māmāruhetyevamuktvā so'ntardhānaṃ cakāra ha ..4..
4.52.d:
राधिका वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मधुसूदनः ॥
मामारुहेत्येवमुक्त्वा सोऽन्तर्धानं चकार ह ॥4॥

4.52.s:
sā manoyāyinī rādhā kṛtvā ca rodanaṃ kṣaṇam..
itastatastamanveṣya vṛndāraṇyaṃ jagāma sā ..9..
4.52.d:
सा मनोयायिनी राधा कृत्वा च रोदनं क्षणम्॥
इतस्ततस्तमन्वेष्य वृन्दारण्यं जगाम सा ॥9॥

4.52.s:
viveśa candanavanaṃ rudantī śokakātarā ..
dadarśa gopikāstatra śokārtā bhayavihvalāḥ.. ..6..
4.52.d:
विवेश चन्दनवनं रुदन्ती शोककातरा ॥
ददर्श गोपिकास्तत्र शोकार्ता भयविह्वलाः॥ ॥6॥

4.52.s:
tāmrāsyā pūrṇanayanā bhramantī sarvakānanam ..
nātha nātheti kurvantīrnirāhārā ruṣā'nvitāḥ .. 7 ..
4.52.d:
ताम्रास्या पूर्णनयना भ्रमन्ती सर्वकाननम् ॥
नाथ नाथेति कुर्वन्तीर्निराहारा रुषाऽन्विताः ॥ 7 ॥

4.52.s:
tā dṛṣṭvā rādhikā sā ca premavicchedakātarā ..
kathayāmāsa vṛttāntaṃ malayabhramaṇādikam.. 8 ..
4.52.d:
ता दृष्ट्वा राधिका सा च प्रेमविच्छेदकातरा ॥
कथयामास वृत्तान्तं मलयभ्रमणादिकम्॥ 8 ॥

4.52.s:
tābhiḥ sārdhaṃ ca sā rādhā ruroda virahāturā ..
hā nāthanāthetyuccārya vilapya ca muhurmuhuḥ .. 9 ..
4.52.d:
ताभिः सार्धं च सा राधा रुरोद विरहातुरा ॥
हा नाथनाथेत्युच्चार्य विलप्य च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 9 ॥

4.52.s:
vinindya kṛṣṇaṃ kopena tarjayāmāsa ca kṣaṇam ..
kṣaṇaṃ śarīramutsraṣṭuṃ kopātsarvāḥ samudyatāḥ .. .. 4.52.10 ..
4.52.d:
विनिन्द्य कृष्णं कोपेन तर्जयामास च क्षणम् ॥
क्षणं शरीरमुत्स्रष्टुं कोपात्सर्वाः समुद्यताः ॥ ॥ 4.52.10 ॥

4.52.s:
etasminnaṃtare kṛṣṇastatra candanakānane ..
svātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa rādhikāṃ gopikāgaṇam .. 11 ..
4.52.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे कृष्णस्तत्र चन्दनकानने ॥
स्वात्मानं दर्शयामास राधिकां गोपिकागणम् ॥ 11 ॥

4.52.s:
rādhā gopāṅganābhiśca dṛṣṭvā prāṇeśvaraṃ mudā ..
sasmitā ca pradudrāva pulakāñcitavigrahā ..12..
4.52.d:
राधा गोपाङ्गनाभिश्च दृष्ट्वा प्राणेश्वरं मुदा ॥
सस्मिता च प्रदुद्राव पुलकाञ्चितविग्रहा ॥12॥

4.52.s:
tūrṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ samāśliṣya jahāra muralīṃ ruṣā ..
mālāṃ ca pītavasanaṃ bhagnaṃ kṛtvā ca māninī .. 13 ..
4.52.d:
तूर्णं कृष्णं समाश्लिष्य जहार मुरलीं रुषा ॥
मालां च पीतवसनं भग्नं कृत्वा च मानिनी ॥ 13 ॥

4.52.s:
punaḥ saṃdhārayāmāsa vastraṃ mālāṃ manoharām ..
vinodamuralīṃ tuṣṭā vṛndāvanavinodinī .. 14..
4.52.d:
पुनः संधारयामास वस्त्रं मालां मनोहराम् ॥
विनोदमुरलीं तुष्टा वृन्दावनविनोदिनी ॥ 14॥

4.52.s:
candanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumāktaṃ cakāra tam ..
muhurmuhurmukhaṃ vīkṣya cucumba paramādaram ..1 5..
4.52.d:
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीकुङ्कुमाक्तं चकार तम् ॥
मुहुर्मुहुर्मुखं वीक्ष्य चुचुम्ब परमादरम् ॥1 5॥

4.52.s:
kṣaṇaṃ saṃtarjayāmāsa kṣaṇaṃ stotraṃ cakāra ha..
sakarpūraṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tasmai mudā dadau .. 16 ..
4.52.d:
क्षणं संतर्जयामास क्षणं स्तोत्रं चकार ह॥
सकर्पूरं च ताम्बूलं क्षणं तस्मै मुदा ददौ ॥ 16 ॥

4.52.s:
atha gopāṅganāḥ sarvā ruruduḥ premavihvalāḥ ..
sarvaṃ nivedanaṃ cakruḥ svaduḥkhaṃ virahodbhavam ..17..
4.52.d:
अथ गोपाङ्गनाः सर्वा रुरुदुः प्रेमविह्वलाः ॥
सर्वं निवेदनं चक्रुः स्वदुःखं विरहोद्भवम् ॥17॥

4.52.s:
dehatyāgaṃ ca snānaṃ ca svāhārasya visarjanam ..
vanevane'harniśaṃ ca śaśvadbhramaṇameva ca..18..
4.52.d:
देहत्यागं च स्नानं च स्वाहारस्य विसर्जनम् ॥
वनेवनेऽहर्निशं च शश्वद्भ्रमणमेव च॥18॥

4.52.s:
kṣaṇaṃ taṃ bhartsayāmāsuḥ stotraṃ cakruḥ kṣaṇaṃ mudā..
kṣaṇaṃ dadurbhūṣaṇaṃ ca kṣaṇaṃ tasmai ca candanam ..19..
4.52.d:
क्षणं तं भर्त्सयामासुः स्तोत्रं चक्रुः क्षणं मुदा॥
क्षणं ददुर्भूषणं च क्षणं तस्मै च चन्दनम् ॥19॥

4.52.s:
kāścidūcuḥ prāṇacoraṃ paśya rakṣeti saṃtatam ..
evaṃ punarna karttavya maneneti ca kāścana .. 4.52.20 ..
4.52.d:
काश्चिदूचुः प्राणचोरं पश्य रक्षेति संततम् ॥
एवं पुनर्न कर्त्तव्य मनेनेति च काश्चन ॥ 4.52.20 ॥

4.52.s:
kāścidūcurimaṃ madhye yūyaṃ kuruta satvaram ..
nibaddhaṃ premapāśena hṛdaye ceti kāścana .. 21 ..
4.52.d:
काश्चिदूचुरिमं मध्ये यूयं कुरुत सत्वरम् ॥
निबद्धं प्रेमपाशेन हृदये चेति काश्चन ॥ 21 ॥

4.52.s:
kāścidūcurayaṃ nāsti pratītirna kadācana..
yatnāccetanacoraṃ ca paśya paśyeti kāścana ..22..
4.52.d:
काश्चिदूचुरयं नास्ति प्रतीतिर्न कदाचन॥
यत्नाच्चेतनचोरं च पश्य पश्येति काश्चन ॥22॥

4.52.s:
kāścidūcurniṣṭhuro'yaṃ naraghātīti kopataḥ..
na punarvadate māṃ ca kāścaneti ca nārada ..23..
4.52.d:
काश्चिदूचुर्निष्ठुरोऽयं नरघातीति कोपतः॥
न पुनर्वदते मां च काश्चनेति च नारद ॥23॥

4.52.s:
nirjanāni ca ramyāṇi yāni yāni vanāni ca ..
bhrameyurgopikāstāni kṛṣṇena saha kautukāt .. 24 ..
4.52.d:
निर्जनानि च रम्याणि यानि यानि वनानि च ॥
भ्रमेयुर्गोपिकास्तानि कृष्णेन सह कौतुकात् ॥ 24 ॥

4.52.s:
evaṃ taṃ gopikāḥ sarvā madhye kṛtvā sadīśvaram ..
yayurvanāntare yatra suramyaṃ rāsamaṇḍalam..29..
4.52.d:
एवं तं गोपिकाः सर्वा मध्ये कृत्वा सदीश्वरम् ॥
ययुर्वनान्तरे यत्र सुरम्यं रासमण्डलम्॥29॥

4.52.s:
rāsaṃ gatvā svarṇapīṭhe tasthau sa rasikeśvaraḥ ..
niśi bhāti yathā''kāśe candrastārāgaṇaiḥ saha ..26..
4.52.d:
रासं गत्वा स्वर्णपीठे तस्थौ स रसिकेश्वरः ॥
निशि भाति यथा'ऽकाशे चन्द्रस्तारागणैः सह ॥26॥

4.52.s:
nānāmūrtīrvidhāyātra saha tābhirjanārdanaḥ ..
cakāra ca punaḥ krīḍāṃ kāmukīnāṃ manoharām .. 27 ..
4.52.d:
नानामूर्तीर्विधायात्र सह ताभिर्जनार्दनः ॥
चकार च पुनः क्रीडां कामुकीनां मनोहराम् ॥ 27 ॥

4.52.s:
svayaṃ rādhāṃ kare dhṛtvā pūrvoktaṃ ratimandiram ..
viśvakarmavinirmāṇamāruroha smarāturaḥ..28..
4.52.d:
स्वयं राधां करे धृत्वा पूर्वोक्तं रतिमन्दिरम् ॥
विश्वकर्मविनिर्माणमारुरोह स्मरातुरः॥28॥

4.52.s:
candanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumāktaṃ suvāsitam ..
tatra campakatalpe sa suṣvāpa ca tayā saha .. 29 ..
4.52.d:
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीकुङ्कुमाक्तं सुवासितम् ॥
तत्र चम्पकतल्पे स सुष्वाप च तया सह ॥ 29 ॥

4.52.s:
nānāprakāraśṛṅgāraṃ kāmaśāstraviśāradaḥ ..
cakāra kāmī krīḍāṃ ca kāminyā saha kautukī ..4.52.30..
4.52.d:
नानाप्रकारशृङ्गारं कामशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
चकार कामी क्रीडां च कामिन्या सह कौतुकी ॥4.52.30॥

4.52.s:
babhūva suratistatra suciraṃ ca tayormune ..
ratiniṣṭhā tayo ramyā viratirnāsti tatkṣaṇam .. 31 ..
4.52.d:
बभूव सुरतिस्तत्र सुचिरं च तयोर्मुने ॥
रतिनिष्ठा तयो रम्या विरतिर्नास्ति तत्क्षणम् ॥ 31 ॥

4.52.s:
evaṃ tau tasthatustatra rādhākṛṣṇau rasotsukau ..
tasthustā gopikābhiśca suratau kṛṣṇamūrtayaḥ .. 32 ..
4.52.d:
एवं तौ तस्थतुस्तत्र राधाकृष्णौ रसोत्सुकौ ॥
तस्थुस्ता गोपिकाभिश्च सुरतौ कृष्णमूर्तयः ॥ 32 ॥

4.52.s:
nārada uvāca ..
ādau rādhāṃ samuccārya paścātkṛṣṇaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
nimittamasya māṃ bhaktaṃ vada bhaktajanapriya ..33 ..
4.52.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
आदौ राधां समुच्चार्य पश्चात्कृष्णं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
निमित्तमस्य मां भक्तं वद भक्तजनप्रिय ॥33 ॥

4.52.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
nimittamasya trividhaṃ kathayāmi niśāmaya ..
jaganmātā ca prakṛtiḥ puruṣaśca jagatpitā .. 34 ..
4.52.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
निमित्तमस्य त्रिविधं कथयामि निशामय ॥
जगन्माता च प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्च जगत्पिता ॥ 34 ॥

4.52.s:
garīyasī trijagatāṃ mātā śataguṇaiḥ pituḥ ..
rādhākṛṣṇeti gaurīśetyevaṃ śabdaḥ śrutau śrutaḥ .. 35 ..
4.52.d:
गरीयसी त्रिजगतां माता शतगुणैः पितुः ॥
राधाकृष्णेति गौरीशेत्येवं शब्दः श्रुतौ श्रुतः ॥ 35 ॥

4.52.s:
kṛṣṇarādheśagaurīti loke na ca kadā śrutaḥ ..
prasīda rohiṇīcandra gṛhāṇārghyamidaṃ mama .. 36 .
4.52.d:
कृष्णराधेशगौरीति लोके न च कदा श्रुतः ॥
प्रसीद रोहिणीचन्द्र गृहाणार्घ्यमिदं मम ॥ 36 ।

4.52.s:
gṛhāṇārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ saṃjñayā saha bhāskara ..
prasīda kamalākānta gṛhāṇa mama pūjanam .. 37 ..
4.52.d:
गृहाणार्घ्यं मया दत्तं संज्ञया सह भास्कर ॥
प्रसीद कमलाकान्त गृहाण मम पूजनम् ॥ 37 ॥
4.52.m:
'Accept the offering given by me together with Saṃjñā, O Bhāskara! / Be gracious, O Kamalākānta, accept my worship!' // 37
Thus is it seen in the Kauthuma recension of the Sāmaveda, O best of sages. / Merely by pronouncing the syllable 'rā', Mādhava becomes thrilled; // 38
And by pronouncing the syllable 'dhā', he eagerly runs after. / If one should utter Puruṣa first and Prakṛti afterwards, // 39
He would become a matricide, O sage, by transgressing the Veda. / In the three worlds, Bhārata is blessed, the realm of action yielding merit. // 40
Even more meritorious than that is Vṛndāvana, by the dust of Rādhā's lotus feet; / for sixty thousand years ascetic penance was performed by Brahmā / to obtain the dust of Rādhikā's lotus feet. // 41
Thus in the Śrī Brahmavaivarta Mahāpurāṇa, in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa, in the dialogue between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada, ends the fifty-second chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Rāsa of Rādhā and Mādhava'. // 52

4.52.s:
iti dṛṣṭaṃ sāmavede kauthume munisattama ..
rāśabdoccāraṇādeva sphīto bhavati mādhavaḥ .. 38 ..
4.52.d:
इति दृष्टं सामवेदे कौथुमे मुनिसत्तम ॥
राशब्दोच्चारणादेव स्फीतो भवति माधवः ॥ 38 ॥

4.52.s:
dhāśabdoccārataḥ paścāddhāvatyeva sasaṃbhramaḥ ..
ādau puruṣamuccārya paścātprakṛtimuccaret .. 39 ..
4.52.d:
धाशब्दोच्चारतः पश्चाद्धावत्येव ससंभ्रमः ॥
आदौ पुरुषमुच्चार्य पश्चात्प्रकृतिमुच्चरेत् ॥ 39 ॥

4.52.s:
sa bhavenmātṛghātī ca vedātikramaṇe mune ..
trailokye bhārataṃ dhanyaṃ karmakṣetraṃ ca puṇyadam .. 4.52.40 ..
4.52.d:
स भवेन्मातृघाती च वेदातिक्रमणे मुने ॥
त्रैलोक्ये भारतं धन्यं कर्मक्षेत्रं च पुण्यदम् ॥ 4.52.40 ॥

4.52.s:
tato vṛndāvanaṃ puṇyaṃ rādhāpādābjareṇunā ..
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptaṃ ca vedhasā ..
rādhikā caraṇāmbhojapādareṇūpalabdhaye .. 41 ..
4.52.d:
ततो वृन्दावनं पुण्यं राधापादाब्जरेणुना ॥
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्तं च वेधसा ॥
राधिका चरणाम्भोजपादरेणूपलब्धये ॥ 41 ॥

4.53.s:
.. nārada uvāca ..
samatīte pūrṇarāse kiṃ cakāra jagatpatiḥ ..
rahasyaṃ kiṃ babhūvātha tadbhavānvaktumarhati .. 1 ..
4.53.d:
॥ नारद उवाच ॥
समतीते पूर्णरासे किं चकार जगत्पतिः ॥
रहस्यं किं बभूवाथ तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥ 1 ॥
4.53.m:
When the full rāsa was over, what did the Lord of the universe do?
What secret happened then? You ought to tell that. // 1

4.53.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
rāsaṃ nivartya rāse ca rāseśvaryā samanvitaḥ ..
svayaṃ rāseśvarastasmādyamunāpulinaṃ yayau .. 2 ..
4.53.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
रासं निवर्त्य रासे च रासेश्वर्या समन्वितः ॥
स्वयं रासेश्वरस्तस्माद्यमुनापुलिनं ययौ ॥ 2 ॥
4.53.m:
Having concluded the rāsa-dance in the circle of the dance, accompanied by the mistress of the rāsa,
the Lord of the rāsa himself went from there to the sandbank of the Yamunā. / 2

4.53.s:
tatra snātvā jalaṃ pītvā nirmalaṃ nirmale jale ..
sārddhaṃ gopāṅganābhiśca jalakrīḍāṃ cakāra saḥ .. 3 ..
4.53.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा जलं पीत्वा निर्मलं निर्मले जले ॥
सार्द्धं गोपाङ्गनाभिश्च जलक्रीडां चकार सः ॥ 3 ॥
4.53.m:
Having bathed there and drunk the pure water in the pure stream,
he engaged in water-sports together with the cowherd women. / 3

4.53.s:
tato jagāma bhagavānbhāṇḍīraṃ rādhayā saha ..
gopāṅganāśca svagṛhānprayayurvirahāturāḥ .. 4 ..
4.53.d:
ततो जगाम भगवान्भाण्डीरं राधया सह ॥
गोपाङ्गनाश्च स्वगृहान्प्रययुर्विरहातुराः ॥ 4 ॥
4.53.m:
Then the Blessed Lord went to Bhāṇḍīra with Rādhā,
and the cowherd women departed for their own homes, distressed by separation. / 4

4.53.s:
krīḍāṃ cakāra rahasi bhāṇḍīre mālatīvane ..
mālatīpuṣpaśayyāyāṃ ramyāyāṃ ramaṇotsukaḥ .. 5 ..
4.53.d:
क्रीडां चकार रहसि भाण्डीरे मालतीवने ॥
मालतीपुष्पशय्यायां रम्यायां रमणोत्सुकः ॥ 5 ॥
4.53.m:
In secret he made sport in Bhāṇḍīra, in a grove of mālatī flowers,
eager for lovemaking upon a charming couch of mālatī blossoms. / 5

4.53.s:
kṛtvā krīḍāṃ ca tatraiva vāsantīkānanaṃ yayau ..
reme tatraiva rāseśo vasante sumanohare .. 6 ..
4.53.d:
कृत्वा क्रीडां च तत्रैव वासन्तीकाननं ययौ ॥
रेमे तत्रैव रासेशो वसन्ते सुमनोहरे ॥ 6 ॥
4.53.m:
Having sported right there, he went to a forest of vāsantī blossoms;
in that very place the Lord of the rāsa took delight during the utterly charming spring. / 6

4.53.s:
tatraiva ramaṇaṃ kṛtvā yayau candanakānanam ..
candanokṣitasarvāṃgo gṛhītvā candanokṣitam.. 17 ..
4.53.d:
तत्रैव रमणं कृत्वा ययौ चन्दनकाननम् ॥
चन्दनोक्षितसर्वांगो गृहीत्वा चन्दनोक्षितम्॥ 17 ॥
4.53.m:
Having made love right there, he went to a sandalwood grove;
his every limb sprinkled with sandalwood, taking her who was sprinkled with sandalwood, / 17 [7]

4.53.s:
ramye candanatalpe ca snigdhe candanapallave ..
pūrṇacandre samudite vijahāra tayā saha .. 8 ..
4.53.d:
रम्ये चन्दनतल्पे च स्निग्धे चन्दनपल्लवे ॥
पूर्णचन्द्रे समुदिते विजहार तया सह ॥ 8 ॥
4.53.m:
upon a delightful couch of sandalwood and smooth sandalwood shoots,
when the full moon had risen, he sported with her. / 8

4.53.s:
kṛtvā vihāraṃ tatraiva yayau campakakānanam ..
ramye campakatalpe ca cakāra ratimīśvarī.. 9 ..
4.53.d:
कृत्वा विहारं तत्रैव ययौ चम्पककाननम् ॥
रम्ये चम्पकतल्पे च चकार रतिमीश्वरी॥ 9 ॥
4.53.m:
Having sported right there, he went to a campaka forest;
and upon a charming couch of campaka flowers the sovereign goddess made love. / 9

4.53.s:
ratiṃ nirvartya tatraiva yayau padmavanaṃ prabhuḥ ..
padmapatrasamākīrṇe talpe'tisumanohare .. 4.53.10..
4.53.d:
रतिं निर्वर्त्य तत्रैव ययौ पद्मवनं प्रभुः ॥
पद्मपत्रसमाकीर्णे तल्पेऽतिसुमनोहरे ॥ 4.53.10॥
4.53.m:
Having finished lovemaking right there, the Lord went to a lotus forest;
upon a most delightful couch covered with lotus petals, / 4.53.10

4.53.s:
sārdhaṃ tatra padmamukhyā śītena padmavāyunā..
cakāra sukhasaṃbhogaṃ yayau nidrāṃ tayā saha .. 11 ..
4.53.d:
सार्धं तत्र पद्ममुख्या शीतेन पद्मवायुना॥
चकार सुखसंभोगं ययौ निद्रां तया सह ॥ 11 ॥
4.53.m:
there together with the lotus-faced woman, in the cool breeze from the lotuses,
he enjoyed pleasurable union and went to sleep with her. / 11

4.53.s:
vihāya nidrāṃ nidreśo dadarśa nidritāṃ priyām ..
śayānāṃ padmatalpe ca sukhasaṃbhogamātrataḥ .. 12 ..
4.53.d:
विहाय निद्रां निद्रेशो ददर्श निद्रितां प्रियाम् ॥
शयानां पद्मतल्पे च सुखसंभोगमात्रतः ॥ 12 ॥
4.53.m:
Shaking off sleep, the Lord of sleep beheld his sleeping beloved,
lying upon the couch of lotuses simply from the pleasurable union. / 12

4.53.s:
dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ ca gharmāktaṃ śaraccandraviniṃditam ..
atisaṃluptasindūraṃ luptaṃ kajjalamulbaṇam .. 13 ..
4.53.d:
दृष्ट्वा मुखं च घर्माक्तं शरच्चन्द्रविनिंदितम् ॥
अतिसंलुप्तसिन्दूरं लुप्तं कज्जलमुल्बणम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.53.m:
Seeing her face bathed in perspiration, putting the autumn moon to shame,
its vermilion mark almost entirely wiped away, its thick collyrium rubbed off, / 13

4.53.s:
saṃluptādhararāgaṃ ca saṃluptagaṇḍapatrakam ..
visrastakabarībhāraṃ netrotpalavimudritam .. 14 ..
4.53.d:
संलुप्ताधररागं च संलुप्तगण्डपत्रकम् ॥
विस्रस्तकबरीभारं नेत्रोत्पलविमुद्रितम् ॥ 14 ॥
4.53.m:
the color on her lower lip rubbed away, the leaf-patterns on her cheeks erased,
the mass of her braid loosened, her lotus eyes closed, / 14

4.53.s:
ratnakuṇḍalayugmenāmūlyena pariśobhitam ..
rājitaṃ mauktikenaiva gajarājodbhavena ca .. 15 ..
4.53.d:
रत्नकुण्डलयुग्मेनामूल्येन परिशोभितम् ॥
राजितं मौक्तिकेनैव गजराजोद्भवेन च ॥ 15 ॥
4.53.m:
adorned with a pair of priceless jewelled earrings,
and illuminated by pearls produced from the king of elephants, / 15

4.53.s:
premṇā svasūkṣmavastreṇa vahniśuddhena mādhavaḥ ..
cakāra mārjanaṃ bhaktyā tadvaktraṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ .. 16 ..
4.53.d:
प्रेम्णा स्वसूक्ष्मवस्त्रेण वह्निशुद्धेन माधवः ॥
चकार मार्जनं भक्त्या तद्वक्त्रं भक्तवत्सलः ॥ 16 ॥
4.53.m:
Mādhava, affectionately, with his own fine cloth cleansed by fire,
loving to devotees, wiped her face with tender care. / 16

4.53.s:
keśasaṃmārjanaṃ kṛtvā nirmāya kabarīṃ hariḥ ..
mādhavīmālatīmālājālena pariśobhitām .. 17 ..
4.53.d:
केशसंमार्जनं कृत्वा निर्माय कबरीं हरिः ॥
माधवीमालतीमालाजालेन परिशोभिताम् ॥ 17 ॥
4.53.m:
Combing her hair and fashioning her braid, Hari
adorned it with a network of garlands of mādhavī and mālatī flowers. / 17

4.53.s:
ratnapaṭṭasūtrabaddhāṃ vāmavaktrāṃ manoharām ..
atīva vartulākārāṃ kundapuṣpasuśobhitām .. 18 ..
4.53.d:
रत्नपट्टसूत्रबद्धां वामवक्त्रां मनोहराम् ॥
अतीव वर्तुलाकारां कुन्दपुष्पसुशोभिताम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.53.m:
Tied with a silken cord set with gems, curved gracefully, enchanting,
exceedingly round in shape, and embellished with kunda flowers, / 18

4.53.s:
dadau sindūratilakamadhaścandanamujjvalam ..
kastūrībindunā sārddhaṃ paritaḥ pariśobhitām .. 19 ..
4.53.d:
ददौ सिन्दूरतिलकमधश्चन्दनमुज्ज्वलम् ॥
कस्तूरीबिन्दुना सार्द्धं परितः परिशोभिताम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.53.m:
he applied a vermilion forehead-mark, and below it bright sandalwood,
beautified all around with a dot of musk. / 19

4.53.s:
cakāra patrakaṃ gaṇḍayugme citravicitritam ..
pradadau kajjalaṃ bhaktyā netrotpalasamujjvalam .. .. 4.53.20 ..
4.53.d:
चकार पत्रकं गण्डयुग्मे चित्रविचित्रितम् ॥
प्रददौ कज्जलं भक्त्या नेत्रोत्पलसमुज्ज्वलम् ॥ ॥ 4.53.20 ॥
4.53.m:
He drew ornamental leaf-patterns on both cheeks in varied designs,
and applied collyrium with devotion, bright as lotus flowers, to her eyes. / 4.53.20

4.53.s:
cakārādhararāgaṃ ca rādhāyāścānurāgataḥ ..
karṇabhūṣaṇayugmaṃ ca cakārātīva nirmalam .. 21 ..
4.53.d:
चकाराधररागं च राधायाश्चानुरागतः ॥
कर्णभूषणयुग्मं च चकारातीव निर्मलम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.53.m:
Out of passionate affection he applied color to Rādhā's lower lip,
and made the pair of ear-ornaments exceedingly spotless. / 21

4.53.s:
amūlyaratnahāraṃ ca stanabhāra yugojjvalam ..
dadau kaṇṭhe ca vaikuṇṭho maṇirājivirājitam .. 22 ..
4.53.d:
अमूल्यरत्नहारं च स्तनभार युगोज्ज्वलम् ॥
ददौ कण्ठे च वैकुण्ठो मणिराजिविराजितम् ॥ 22 ॥
4.53.m:
A priceless necklace of jewels illuminating the pair of heavy breasts,
shining with an array of gems, Vaikuṇṭha placed upon her neck. / 22

4.53.s:
vahniśuddhāṃśukaṃ divyamamūlyaṃ viśvaratnataḥ ..
vāsayāmāsa vasanaṃ kastūrīkuṅkumāktakam .. 23 ..
4.53.d:
वह्निशुद्धांशुकं दिव्यममूल्यं विश्वरत्नतः ॥
वासयामास वसनं कस्तूरीकुङ्कुमाक्तकम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.53.m:
A divine garment cleansed by fire, priceless beyond all the gems in the universe,
scented with musk and saffron, he dressed her in as clothing. / 23

4.53.s:
pradadau pādayugale ratnamañjīrarañjitam ..
cakārālaktakaṃ bhaktyā pāduṅgulinakheṣu ca ..24..
4.53.d:
प्रददौ पादयुगले रत्नमञ्जीररञ्जितम् ॥
चकारालक्तकं भक्त्या पादुङ्गुलिनखेषु च ॥24॥
4.53.m:
On both feet he placed [anklets], brightened with jewelled anklets,
and devotedly applied red lac dye to the nails of her toes. / 24

4.53.s:
cakāra sevāṃ sevyāyāḥ sevyastrijagatāṃ satām ..
aho sevakasaṃbhaktyā śvetena cāmareṇa ca .. 25 ..
4.53.d:
चकार सेवां सेव्यायाः सेव्यस्त्रिजगतां सताम् ॥
अहो सेवकसंभक्त्या श्वेतेन चामरेण च ॥ 25 ॥
4.53.m:
He who is worthy of worship by the virtuous in the three worlds rendered service to her who is worthy of worship,
ah, with the deep devotion of a servant, and with a white fly-whisk! / 25

4.53.s:
sarvabhāvavidāṃ śreṣṭho bodhajñaḥ kāmaśāstravit ..
kāminīṃ bodhayāmāsa vāsayāmāsa vakṣasi .. 26 ..
4.53.d:
सर्वभावविदां श्रेष्ठो बोधज्ञः कामशास्त्रवित् ॥
कामिनीं बोधयामास वासयामास वक्षसि ॥ 26 ॥
4.53.m:
Best among knowers of every emotional state, wise, versed in the science of love,
he awakened the loving woman and seated her upon his chest. / 26

4.53.s:
premṇā ca pradadau tasyai sadratnadarpaṇaṃ śubham ..
suveṣadarśanārthaṃ ca mukhacandraṃ ca mārjitum .. 27..
4.53.d:
प्रेम्णा च प्रददौ तस्यै सद्रत्नदर्पणं शुभम् ॥
सुवेषदर्शनार्थं च मुखचन्द्रं च मार्जितुम् ॥ 27॥
4.53.m:
And with love he handed her an auspicious mirror made of fine jewels,
so she might see her fine attire and admire the moon of her face. / 27

4.53.s:
nānāpuṣpairviracitāmamlānāṃ candanokṣitām ..
gaṇḍe saubhāgyayuktāyāḥ saubhāgyena dadau hariḥ .. 28 ..
4.53.d:
नानापुष्पैर्विरचितामम्लानां चन्दनोक्षिताम् ॥
गण्डे सौभाग्ययुक्तायाः सौभाग्येन ददौ हरिः ॥ 28 ॥
4.53.m:
Fashioned with various flowers, unfading, sprinkled with sandalwood,
Hari graciously placed [a garland] on the neck of the fortunate woman. / 28

4.53.s:
kastūrīkuṅkamāktaṃ ca sugandhicandanaṃ tataḥ ..
dadau priyāyāḥ sarvāṅge priyaḥ premabhareṇa ca .. 29 ..
4.53.d:
कस्तूरीकुङ्कमाक्तं च सुगन्धिचन्दनं ततः ॥
ददौ प्रियायाः सर्वाङ्गे प्रियः प्रेमभरेण च ॥ 29 ॥
4.53.m:
Then fragrant sandalwood mixed with musk and saffron
the beloved [Lord] applied all over the body of his beloved with abundant love. / 29

4.53.s:
pārijātasya kusumaṃ dattaṃ rahasi brahmaṇā ..
pradadau tatkabaryāṃ ca lalitāyāṃ ca nārada .. 4.53.30 ..
4.53.d:
पारिजातस्य कुसुमं दत्तं रहसि ब्रह्मणा ॥
प्रददौ तत्कबर्यां च ललितायां च नारद ॥ 4.53.30 ॥
4.53.m:
A blossom of the pārijāta tree, given in secret by Brahmā,
he placed into her charming braid, O Nārada. / 4.53.30

4.53.s:
kamalaṃ nirmalaṃ divyaṃ sahasradalamujjvalam ..
śivena dattaṃ rahasi dadau taddakṣiṇe kare .. 31 ..
4.53.d:
कमलं निर्मलं दिव्यं सहस्रदलमुज्ज्वलम् ॥
शिवेन दत्तं रहसि ददौ तद्दक्षिणे करे ॥ 31 ॥
4.53.m:
A spotless, divine lotus, shining with a thousand petals,
given in secret by Śiva, he placed in her right hand. / 31

4.53.s:
atisāraṃ maṇīndrāṇāṃ maṇiratnaṃ ca kaustubham ..
dattaṃ rahasi dharmeṇa tasyai suprītaye dadau .. 32..
4.53.d:
अतिसारं मणीन्द्राणां मणिरत्नं च कौस्तुभम् ॥
दत्तं रहसि धर्मेण तस्यै सुप्रीतये ददौ ॥ 32॥
4.53.m:
And the Kaustubha jewel, the most excellent of precious gems
Given in secret by Dharma, he gave to her for her great delight. // 32

4.53.s:
āsavaṃ ratnapātrasthaṃ dasradattaṃ ca nirjane ..
pānārthaṃ pradadau tasyai kāmonmādakaraṃ param..33..
4.53.d:
आसवं रत्नपात्रस्थं दस्रदत्तं च निर्जने ॥
पानार्थं प्रददौ तस्यै कामोन्मादकरं परम्॥33॥
4.53.m:
And wine placed in a jewelled vessel, given in solitude by Dasra,
Utterly intoxicating with passion, he gave her to drink. // 33

4.53.s:
mālatīmādhavīkundamandāracampakādikam..
puṣpaṃ sadratnapātrasthaṃ tasyai suprītaye dadau .. 34 ..
4.53.d:
मालतीमाधवीकुन्दमन्दारचम्पकादिकम्॥
पुष्पं सद्रत्नपात्रस्थं तस्यै सुप्रीतये ददौ ॥ 34 ॥
4.53.m:
Flowers such as mālatī, mādhavī, kunda, mandāra, and campaka,
Set in a fine jewelled vessel, he gave to her for her great delight. // 34

4.53.s:
sudurlabhaṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ karpūrādisusaṃskṛtam ..
bhakṣaṇaṃ kārayāmāsa samayajñaśca tāṃ priyām .. 35 ..
4.53.d:
सुदुर्लभं च ताम्बूलं कर्पूरादिसुसंस्कृतम् ॥
भक्षणं कारयामास समयज्ञश्च तां प्रियाम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.53.m:
And rare betel well prepared with camphor and other spices
He, knowing the right moment, had his beloved chew. // 35

4.53.s:
sudurlabhaṃ ca viśveṣu vākpateḥ parinirmitam ..
anuttamamamūlyaṃ ca varuṇena rahaḥsthale .. 36 ..
4.53.d:
सुदुर्लभं च विश्वेषु वाक्पतेः परिनिर्मितम् ॥
अनुत्तमममूल्यं च वरुणेन रहःस्थले ॥ 36 ॥
4.53.m:
Rare in the worlds, fashioned by Bṛhaspati,
Incomparable and priceless, given in a secret place by Varuṇa, // 36

4.53.s:
atisūkṣmamanupamaṃ dattaṃ bhaktyā virājitam ..
vāsayāmāsa vasanaṃ kṛtvā nagnāṃ ca kautukāt .. 37 ..
4.53.d:
अतिसूक्ष्ममनुपमं दत्तं भक्त्या विराजितम् ॥
वासयामास वसनं कृत्वा नग्नां च कौतुकात् ॥ 37 ॥
4.53.m:
Extremely fine, peerless, radiant, presented with devotion—
Having undressed her in playful delight, he clothed her in that garment. // 37

4.53.s:
devarājena dattaṃ ca gajarājendramauktikam ..
nāsikābhūṣaṇaṃ cāru tasyai suprītaye dadau .. 38 ..
4.53.d:
देवराजेन दत्तं च गजराजेन्द्रमौक्तिकम् ॥
नासिकाभूषणं चारु तस्यै सुप्रीतये ददौ ॥ 38 ॥
4.53.m:
And a pearl from the lord of elephants, given by the king of the gods,
A beautiful nose-ornament, he gave to her for her great delight. // 38

4.53.s:
etasminnantare tatra suśīlādyāśca gopikāḥ ..
ṣaṣṭiḥ satsahacaryaśca rādhāyāḥ supratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 39 ..
4.53.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र सुशीलाद्याश्च गोपिकाः ॥
षष्टिः सत्सहचर्यश्च राधायाः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 39 ॥
4.53.m:
Meanwhile, the gopīs headed by Suśīlā,
Sixty exalted companions of Rādhā, renowned, // 39

4.53.s:
ṣaṣṭisatkoṭigopībhiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃhṛṣṭamānasāḥ ..
āyayuḥ pādacihnena priyasya vahataḥ priyām .. 4.53.40 ..
4.53.d:
षष्टिसत्कोटिगोपीभिः सार्धं संहृष्टमानसाः ॥
आययुः पादचिह्नेन प्रियस्य वहतः प्रियाम् ॥ 4.53.40 ॥
4.53.m:
Together with sixty crore gopīs, their minds joyful,
Arrived following the footprints of the beloved carrying his beloved. // 40

4.53.s:
kāściccaṃdanahastāśca kāściccāmaravāhikāḥ ..
kāścitkastūrihastāśca mālāhastāśca kāścana .. 41 ..
4.53.d:
काश्चिच्चंदनहस्ताश्च काश्चिच्चामरवाहिकाः ॥
काश्चित्कस्तूरिहस्ताश्च मालाहस्ताश्च काश्चन ॥ 41 ॥
4.53.m:
Some had sandalwood paste in hand, and some bore fly-whisks;
Some had musk in hand, and some held garlands; // 41

4.53.s:
kāścitsiṃdūrahastāśca kāścitkaṃkatikākarāḥ ..
kāścidalaktakakarā vastrahastāśca kāścana .. 42 ..
4.53.d:
काश्चित्सिंदूरहस्ताश्च काश्चित्कंकतिकाकराः ॥
काश्चिदलक्तककरा वस्त्रहस्ताश्च काश्चन ॥ 42 ॥
4.53.m:
Some held red vermilion in hand, and some had combs in their hands;
Some had red lac-dye in hand, and some held garments in hand; // 42

4.53.s:
kāściddarpaṇahastāśca puṣpapātradharā varāḥ ..
kāścitkrīḍāpadmahastā mālāhastāśca kāścana .. 43 ..
4.53.d:
काश्चिद्दर्पणहस्ताश्च पुष्पपात्रधरा वराः ॥
काश्चित्क्रीडापद्महस्ता मालाहस्ताश्च काश्चन ॥ 43 ॥
4.53.m:
Some held mirrors, and the excellent maidens held vessels of flowers;
Some held lotus-playthings in hand, and some held garlands; // 43

4.53.s:
kāścidāsavahastāśca kāścidbhūṣaṇavāhikāḥ ..
karatālakarāḥ kāścinmṛdaṃgavāhikāḥ parāḥ .. 44 ..
4.53.d:
काश्चिदासवहस्ताश्च काश्चिद्भूषणवाहिकाः ॥
करतालकराः काश्चिन्मृदंगवाहिकाः पराः ॥ 44 ॥
4.53.m:
Some had wine in hand, and some carried ornaments;
Some held cymbals in hand, others carried mṛdaṅga drums; // 44

4.53.s:
svarayaṃtrakarāḥ kāścidvīṇāhastāśca kāścana ..
ṣaṭtriṃśadrāgarāgiṇyo gopikārūpadhārikāḥ .. 45 ..
4.53.d:
स्वरयंत्रकराः काश्चिद्वीणाहस्ताश्च काश्चन ॥
षट्त्रिंशद्रागरागिण्यो गोपिकारूपधारिकाः ॥ 45 ॥
4.53.m:
Some held musical instruments in hand, and some held vīṇās;
The thirty-six rāgas and rāgiṇīs assumed the form of gopīs, // 45

4.53.s:
golokādāgatāyāśca bhārataṃ rādhayā saha ..
kāścijjaguśca nanṛtustatrāgatya ca kāścana .. 46 ..
4.53.d:
गोलोकादागतायाश्च भारतं राधया सह ॥
काश्चिज्जगुश्च ननृतुस्तत्रागत्य च काश्चन ॥ 46 ॥
4.53.m:
Who had come from Goloka to Bhārata together with Rādhā.
Having arrived there, some sang and some danced. // 46

4.53.s:
kāściccakruśca sevāṃ ca rādhāyāḥ śvetacāmaraiḥ ..
kāściccakruśca devyāśca pādasaṃvāhanaṃ mudā ..47..
4.53.d:
काश्चिच्चक्रुश्च सेवां च राधायाः श्वेतचामरैः ॥
काश्चिच्चक्रुश्च देव्याश्च पादसंवाहनं मुदा ॥47॥
4.53.m:
Some rendered service to Rādhā with white fly-whisks,
And some happily massaged the feet of the goddess. // 47

4.53.s:
kāciddadau ca tāmbūlaṃ bhakṣaṇārthe mahāmune ..
evaṃ kautukayuktaśca puṇye vṛndāvane vane .. .. 48 ..
4.53.d:
काचिद्ददौ च ताम्बूलं भक्षणार्थे महामुने ॥
एवं कौतुकयुक्तश्च पुण्ये वृन्दावने वने ॥ ॥ 48 ॥
4.53.m:
One offered betel for chewing, O great sage.
Thus engaged in playful sport in the sacred forest of Vṛndāvana, // 48

4.53.s:
pratasthau gopikāsārddhaṃ rādhāvakṣaḥsthalasthitaḥ ..
kṣaṇaṃ papau ca mādhvīkaṃ priyayā saha mādhavaḥ .. 49 ..
4.53.d:
प्रतस्थौ गोपिकासार्द्धं राधावक्षःस्थलस्थितः ॥
क्षणं पपौ च माध्वीकं प्रियया सह माधवः ॥ 49 ॥
4.53.m:
Resting against the bosom of Rādhā, he remained together with the gopīs.
For a moment Mādhava drank honey-wine with his beloved; // 49

4.53.s:
kṣaṇaṃ cakhāda tāmbūlaṃ kṣaṇaṃ nidrāṃ yayau mudā ..
kṣaṇaṃ cakāra śṛṅgāraṃ ratnanirmitamandire .. 4.53.50 ..
4.53.d:
क्षणं चखाद ताम्बूलं क्षणं निद्रां ययौ मुदा ॥
क्षणं चकार शृङ्गारं रत्ननिर्मितमन्दिरे ॥ 4.53.50 ॥
4.53.m:
For a moment he chewed betel; for a moment he went happily to sleep;
For a moment he made love in a jewelled pavilion; // 50

4.53.s:
kṣaṇaṃ jalavihāraṃ ca cakāra yamunājale ..
ityevaṃ kathitā vatsa rāsakrīḍā hareraho ..51..
4.53.d:
क्षणं जलविहारं च चकार यमुनाजले ॥
इत्येवं कथिता वत्स रासक्रीडा हरेरहो ॥51॥
4.53.m:
For a moment he enjoyed water-sports in the waters of the Yamunā.
Thus, O child, the rāsa-play of Hari has been told, wondrous indeed! // 51

4.53.s:
svecchāmayasyātmanaśca paripūrṇatamasya ca ..
nirguṇasya svatantrasya parasya prakṛteḥ prabhoḥ ..52..
4.53.d:
स्वेच्छामयस्यात्मनश्च परिपूर्णतमस्य च ॥
निर्गुणस्य स्वतन्त्रस्य परस्य प्रकृतेः प्रभोः ॥52॥
4.53.m:
Of the Self whose will is supreme, the most complete,
Free from the gunas, independent, beyond Prakṛti, the Lord, // 52

4.53.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāmīśvarasya parasya ca ..
kṛṣṇajanmarahasyaṃ ca bālakrīḍanamīpsitam..53..
4.53.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादीनामीश्वरस्य परस्य च ॥
कृष्णजन्मरहस्यं च बालक्रीडनमीप्सितम्॥53॥
4.53.m:
The supreme Sovereign of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others,
The secret of Kṛṣṇa's birth and his wished-for childhood play, // 53

4.53.s: uktaṃ kiśoracaritaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 54 ..
4.53.d: उक्तं किशोरचरितं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 54 ॥
4.53.m: And his youthful deeds have been related. What more do you wish to hear? // 54

4.54.s:
nārada uvāca ..
ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ rahasyaṃ babhūva munisattama ..
kathaṃ jagāma bhagavānmathurāṃ nandamandirāt .. 1 ..
4.54.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
अतः परं किं रहस्यं बभूव मुनिसत्तम ॥
कथं जगाम भगवान्मथुरां नन्दमन्दिरात् ॥ 1 ॥
4.54.m:
What secret took place after this, O best of sages?
How did the Blessed One go from Nanda's abode to Mathurā? // 1

4.54.s:
nando dadhāra prāṇāṃśca vicchedena hareḥ katham ..
gopāṅganā yaśodā vā kṛṣṇaikatānamānasāḥ ..2..
4.54.d:
नन्दो दधार प्राणांश्च विच्छेदेन हरेः कथम् ॥
गोपाङ्गना यशोदा वा कृष्णैकतानमानसाः ॥2॥
4.54.m:
How did Nanda preserve his life during separation from Hari,
Or the cowherd women, or Yaśodā, whose minds were solely intent on Kṛṣṇa? // 2

4.54.s:
cakṣurnimeṣavicchedādyā rādhā na hi jīvati ..
kathaṃ dadhāra sā devī prāṇānprāṇeśvaraṃ vinā .. 3 ..
4.54.d:
चक्षुर्निमेषविच्छेदाद्या राधा न हि जीवति ॥
कथं दधार सा देवी प्राणान्प्राणेश्वरं विना ॥ 3 ॥
4.54.m:
Rādhā, who could not live for the blinking of an eye during separation—
How did that goddess preserve her life without the lord of her life? // 3

4.54.s:
yeye tatsaṅgino gopāḥ śayanāsanabhogataḥ ..
kathaṃ visasmaruste ca tādṛśaṃ bāṃdhavaṃ vraje ..4 ..
4.54.d:
येये तत्सङ्गिनो गोपाः शयनासनभोगतः ॥
कथं विसस्मरुस्ते च तादृशं बांधवं व्रजे ॥4 ॥
4.54.m:
Whichever cowherds were his companions in sleeping, sitting, and dining,
How did they forget such a kinsman in Vraja? // 4

4.54.s:
śrīkṛṣṇo mathurāṃ gatvā kiṃ kiṃ karma cakāra saḥ ..
svargārohaṇaparyantaṃ tadbhavānvaktumarhati .. 5 ..
4.54.d:
श्रीकृष्णो मथुरां गत्वा किं किं कर्म चकार सः ॥
स्वर्गारोहणपर्यन्तं तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥ 5 ॥
4.54.m:
Having gone to Mathurā, what deeds did Śrī Kṛṣṇa perform?
You ought to tell that up to his ascension to heaven. // 5

4.54.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
kaṃsaścakāra yajñaṃ ca samāhūto dhanurmakham ..
jagāma tatra bhagavāṃstena rājñā nimantritaḥ .. 6 ..
4.54.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
कंसश्चकार यज्ञं च समाहूतो धनुर्मखम् ॥
जगाम तत्र भगवांस्तेन राज्ञा निमन्त्रितः ॥ 6 ॥
4.54.m:
Kaṃsa performed a sacrifice, summoned [to assemble] the Bow Sacrifice;
Invited by that king, the Blessed One went there. // 6

4.54.s:
rājā prasthāpayāmāsa cākrūraṃ bhagavatpriyam ..
akrūraḥ prerito rājñā gatvā ca nandamandiram.. 7 ..
4.54.d:
राजा प्रस्थापयामास चाक्रूरं भगवत्प्रियम् ॥
अक्रूरः प्रेरितो राज्ञा गत्वा च नन्दमन्दिरम्॥ 7 ॥
4.54.m:
The king sent Akrūra, who was dear to the Lord.
Dispatched by the king, Akrūra went to Nanda's dwelling.

4.54.s:
śrīkṛṣṇaṃ ca gṛhītvā sa sagaṇaṃ mathurāṃ gataḥ ..
kṛṣṇaḥ śrīmathurāṃ gatvā jaghāna nṛpatiṃ mune .. 8 ..
4.54.d:
श्रीकृष्णं च गृहीत्वा स सगणं मथुरां गतः ॥
कृष्णः श्रीमथुरां गत्वा जघान नृपतिं मुने ॥ 8 ॥
4.54.m:
Taking Śrī Kṛṣṇa and his companions, he departed for Mathurā.
Having arrived at glorious Mathurā, Kṛṣṇa slew the king, O sage.

4.54.s:
jaghāna rajakaṃ caiva cāṇūraṃ muṣṭikaṃ gajam ..
cakāra pitroruddhāraṃ bāndhavānāṃ ca bāndhavaḥ .. 9 ..
4.54.d:
जघान रजकं चैव चाणूरं मुष्टिकं गजम् ॥
चकार पित्रोरुद्धारं बान्धवानां च बान्धवः ॥ 9 ॥
4.54.m:
He also slew the washerman, Cāṇūra, Muṣṭika, and the elephant.
The kinsman delivered his parents and his relatives.

4.54.s:
kubjayā saha śṛṅgāraṃ kṛtvā ca kautukena ca ..
taṃ ca prasthāpayāmāsa golokaṃ gopikāpatiḥ .. 4.54.10 ..
4.54.d:
कुब्जया सह शृङ्गारं कृत्वा च कौतुकेन च ॥
तं च प्रस्थापयामास गोलोकं गोपिकापतिः ॥ 4.54.10 ॥
4.54.m:
And having made love sportively with Kubjā,
the Lord of the gopīs sent her to Goloka.

4.54.s:
cakāra kṛpayā viṣṇurmālākārasya mokṣaṇam ..
kṛpayā coddhavadvārā bodhayāmāsa gopikāḥ .. 11 ..
4.54.d:
चकार कृपया विष्णुर्मालाकारस्य मोक्षणम् ॥
कृपया चोद्धवद्वारा बोधयामास गोपिकाः ॥ 11 ॥
4.54.m:
Through his grace, Viṣṇu granted liberation to the garland-maker.
Out of compassion, he consoled the gopīs by means of Uddhava.

4.54.s:
tadopanīto bhagavānavantīnagaraṃ yayau ..
cakāra vidyāgrahaṇaṃ muneḥ sāṃdīpanerguroḥ .. 12 ..
4.54.d:
तदोपनीतो भगवानवन्तीनगरं ययौ ॥
चकार विद्याग्रहणं मुनेः सांदीपनेर्गुरोः ॥ 12 ॥
4.54.m:
Then, having undergone his sacred initiation, the Lord went to the city of Avantī.
He acquired knowledge from the sage Sāndīpani, his guru.

4.54.s:
tato jitvā jarāsandhaṃ nihatya yavaneśvaram ..
ugrasenaṃ ca nṛpatiṃ cakāra vidhipūrvakam .. 13 ..
4.54.d:
ततो जित्वा जरासन्धं निहत्य यवनेश्वरम् ॥
उग्रसेनं च नृपतिं चकार विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.54.m:
Then, having defeated Jarāsandha and killed the lord of the Yavanas,
he duly installed Ugrasena as king.

4.54.s:
gatvā samudranikaṭaṃ nirmāya dvārakāṃ purīm ..
jahāra rukmiṇīṃ devīṃ jitvā nṛpatisaṃghakam ..14 ..
4.54.d:
गत्वा समुद्रनिकटं निर्माय द्वारकां पुरीम् ॥
जहार रुक्मिणीं देवीं जित्वा नृपतिसंघकम् ॥14 ॥
4.54.m:
Going near the ocean, he built the city of Dvārakā.
Having conquered the assembly of kings, he carried off Queen Rukmiṇī.

4.54.s:
kāliṃdīṃ lakṣmaṇāṃ śaibyāṃ satyāṃ jāṃbavatīṃ satīm ..
mitraviṃdāṃ nāgnajitīṃ samudvāhaṃ cakāra saḥ .. 15 ..
4.54.d:
कालिंदीं लक्ष्मणां शैब्यां सत्यां जांबवतीं सतीम् ॥
मित्रविंदां नाग्नजितीं समुद्वाहं चकार सः ॥ 15 ॥
4.54.m:
He married Kālindī, Lakṣmaṇā, Śaibyā, Satyā, the virtuous Jāmbavatī,
Mitravindā, and Nāgnajitī.

4.54.s:
nihatya narakaṃ bhūpaṃ raṇena dāruṇena ca ..
patnīṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ vihāraṃ ca cakāra saḥ .. 16 ..
4.54.d:
निहत्य नरकं भूपं रणेन दारुणेन च ॥
पत्नीषोडशसाहस्रं विहारं च चकार सः ॥ 16 ॥
4.54.m:
Having killed King Naraka in a fierce battle,
he sported with his sixteen thousand wives.

4.54.s:
jahāra pārijātaṃ ca jitvā śakraṃ ca līlayā ..
ciccheda bāṇahastāṃśca jitvā ca candraśekharam .. 17 ..
4.54.d:
जहार पारिजातं च जित्वा शक्रं च लीलया ॥
चिच्छेद बाणहस्तांश्च जित्वा च चन्द्रशेखरम् ॥ 17 ॥
4.54.m:
Effortlessly defeating Śakra, he carried off the Pārijāta tree.
Having defeated Candraśekhara, he severed the arms of Bāṇa.

4.54.s:
pautrasya mokṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā punarāgatya dvārakām ..
ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa lokāṃśca pratimandiram ..18 ..
4.54.d:
पौत्रस्य मोक्षणं कृत्वा पुनरागत्य द्वारकाम् ॥
आत्मानं दर्शयामास लोकांश्च प्रतिमन्दिरम् ॥18 ॥
4.54.m:
Having secured the liberation of his grandson and returned again to Dvārakā,
he displayed himself and the worlds in every house.

4.54.s:
yoge ca vasudevasya tīrthayātrāprasaṃgataḥ ..
prāṇādhiṣṭhātṛdevīṃ ca dadarśa tatra rādhikām .. 19 ..
4.54.d:
योगे च वसुदेवस्य तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगतः ॥
प्राणाधिष्ठातृदेवीं च ददर्श तत्र राधिकाम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.54.m:
On the occasion of Vasudeva's sacrifice during a pilgrimage to a holy site,
he saw Rādhikā there, the presiding deity of his life-breath.

4.54.s:
pūrṇe ca śatavarṣe ca sudāmnaḥ śāpamokṣaṇe ..
punaryayau tayā sārddhaṃ puṇyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ vanam .. 4.54.20 ..
4.54.d:
पूर्णे च शतवर्षे च सुदाम्नः शापमोक्षणे ॥
पुनर्ययौ तया सार्द्धं पुण्यं वृन्दावनं वनम् ॥ 4.54.20 ॥
4.54.m:
When a hundred full years had passed and the curse of Sudāman had ended,
he returned with her once more to the sacred forest of Vṛndāvana.

4.54.s:
punaścaturdaśābdaṃ ca tayā sārdhaṃ jagatpatiḥ ..
cakāra rāsaṃ rāse ca puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate .. 21 ..
4.54.d:
पुनश्चतुर्दशाब्दं च तया सार्धं जगत्पतिः ॥
चकार रासं रासे च पुण्यक्षेत्रे च भारते ॥ 21 ॥
4.54.m:
For another fourteen years, the Lord of the universe, together with her,
performed the rāsa dance in the rāsa circle in the holy land of Bhārata.

4.54.s:
pūrṇamekādaśābdaṃ ca nivṛtya nandamaṃdire ..
mathurāyāṃ dvārakāyāṃ pūrṇamabdaśataṃ vibhuḥ .. 22 ..
4.54.d:
पूर्णमेकादशाब्दं च निवृत्य नन्दमंदिरे ॥
मथुरायां द्वारकायां पूर्णमब्दशतं विभुः ॥ 22 ॥
4.54.m:
Having resided in Nanda's home for eleven full years,
and in Mathurā and Dvārakā for a full hundred years, the all-pervading Lord

4.54.s:
cakāra bhāraharaṇaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthuvikramaḥ..
paṃcaviṃśativarṣe ca śatavarṣādhikaṃ mune .. 23 ..
4.54.d:
चकार भारहरणं पृथिव्यां पृथुविक्रमः॥
पंचविंशतिवर्षे च शतवर्षाधिकं मुने ॥ 23 ॥
4.54.m:
of immense prowess relieved the burden of the earth.
Having remained on earth for a hundred and twenty-five years,

4.54.s:
tiṣṭhañjagāma golokaṃ pṛthivyāṃ ca purātanaḥ ..
yaśodāyai ca nandāya vṛṣabhānāya dhīmate .. 24 ..
4.54.d:
तिष्ठञ्जगाम गोलोकं पृथिव्यां च पुरातनः ॥
यशोदायै च नन्दाय वृषभानाय धीमते ॥ 24 ॥
4.54.m:
the Ancient One departed for Goloka, O sage.
To Yaśodā, Nanda, the wise Vṛṣabhānu,

4.54.s:
rādhāmātre kalāvatyai dadau sāmīpyamokṣaṇam ..
kṛṣṇena sārddhaṃ gopī ca rādhikā ca kutūhalāt .. 25 ..
4.54.d:
राधामात्रे कलावत्यै ददौ सामीप्यमोक्षणम् ॥
कृष्णेन सार्द्धं गोपी च राधिका च कुतूहलात् ॥ 25 ॥
4.54.m:
and Rādhā's mother Kalāvatī, he granted the liberation of proximity.
Together with Kṛṣṇa, the gopī Rādhikā joyfully [departed],

4.54.s:
nibadhya dharmasetuṃ ca vedoktaṃ ca yuge yuge ..
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ samāsena mahāmune ..26..
4.54.d:
निबध्य धर्मसेतुं च वेदोक्तं च युगे युगे ॥
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं समासेन महामुने ॥26॥
4.54.m:
having established the bridge of dharma taught in the Vedas in age after age.
Thus all has been related in brief, O great sage.

4.54.s:
śrīkṛṣṇacaritaṃ ramyaṃ caturvargaphalapradam ..
brahmādistambaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ naśvarameva ca ..27..
4.54.d:
श्रीकृष्णचरितं रम्यं चतुर्वर्गफलप्रदम् ॥
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्तं सर्वं नश्वरमेव च ॥27॥
4.54.m: The charming life of Śrī Kṛṣṇa bestows the fruit of the four aims of life.

4.54.s:
bhaja taṃ paramānandaṃ sānandaṃ nandanandanam ..
svecchāmayaṃ paraṃ brahma paramātmānamīśvaram..28..
4.54.d:
भज तं परमानन्दं सानन्दं नन्दनन्दनम् ॥
स्वेच्छामयं परं ब्रह्म परमात्मानमीश्वरम्॥28॥
4.54.m:
Worship that supreme bliss, the joyful son of Nanda,
who acts of his own will, the supreme Brahman, the Paramātman, the Lord,

4.54.s:
paramavyayamavyaktaṃ bhaktānugrahavigraham ..
satya nityaṃ svataṃtraṃ ca sarveśaṃ prakṛteḥ param .. 29 ..
4.54.d:
परमव्ययमव्यक्तं भक्तानुग्रहविग्रहम् ॥
सत्य नित्यं स्वतंत्रं च सर्वेशं प्रकृतेः परम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.54.m:
the supreme, imperishable, unmanifest one, whose form is assumed out of grace toward his devotees,
true, eternal, independent, the Lord of all, beyond Prakṛti,

4.54.s: nirguṇaṃ ca nirīhaṃ ca nirākāraṃ nirañjanam .. 4.54.30 ..
4.54.d: निर्गुणं च निरीहं च निराकारं निरञ्जनम् ॥ 4.54.30 ॥
4.54.m: free from gunas, devoid of desire, formless, and stainless.

4.54.s:
iti śrībrahmaivavarte mahāpurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍe nārāyaṇanāradasaṃvāde śrīkṛṣṇarādhikāsaṃvādo nāma catuṣpañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 54 .. ..
śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇamastu ..
.. pūrvārddhaṃ samāptam .. ..
.. śubhaṃ bhavatu ..
idaṃ pustakaṃ mumbayyāṃ śrīkṛṣṇadāsātmajena kṣemarājena svakīye śrīveṅkaṭeśvara ( sṭīm ) mudraṇayantrālaye'ṅkayitvā prakāśitam .
saṃvat 1988, śakābdāḥ 1853
4.54.d:
इति श्रीब्रह्मैववर्ते महापुराणे श्रीकृष्णजन्मखण्डे नारायणनारदसंवादे श्रीकृष्णराधिकासंवादो नाम चतुष्पञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ॥ 54 ॥ ॥
श्रीकृष्णार्पणमस्तु ॥
॥ पूर्वार्द्धं समाप्तम् ॥ ॥
॥ शुभं भवतु ॥
इदं पुस्तकं मुम्बय्यां श्रीकृष्णदासात्मजेन क्षेमराजेन स्वकीये श्रीवेङ्कटेश्वर ( स्टीम् ) मुद्रणयन्त्रालयेऽङ्कयित्वा प्रकाशितम् ।
संवत् 1988, शकाब्दाः 1853
4.54.m:
Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā', in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa of the Mahāpurāṇa Brahmavaivarta, in the dialogue between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada.
The first half is complete.
May there be auspiciousness.
